Part of the metal roofing of the White Point Community Center was peeled back.
Numerous tree limbs were down throughout Trenton. The power was also knocked out for nearly 4 hours.
A home in Trenton was struck by lightning and some appliances in the home were damaged.

Estimated winds of 65 mph blew down trees, fences, power poles, and power lines in Van Alstyne. Some trees fell on power lines. One large tree in particular snapped about half way up and partially fell onto the building of the Van Alstyne Leader.

Numerous trees were uprooted, twisted, and snapped along FM 1047 from Star to the Game Warden Academy. A trailer house next to the Academy was rolled onto it's side and several barns lost their roofs in the same area.
Lightning from a non-severe thunderstorm struck a tree in the Tamarack subdivision of Gun Barrel City. A tree limb crashed through the roof of a nearby home. No one was injured.

Numerous trees were down across the county. An estimated 100 trees were down in the western half of the county. Dozens of downed trees were estimated in the eastern portions of the county. A large tree fell over the road at an intersection of FM 804 to the southeast of Athens. Approximately 5,000 electric customers were without power in the western half of the county.
Measured winds of 67 mph were reported in Thorp Springs with debris blowing around.

Hail up to the size of Golfballs did considerable damage in Granbury. Up to 200 windows were broken at the Bromley Apartments and the roof was damaged. Cars were also damaged at the apartment complex with the windows broken on a few cars. Approximately 150 automobiles were damaged at Mike Brown Ford, but no windows were broken on the complex. Another 130 vehicles were damaged at Jerry Durant Toyota. A skylight was broken at Oak Woods Intermediate School.
Peak winds of 68 mph were measured in Cresson.

In Sulphur Springs, trees and large limbs were down in the 1500 block of East Industrial Drive and along State Highway 154 south of the city. A large tree on South Davis Street was also snapped near the base and fell against a house. Power outages were reported on the south side of town.
Trees and large limbs were reported down on State Highway 19 near CR 1116.
Trees and large limbs were reported down on FM 69 in the Black Oak area south of Como.
Trees and large limbs were reported down near the intersection of CR 4546 and 4544.
Tree limbs ranging from 1-6 were knocked down at Beaumont Ranch southeast of Grandview.

A century old pecan tree that was several feet in diameter fell over, crushing part of the garage at a home on CR 2043 near Kemp. In addition, fallen trees and tree limbs along CR 2043 resulted in power outages to the surrounding area.
Large trees, several feet in diameter, were uprooted at Kings Creek Golf Club.

An estimated seven inches of rain in about 10 hours resulted in flooding in Forney. Street flooding closed down neighborhood streets and the water was up to the foundation of some homes in areas where the terrain was slightly lower. In parts of Downtown Forney, the water was up to the bumper of cars. The Curves on East Main Street was flooded and Mustang Creek rose out of its banks on one side. High water also closed down the intersections of Bowie Street and Pinson Road and Heritage Hill Drive at FM 470.

Hail up to the size of Tennis Balls was reported by a CoCoRaHS observer located 6.2 miles east of Lampasas. The hail lasted for 15 minutes. The hail shredded leaves off trees and tore a few small branches off trees.

A horse trailer on a property west of Lometa was overturned and tossed through a fence. Several large trees were uprooted at Lometa Regional Park and additional large trees, including cedar trees, were uprooted in and around Lometa. The sign at the Church of Hills was blown out of its concrete base.
Baseball size hail fell in Priddy.
A Caradan man was struck by lightning that hit a nearby television pole, traveled through the ground and up his body. He was hospitalized for approximately 24 hours but not seriously injured.
Widespread property and tree damage was reported across the county. Several power outages also occurred.
At least one tree was uprooted and another tree splintered in the Bluffview Estates on Richland Chambers Lake.

Major damage to hundreds of trees was sustained in Springtown. One 80 feet tall, 10 feet wide, 100 year old pecan tree fell through the roof of a doublewide on Walnut Creek Drive. Numerous trees had to be cleared from roads around the city. Portable buildings, sheds, and fences were also damaged across town. Shingles were torn off numerous homes. City Hall lost a flag pole, gutters on the building, a light on top of the building, and shingles. A light tower at the SISD Event Complex that was designed to sustain high winds was broken.
Numerous large trees were uprooted or destroyed in Bonnie Bell Estates south of Springtown.
Numerous large trees were uprooted or destroyed in Reno. Clean up efforts took 3 days to complete.
Heavy rainfall caused flooding along Walnut Creek Drive; likely the result of the nearby creek overflowing its banks.
The drainage ditch at Shawnee Park was flooded and the water flowed onto Elm Street. Several roads in the city were left impassable due to heavy rain from an MCS.
A large oak tree was split in half at Oak Street Baptist Church. Part of the tree fell on the street.
Several trees were knocked down across the county.
Numerous large trees are reported down along HWY 199 from near Joplin to near Springtown. Several houses had roof damage due to tree limbs falling on them.
Numerous large trees are reported down along HWY 199 from near Joplin to near Springtown. Several houses had roof damage due to tree limbs falling on them.
Numerous large trees are reported down along HWY 199 from near Joplin to near Springtown. Several houses had roof damage due to tree limbs falling on them.
Peak winds of 60-65 mph were estimated at the Heritage Creek Airstrip located 9 miles southeast of Decatur. Small tree limbs were down.
A lightning strike started a fire at a large two-story home in McLendon-Chisolm. The second story caved into the garage and the house was destroyed.
Part of the roof of City Garage at Princeton Street and Valley Parkway was torn off and landed on a nearby home. The Lewisville Visitor's Center also sustained roof damage and had to be closed.
Numerous fences were down in the Harriet Creek Subdivision located near FM 156 and HWY 114. Winds were estimated to be 70 mph.
Estimated winds of 75 mph were reported in Frisco on the Denton County side. Large tree limbs were also reported down.
Peak winds of 70 mph were estimated 1 mile east-northeast of New Hope.
Most of the ceiling of a drive-through bank at Hebron Parkway and Old Denton Road in Carrollton was lost.
Peak winds of 75 mph were reported in McKinney and large tree limbs were down. Power lines were also reported down around the city and many downed power lines blocked roads.
A grain silo was overturned near Pizza Hut Park in Frisco.
A large tree fell onto Jim's Cleaners on East Broad Street in Mansfield causing approximately $1,000 in damage to the roof.

Significant damage occurred at Eagle Mountain Lake Marina. Most of the damage was to the docks, dock roofs, and walkways. Only one boat was lost and a few had scratches and dings. Eight teenagers were trapped during the storm and had to be lead out to safety.

A home near Boat Club Road and Caballo Street was struck by lightning and sustained moderate damage. The lightning bolt entered through the roof and emerged through the laundry room. No possessions in the home were lost.
A recently built home on Centerboard Lane near Eagle Mountain Lake was completely destroyed in a fire started by lightning. All new appliances, furniture, and entertainment systems were lost.

Training echoes for several hours dropped several inches of rain that caused Big Fossil Creek to flow out of its banks on the east side of Saginaw. Some lanes of FM 156/Blue Mound Road at East Bailey-Boswell Road were flooded and barricaded. In some locations, the water was about a foot deep.

Training echoes for several hours dropped several inches of rain that caused Little Fossil Creek to flow out of its banks on the east side of Saginaw. East McLeroy Street was closed through Thursday morning due to water over the road.
Flooding along Big Bear Creek in Keller flooded the park and kept Bear Creek Parkway closed for part of the morning until the waters finally receded during the afternoon hours.
Lightning started a small house fire on Foxcroft Lane in Keller.

Training echoes for several hours dropped several inches of rain that caused Big Bear Creek to flow out of its banks near Bear Creek Park in Keller. The park was flooded and Bear Creek Parkway had to be closed between Cindy Court and Anita Avenue due to water over the road.
A creek flowing under Hurstview Drive in south Hurst overflowed its banks and flooded nearby homes. The water was reported to be a foot deep in some homes. The bridge over the creek was closed.
Lightning started a fire at the Chatham Creek Apartments on Thomason Circle in Arlington. This was a two-alarm fire. Eight people were displaced from their home.
The Saddle Creek Apartment complex in Euless was damaged and about 2 dozen tenants were displaced.
The Bear Creek Apartment complex in Euless was damaged.

Fort Worth Fire Deparment responded to a total of 7 structure fires during this MCS event: a commercial building on the 1100 block of North Sylvania Avenue, a residence in the 10300 block of Vintage Drive, a residence in the 1800 block of Marlene Drive, a residence in the 3800 block of Buckhorn Place, a residence in the 4500 block of East Loop 820, a residence at Wilbarger Street and Martin Luther King Freeway, and a residence at Shadydell Drive and Boat Club Road.
The roof was lost off a home on FM 2862.
Peak winds of 60 mph were estimated 3 miles east of Addison. Large trees limbs were down.

Two lightning strikes hit the Dallas pumping station causing the failure of one of the pumps that is responsible for parts of west Dallas. This failure exacerbated flooding in neighborhoods around Hampton Road and Canada Drive. Some evacuations were performed.

Two lightning strikes hit the Dallas pumping station causing the failure of one of the pumps that is responsible for parts of west Dallas. This failure exacerbated flooding that was already ongoing in Dallas. Some evacuations were performed in neighborhoods around Hampton Road and Canada Drive.
A lightning stike started a house fire in Mesquite. Minimal damage was sustained to the house.

Widespread street and creek flooding was reported around Irving. The river walk at Centennial Park in Irving was flooded, and several other parks were flooded and closed. A few motorists had to be rescued from their cars and in at least one case the water was 3-4 feet deep. Some major highways had to be closed down.
Numerous trees were uprooted or knocked down in Coppell. Tree limbs were also knocked down. Many of the trees that were knocked over were bradford pears. Power outages also occurred.

Significant flash flooding occurred in Highland Park from training echoes over Dallas County. Turtle Creek overflowed its banks and flooded roadways near its shores. A highwater rescue was required where Fitzhugh/Wycliff crosses the creek. The water was chest deep at the time of the rescue. Another water rescue was needed on Westside Drive and at the intersection of Armstrong Avenue and Lakeside Drive. Also, about 6 homes were flooded with water and the basement of the HPDPS was flooded.

Significant flash flooding occurred in University Park from training echoes over Dallas County. Twenty emergency calls of vehicles stalled in water were reported to the police department and fire department. Barricades were needed in 18 locations to close down streets inundated with high water.
The trailer of an 18-wheeler was blown over onto its side at Rig Trucking at Interstate 20 and FM 1189.

The Lifeline Community Church on Haymarket Road in Balch Springs was damaged by high winds. Much of the roof, which was under repair at the time, was ripped off and the inside of the church was damaged. Services could not be held at the church because of the damage and it was estimated that repairs would take 3-6 months.
A lightning strike is believed to have started a fire that burned the saltwater disposal tanks on Highway 16 South.
Cars were stranded in high water at Elam Road and St. Augustine Road in southeast Dallas.
All lanes of Collins Street at Interstate 30 had be closed due to downed power lines across the road.
A man had to be rescued from his flooded car on Riverside Parkway in Grand Prairie. The water was up to the headlights of the sedan.
Severe Drought conditions were observed across Young County during the first half of June according to the U.S. Drought Monitor. Conditions improved by mid month due to rainfall over the county.
Severe Drought conditions were observed across Stephens County during the first half of June according to the U.S. Drought Monitor. Conditions improved by mid month due to rainfall over the county.

Drought conditions continued to worsen across Milam County during the month of June according to the U.S. Drought Monitor. Extreme Drought was observed across the county for most of the month, but Exceptional Drought was declared across the southern third of the county by the end of the month. Rain amounts during the month continued to be below normal across the county.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, drought conditions worsened across Robertson County into Severe and then Extreme category during the month of June. Rainfall totals continued to be below normal with most of the county receiving less than an inch of rain in June.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, drought conditions worsened across Leon County into Severe category during the month of June. By the end of the month, Extreme Drought was observed across the western half of the county. Rainfall totals continued to be below normal with most of the county receiving less than an inch of rain in June.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, drought conditions quickly worsened across far southern Bell County into Extreme Drought category during the month of June. Rainfall totals continued to be below normal with less than an inch of rain in June.
Pea to Nickel size hail was reported on CR 576 in southwestern Stephens County.

An EF0 tornado in Hebron was video taped by a storm chaser. This tornado occurred in a field south of SH 121 behind the Best Buy. The tornado occurred along the leading edge of the MCS, but video evidence suggests it was not a gustnado.

According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Severe to Extreme Drought continued across the county with the worst conditions occurring across the southern half of the county.
According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Severe to Extreme Drought continued across the county with the worst conditions occurring across the southern third of the county.
According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Severe to Extreme Drought was observed across the southern half of the county.

According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Severe to Extreme Drought continued across the county with the worst conditions occurring across the western half of the county. By the end of the month, conditions had improved across the county due to several days of rain.
According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Extreme to Exceptional Drought continued across the county. Several days of rainfall during the month provided little relief.

According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Severe to Extreme Drought was observed across the county with the worst conditions occurring across the southern portions of the county. By the end of the month, conditions had improved slightly across the county due to several days of rain.

Several signs along the frontage road of Interstate 30 were knocked down. Several power outages also occurred in southern Greenville and in areas south and west of Greenville due to downed power lines. Some power poles and fences were also knocked down in these areas.
Several businesses on the east side of Greenville and just east of Greenville had their signs bent over or blown out by high winds. Some of the signs were large and associated with strip malls.

A few large trees were split in the city of Fairfield by high winds. One tree on Cotton Street was partially leaning against a house. In addition, the underpinnings of a manufactured home on Old Palestine Road were damaged.
Heavy rainfall resulted in high water on County Road 506. The road was left impassable until 9 am.
Residual flooding from heavy rain early in the morning left County Road 506 impassable until 9 am.
Lightning started a house fire on Claybrook in Wylie. Damage occurred to the attic and second story of the home.
Lightning started a house fire on Santiago Trail in the Seis Lagos area near Lucas.
A large tree was uprooted and fell onto a garage and a newly purchased truck.  The truck and the corner of the garage were crushed.
A tree was uprooted and a porch was damaged in Millsap.
An unsold house on Jewel Lane near Stillhouse Hollow Lake was destroyed by a fire started by lightning.
A lightning strike near the Copperas Cove Solid Waste Department on South FM 116 damaged the phone line and a computer in the building.
The metal roof of a barn on Luthern Church Road was blown off. A second barn in the same area was also damaged.
Three cars were trapped in high water at teh intersection of Douglas Avenue and Lemmon Avenue. The water was reported to be 9 inches deep.

Damaging winds, likely from a downburst, hit the town of Muenster. A 1,000 pound creep feeder was moved approximately half mile. Other heavy items in the city were moved about a half of a mile, and a camper was moved over 30 feet. Sheds were destroyed, trailers were moved, tree leaves were shredded off limbs, and a cattle trailer was shoved up against a fence. Residents also reported their homes shaking during the damaging wind event and missing roof shingles.
A trained spotter estimated a wind gust of 69 mph. The spotter also reported a broken window, shingles off a roof, and damage to large trees.
Nickel size hail was reported 7 miles south of Weatherford.
An amateur radio operator estimated a 60 mph wind gust near the Denison Dam.
A storm spotter measured a 71 mph wind gust northwest of Sherman on Plainview Rd.
A tower at Grayson Community College was blown down onto the Grounds Maintenance Building and the Criminal Justice Building lost most of its roof due to high winds.
A storm spotter measured a 71 mph wind gust at the intersection of Farm-to-Market Road 1417 and Lamberth Rd.
A storm spotter reported a wind gust of 60 mph 2 miles east-southeast of Callisburg.
The emergency manager reported a wind gust of 58 mph and powerlines down in the city of Gainesville.

An amatuer radio operator estimated a 70 mph wind gust and vehicles being blown off the roadways.
An amateur radio operator reported several power poles were leaning and multiple power flashes in the city of Sherman.
