A large boat was pushed ashore at Belton Lake, walls at a restauraunt under construction were blown down, and minor tree damage was reported.
Small limbs were knocked off trees in Greenville.
Numerous streets were flooded in the city of Paris. One person was rescued when a wrecker removed a stranded vehicle from high waters.
A tree fell on a house but did not cause major damage to the structure.
There were numerous reports of wind damage in the community of Payne Springs. Numerous trees and powerlines were down. There was roof damage to 10 homes due to fallen trees.

Lightning struck two structures and started fires at both places in far eastern Parker County. The first structure was a home on Deer Crossing Way and the second was a church on Reese Lane. The home was destroyed and the church suffered minor damage to the roof.
Lightning struck the Fort Worth Weather Forecast Office and destroyed two computers and damaged Amatuer Radio equipment.
Quarter size hail was reported north of the city of Barry.
Four power poles were snapped in the city of Barry.
Three modular buildings approximately 60'x20' were blown over on North Burleson Blvd.
A roof near Trinity Blvd and I-820 was damaged when a tree fell onto it. Also, a 5 diameter tree limb was thrown 50 feet.
Power poles and large trees were blown down on FM 744 west of Corsicana.
Multiple trees were blown down across county roads and a structure was pushed into County Road 321 near Leon Junction.
A mobile home was severely damaged, a grain bin was moved 100 yards, and a large tree and limbs were blown down by strong winds.
A large evergreen tree was uprooted and a trampoline was lifted across a field. The winds were estimated between 60 and 70 mph.
A brick and wooden fence was blown down in Hewitt. The wind gust was estimated to be between 60 and 70 mph.

A 14 inch diameter tree was knocked down at the city manager's residence in Hillsboro, and another large tree fell onto a truck causing minor damage. In addition, roofs were blown off several barns in western parts of Hillsboro. Power lines and 4 to 5 inch diameter tree limbs were knocked down throughout the city.
A large tree and power lines were blown down near the Silver Shores community.
A large tree was blown over onto County Road 1206 between the towns of Slocum and Denson Springs.
Nickel size hail was reported in the community of Pioneer.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in Alvarado.
Numerous fences were blown down and trees uprooted. The winds were estimated at 70 mph.

Lightning struck a pregnant female at 7:30 pm CDT as she crossed a residential street after exiting her car. The unborn child died soon after the strike and the mother died in the hospital three days later on August 30th at 4:44 PM CDT.
Numerous streets were flooded in the city of Sulphur Springs. The water was knee to waist deep and several water rescues were performed for trapped motorists.
Trees fell onto many homes in Denison, a parked truck and boat, and onto two carports.
A man was injured on the 1600 block of West Bond when a large tree fell through his home. He suffered minor cuts and bruises.
An air traffic controller at Grayson County Airport stated the airport had measured a wind gust of 75 mph.
Minor roof damage was reported at the Longhorn Grill on Parkway Ave. A 30 foot section of the metal roof was peeled off and water damage was reported to the inside of the building.
A homeowner suffered damage to his roof when a large limb fell, puncturing a hole into the roof. Several outbuildings were also destroyed on the property.
Widespread tree damage was reported in Enchanted Oaks. Numerous trees fell on homes, carports, and powerlines. Damage was reported to several structures.
Lightning destroyed a house on the 5000 block of Pinehurst.
A barn, several outbuildings, and a garage door suffered damage due to high winds.
Large limbs were knocked down and two large barns suffered damage to a roof and sides in the community of Big Hill.
A seventh month old female died in a parked car outside of an elementary school in Corsicana. The child was left in the car for approximately 5 hours. The temperature at the time was 89 degrees.
A large tree was uprooted and knocked down powerlines in Walnut Springs.
Trees were reported down across southeastern Hopkins County.
The County Commissioner reported about a half dozen trees knocked down onto roadways.

According to the U.S Drought Monitor, at the beginning of the month Extreme to Exceptional Drought continued across the county with the worst conditions occurring across the southern half of the county. By the end of the month, almost the entire county was experiencing Execptional Drought Conditions.

According to the U.S Drought Monitor, at the beginning of the month Severe to Extreme Drought continued across the county with the worst conditions occurring across the southern half of the county. By the end of the moth, conditions worsened and most of the entire county was experiencing Exceptional Drought.
According to the U.S Drought Monitor, the entire county experienced extreme drought for the month.
According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Severe to Extreme Drought continued across the county with the worst conditions occurring across the southern half of the county.
According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Severe to Extreme Drought was observed across the southern half of the county.
According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Severe to Extreme Drought was observed across the county with the southern half experiencing the worst conditions.
Trees were reported down near Saint Jo.
Flooding was reported at the intersection of FM 919 and FM 2692. In addition, persistent street flooding was reported in Gordon.
A 60 mph wind gust was reported 6 miles north of Granbury near the Hood/Parker County line.
A trained spotter measured a 69 mph wind gust at Loop 820 and Spur 580 on the west side of Fort Worth.

A NWS Storm Survey determined that a downburst damaged a one square mile area in northwestern Johnson County located approximately 8 miles west of Burleson and 1.25 miles south of the Johnson/Tarrant county line. At least 10 homes were left uninhabitable and several trees were knocked down. The winds were estimated to be 90-100 mph.
An 18-wheeler was blown over in a Walmart parking lot located one mile north-northwest of Cleburne.
Sixty mph winds were estimated in Burleson.
A 60 mph wind gust was reported in Egan.
A trained spotter measured a 67 mph wind gust 3 miles south-southeast of Mansfield.
A trained spotter reported a 64 mph wind gust in Keene.
Highway 67 in Keene had water over the road.
Water was over the road between Joshua and Cleburne.
County Road 256, 2 miles southwest of Stephenville, was impassable.
County Road 185, 4 miles southeast of Stephenville, was impassable.
Trees and 4 tree limbs were reported down in Itasca. Power lines were also down.
The exit ramp from Interstate 35 onto Illinois Avenue was closed due to high water. Seven cars went around the barricades and were stranded in the high water.
Several inches of water were flowing over Mountain Creek Parkway because ditches along the road were overflowing.
The Sheriff's Office reported that numerous county roads across the county were closed due to high water.

Widespread flooding was reported in Rockdale. Numerous streets were closed and Highway 79 west of Rockdale was closed due to high water. High water was also reported in parts of Milano and Cameron. FM 1915 at Big Elm Creek and FM 486 at the Little River had to be closed. Other county roads that were closed at some point during this time were CRs 119, 120, 147, 203, 230, 335, 402, 405, 408, 412, and 414.
Residual flooding of County Roads and numerous roads in the city of Rockdale continued until the late evening hours. Many roads remains closed throughout the day.
Numerous roads in eastern Navarro County were closed due to high water. TxDOT had to close several of the roads.
Residual flooding of numerous roads in eastern Navarro County continued into the overnight hours. Several of these roads remained closed.
Roads were closed around Axtell due to water over the roads.
Roads were closed in the Spring Lake area due to water over the roads.
Lightning struck a home on the 900 block of Condor Drive in Coppell. The brick chimney was damaged but no other information was available.
Many tree limbs were down, the bank's awning was torn and the scoreboard at Zebra Stadium was damaged.
Lightning struck a fiberglass tank at a saltwater disposal site starting a blaze. Five tanks were lost in the blaze, and the site had to be monitored by local firefighters until the next morning.
An 18-wheeler was blown over on Interstate 35 by high winds. There were no injuries.
Part of the metal roof of a manufactured home on CR 411 south of Goldthwaite was peeled back. The beams were also lifted off with the sheet of metal.
Tree limbs and flag poles were down in Laguna Vista.
A tree partially fell onto a home on McNeill Street in Stephenville. Significant damage did not occur.

Heavy rain during the day, in combination with rainfall from earlier in the week, was thought to be the reason for the collapse of a ceiling at an apartment complex on the 2900 block of Robin Road. One man was taken to the hospital with a slight laceration on his forehead.
Quarter to Golfball size hail fell for over 10 minutes in the town of Strawn.
Golfball size hail fell just north of the town of Gordon.
Hail up to 2 inches in diameter fell in the town of Saint Jo.
Golfball size hail fell in Gordon.
Penny size hail was reported in the community of Willow Park, 9 miles east of Weatherford.
Quarter size hail was reported 2 miles north of Granbury.
Quarter size hail was reported 9 miles southwest of Benbrook.
Penny size hail fell 4 miles southwest of Stephenville.
Nickel size hail fell 1 mile northwest of Stephenville.
Nickel size hail fell 2 miles northwest of Stephenville.
Golfball size hail was reported in the community of Graford.
A COOP Observer reported Pea to Golfball size hail 1 mile southwest of Gordon.

Significant flash flooding occurred in southern Bell County when 9-15 of rain fell in less than 10 hours. The town of Salado was hit the hardest during the early afternoon hours. Salado Creek that runs through town overflowed its banks and forced the evacuations of approximately 12 families. The rapid rise in the creek also heavily damaged the Main Street Bridge, ripping the asphalt from the bridge and forcing its closure through October 14th. In other areas of Salado, the water was reported to be nearly 10 feet over some bridges and some homes were flooded with up to two feet of water. In addition, Interstate 35 near the Bell/Willimason county line had to be closed for a few hours and other parts of the interstate were down to one lane due to water on the road. The access roads of Interstate 35 between Salado and the Bell/Williamson county line were also closed due to water over the roads. Many of these road closures began during the early afternoon hours. In the town of Bartlett, 5 of water was reported to be flooding streets, and 5 of water was also reported over FM 487, east of Bartlett. Additional roads in the southern portions of the county were flooded and closed as well.

Ongoing flooding continued in southern Bell County and additional rainfall during this period kept much of the area flooded. The town of Salado remained flooded and several roads in the southern portions of the county remain closed due to high water.

Significant flash flooding occurred across mainly the southern half of Dallas County from continuous rainfall that lasted nearly 12 hours. The Dallas EOC reported several streets southeast of downtown Dallas had to be closed. Also, the area north of Interstate 30 and south of the Trinity River in west Dallas was significantly flooded when the water pump system failed due to the heavy rainfall. Several intersections along Carrier Parkway and other major roads in Grand Prairie were flooded. Numerous other roadways in southwest Dallas County were flooded. High water rescues were performed in the southern portions of Dallas County, Interstate 45 at Simpson Stuart was closed, and the exit ramp from Interstate 35 to Illinois Avenue was closed.

Significant flooding continued across the southern and southwestern portions of Dallas County. Several roads remained closed. Also, the area north of Interstate 30 and south of the Trinity River in west Dallas remained flooded.

Significant flooding was observed across the far southern and far western portions of Tarrant County. Road closures were widespread in Arlington, Crowley, and Mansfield. Cars were stuck in water and high water rescues were required.

Several flooded areas were reported across the county but the city of Burleson was impacted the most. Numerous roads were closed in Burleson and cars were stranded in water in the city. A few residents had to be evacuated on Bowden Circle between 4-5 am CST. In Joshua, five water rescues in automobiles were needed on CRs 913, 914, 1021, and 705 and Indian Hills.  Several streets in the city of Joshua were also closed for several hours. The fire department in Joshua reported the floodwaters began to recede in Joshua around 645 am CST. Other road closures were reported across the county.

Significant flooding was reported across Ellis County from heavy rainfall that fell in just a few hours. It was reported that over 10 of rain fell in parts of the northern portions of the county. Water was reported over the road at Interstate 35E, mile marker 395. Water was over the road on Highway 77 near Italy and high water rescues were reported in the Ferris area. A local newspaper listed several roads that were closed around the county, including part of the I-35E service road, the service roads along I-45 (in the Palmer area), and numerous County Roads and Farm-to-Market roads around the county. Another local newspaper also reported that the water was 3 feet deep in Bristol on FM 660.

Residual flooding continued across Ellis County into the next day. Additional periods of rainfall caused additional problems across the county. In particular, the service roads along Interstate 45 in Palmer remained under water, the southbound exit of Interstate 45 at mile maker 258 was under water, parts of FM 660 in Bristol remained under 3' of water, and several roads across the county remained closed.

Localized flash flooding was reported in Temple. The intersection of First Street and south Loop 363 had to be closed and so did the eastbound access road of Loop 363 in front of Kings' Daughters Hospital.

According to the US Drought Monitor, Exceptional Drought was observed across the county in the beginning of the month. However, heavy rainfall in the middle of September eased drought conditions and the county was classified as moderate by the end of the month.

According to the US Drought Monitor, Exceptional Drought was observed across the county in the beginning of the month. However, heavy rainfall in the middle of September eased drought conditions, and the county was classified as Abnormally Dry (D0) by the end of the month.

According to the US Drought Monitor, Extreme Drought was observed across the county in the beginning of the month. However, heavy rainfall in the middle of September eased drought conditions, and the county was classified as Abnormally Dry (D0) by the end of the month.

According to the US Drought Monitor, Extreme Drought was observed across the county in the beginning of the month. However, heavy rainfall in the middle of September eased drought conditions, and the county was classified as Severe (D2) by the end of the month.

According to the US Drought Monitor, Extreme Drought was observed across the county in the beginning of the month. However, heavy rainfall in the middle of September eased drought conditions, and the county was classified as Severe (D2) by the end of the month.

According to the US Drought Monitor, Severe to Extreme Drought was observed across the southern half of the county in the beginning of the month. However, heavy rainfall in the middle of September eased drought conditions, and the county was classified as Abnormally Dry (D0) before the end of the month.
A home in Murphy was completely destroyed on the interior by a fire that was started from a lightning strike.
Lightning started a fire at a home in Murphy that caused minor damage to the home.

Lightning struck the building that houses KJCR 88.3 Radio Station, starting a fire that heavily damaged the building. All the radio equipment was destroyed including mixing boards and the wiring relay system that sends the signal to the transmitter.
A radio listener located southeast of Dublin reported a few large tree limbs were knocked down by high winds.
Estimated winds of 65 mph were reported in Sanger.
High winds knocked down several trees in Burleson.  In the Briar Oaks subdivision, tree limbs up to 6 in diameter and wood fences were reported down.
Tree limbs that were 2-3 in diameter were knocked down just north of Spinks Airport (KFWS).
A 60 mph wind gust was estimated 12 miles east of Lampasas.
Trees were down near HWY 31 between Brownsboro and Chandler.
A couple of large trees were reported down near the intersection of County Line Road, FM 933, and Rogers Hill Road.
Tree limbs that were 1-2 in diameter were down on the south side of Marquez.
A transformer was down in Jacksboro.
Water entered three homes and the City Hall in Trenton.
The automated weather station at Stephens County Airport in Breckenridge (KBKD) measured a 58 mph wind gust.
Large tress were uprooted, a large grill was moved, and a wind turbin was ripped off a home 2 miles west of Lorena.
Park Central Drive at I-635 in north Dallas was closed due to high water.
Campbell/Blackburn Road in Garland was closed between North Garland Ave and East Brand Road due to high water.
Highway 114 near the Texas Motor Speedway was closed for several hours due to high water over the road.
An off-duty NWS employee estimated 65 mph winds near the Tarrant/Parker county line.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured in Trenton.
The Azle Police Department closed the intersection of HWY 199 and Boyd Rd/FM 730 due to high water. High water rescues were also taking place at this intersection.
Flood waters from a swollen creek were entering a home on South Alabama Drive in Celina. Also in Celina, flooding was reported at Ash Street and South Ohio Drive.
A high water rescue was reported near Lake Pat Cleburne.
A high water rescue was ongoing on HWY 82, 2 miles west of Honey Grove.
A few roads south and west of McKinney were closed due to high water.
Water was reported over a few roadways near Aubrey and at the intersection of HWY 377 and FM 3524/Sherman Drive north of Aubrey.
Residual flooding of roads near Aubrey continued due to heavy rainfall earlier in the evening.
Multiple roads in Greenville were flooded. On Stonewall Street, the water was reported to be 2-3 feet deep.
Flooding of roadways in Hunt County continued. Several roads in Greenville remained flooded and sections of HWY 380, FM 3211, FM 1565, and FM 36 had to be barricaded.
A portion of FM 79 near Lake Cook was closed due to high water.
Water was over the road on parts of FM 46 south, FM 50, and HWY 6 south of Hearne. TxDOT was installing barricades.

Several secondary roads were flooded across Navarro County from persistent rainfall over the county. It was also reported that creeks, streams, and ditches were overflowing their banks causing some flooding.
High water was reported on County Roads 1806, 2120 at 2102, and 1129 at 1110. The flooding was the result of persistent rainfall over the county for several hours.
High water was reported on County Road 752 near Lake Limestone.
High water was reported on County Road 456 west of the Navasota River. Other flooding was also reported along the Navasota River and some roads were covered in water.

A few secondary roads in the county were flooded due to persistent rainfall over several hours. Buffalo Creek in the northern portion of the county overflowed its banks and flooded some county roads near the creek for a few days.
Several secondary roads north of Palestine were flooded due to persistent rainfall over several hours.

Eight inches of water was reported over HWY 175, 1 mile north of Kaufman. Near Terrell, the water was a foot deep at HWY 34 and FM 2578. In Terrell, significant street flooding occurred with 3-4 feet of water reported on Catherine Street and Alamo Street, and High Street and Delthine. High water rescues were reported on Catherine Street. In the mid afternoon hours, it was reported that at least a dozen county roads had to be closed; including 4007, 4008, 4009, and 4011. The baseball field in Mabank and Optimist Park in Seven Points was under water.

Numerous city streets in Sulphur Springs were inundated and a few were barricaded. Highway 19 just north of Sulphur Springs was under water, and FM 1870 southeast of Sulphur Springs had high water over the road. FM 69 north of Interstate 30 had to be closed down because the water was a foot deep over a 100 feet section of the road. CR 4766 south of FM 71 was impassable but possibly because it lies near a swollen section of the South Sulphur River.
Vehicles were unable to pass on FM 269 at CR 3310 due to high water.
Ongoing flooding of roads, creeks, and ditches continued across the county. Some roads remained closed through the late afternoon hours.

Widespread flooding was reported around the county; especially north and west of Hillsboro where 10 county roads had to be closed. Near Whitney, CRs 1240, 1248, and 1258 were closed due to high water. FM 309 west of Woodbury was closed after Cottonwood Creek overflowed its banks. Whitney Creek also overflowed its banks, resulting in the evacuation of 30 residents in an apartment complex nearby. Another home along the creek had water in the house up to the top of the baseboards.
Ongoing flooding continued across the county and in Terrell due to heavy rainfall earlier in the day. Several roads remained closed.
High water was reported in Grand Saline and high water rescues were ongoing.

Ongoing flooding continued across the county from earlier heavy rainfall. The flooding damaged several roads and washed out culverts and headwalls of bridges. Several of the roads were going to need to be torn up and redone according to local officials.
High water was reported in Van and high water rescues were ongoing.

In north Fort Worth, NE 28th Street at Decatur Avenue and Northside Drive at Cold Springs Road had to be closed due to cars stuck in both intersections. Water rescues were required on NE 28th Street.  The Fort Worth Police Department responded to approximately 33 high water rescue calls during the rain event. The city of Fort Worth also experienced sewer overflows when rainfall entered the city's sewer pipe lines and flooded the system.
Multiple roads in Watagua were closed due to high water.
Hail the size of a thumb fell north of Topsey. The amount of hail was large enough to nearly cover the ground.

Significant damage occurred to a double wide home on CR 118 north of Topsey. Strong winds destroyed three sheds, one of which was a car shed. The winds also tore shingles off the roof and the side of the home. Some eaves of the home were also damaged, and a 2x4 was driven though a wall. Three holes were created in the home and rainwater entered the home through the holes causing significant water damage. Also on the property, cattle fences were damaged.
Damage to two sheds occurred at the Topsey Exotic Ranch. The roof was blown off one shed and the tin bent up on another shed. A flagpole was also bent.
Several large tree limbs and at least one large tree was blown down in Normangee.

The following roads in Hunt County were closed due to flash flooding: FM 2655 at the Middle Sulphur River, FM 272 two miles west of Celeste, FM 3211 between the 618 and 620 mile markers, FM 118 at the Sulphur River, and FM 1565 between SH 276 and the Hunt/Kaufman County Line.
Several roads remained under water and closed through the afternoon hours from earlier heavy rainfall.
TxDOT had to close down HWY 271 just west of Pattonville for several hours due to water over the road.
Heather Drive, Whitehead Drive, and Park Street in Granbury had to be closed due to high water.

Five bridges in Salado were closed for a few hours due to high water that covered each bridge with up to 3 feet of water. The South Ridge and Chisholm Trail bridges in Mill Creek, the Smith Bluff bridge east of Mill Creek, and two access road bridges along Interstate 35 were all closed down.

Two flooded bridges along the access road of Interstate 35 in Salado were reopened during the afternoon hours, but the South Ridge bridge and Chisholm Trail bridges in Mill Creek remained closed until the following morning when the water finally drained. The closure of these two bridges cut off residents' access through the subdivision.
FM 1565 near the intersection of SH 276 was under water and other county roads were also impassable during the heavy rain period.
Some roads in Gun Barrel City were closed; including Blacklash Road, Harbor Point, Flag Lake Road, and Pritchard @ Jess Hinton Road.
Quarter size hail fell 9 miles east-northeast of Goldthwaite.
Penny size hail fell along Interstate 35 south of Gainesville.
Quarter size hail fell in the town of Priddy.
Quarter size hail fell near the town of Sanger.
Nickel size hail fell 3 miles north of Denton.
Penny size hail fell in the town of Crowley.
Golfball size hail was reported in Tioga.
Golfball size hail fell in the town of Bryson.
Teacup size hail was reported in Nocona.
Quarter size hail fell 4 miles southwest of Azle.
Quarter size hail fell along Interstate 35 just south of the Cooke/Denton county line.
Quarter size hail was reported 5 miles west of Weatherford.
Nickel size hail fell in Johnson Creek Park 3 miles east of Valley View.
Quarter size hail fell at the intersection of Interstate 20 and Highway 51 south of Weatherford.
Nickel size hail fell in the town of Gordonville.
Nickel size hail was reported along Interstate 20 north of Benbrook.
Quarter size hail fell at the intersection of Highway 36 and FM 589 northwest of Comanche.

Numerous roads around the county were closed due to high water. It was reported that over 60 roads in the county had to be closed at some point during the day, and the majority of the closed roads were across the eastern half of the county. The water in some places was 2 feet deep over the road. The right lanes of northbound Interstate 35 south of Waxahachie were closed due to pavement damage from the heavy rainfall.

Several roads around the county remained closed. Damage was sustained on several roads where the gravel was washed away or other erosion occurred. The water didn't drain off some roads that lie near creeks until later in the week.
Watercrest Road at Cody Poe Road and Little Nolan Road at Cunningham Road in Killeen had to be closed due to high water.
TXDot closed FM 1565 between SH 276 and the Kaufman County line and FM 36 between FM 1564 and SH 276.

A car got stuck in a low water crossing at Wildflower Country Club in Temple, and the driver had to be rescued. The water was up to the bumper of the sedan. Also in Temple, several manholes in the Bird Creek area were overflowing from the excessive amount of rain.

FM 1915 north of Buckholts from HWY 190 to FM 485 was closed because Bear Creek overflowed its banks and water was covering the roadway. Also, FM 487 at Donahue Creek and FM 486 at Little River south of Pettibone were closed due to water over the road.
FM 1713 near Whitney was closed due to high water.
Several roads were closed in the Styx area and in Arnold Hills in Seven Points. Also, CRs 2100 and 2138 south were closed.  Some of these roads were washed out.

CR 4011 and 1390 were closed off due to high water. Also, a small lake near Warsaw overflowed its banks flooding the surrounding roads, neighborhoods and pastures. This resulted in the closing of FM 148.
Residual flooding continued across Kaufman County through the following day. Areas around a lake near Warsaw remained flooded and CRs 4011 and 1390 also remained closed.
Several roads in the county were closed due to high water.

Residual flooding continued across the county. The waters washed away the gravel on some roads and these roads had to remain closed for several days until they could be fixed. This included CR 3150 off the lime plant road, CR 3310 between Valley Mills and Clifton, and CR 3512 near Cayote.
Numerous roads around the county were closed due to high water. Also, high water rescues were needed in Whitesboro on HWY 377.
Four feet of water was reported on Icehouse Road near Sabathaney in northeastern Parker County.

At first, a few rural roads in the county were closed due to high water; however as the rain continued, heavy flooding of creeks and farmland occurred causing problems on additional roads in the county.

Creeks in Decordova were 3-5 feet out of their banks and flooding surrounding areas. At least 4 county roads were closed due to high water and several more low water crossing locations were barricaded. Just after midnight, a man had to be rescued from his truck after getting stuck at a low water crossing on Stroud Creek Avenue near Thorp Spring. The water was 2 feet deep in the low water crossing. The truck was swept into the raging Stroud Creek just moments after the man was rescued. The man was injured during the rescue.
Several streets in Lampasas were closed due to high water.

Numerous low water crossings, FM roads, and county roads were impassable and barricaded. Flooding conditions were especially bad in Coryell City. Other reports included FM 1829 at Mound was closed and Hwy 236 at Mother Neff State Park was closed.

Flooding continued across the county with several roads impassable. Near Burleson, flooding of creeks and farmland continued. High water rescues were also reported in Lillian; including one at the intersection of CR 528 and CR 526.

Numerous county roads and low water crossings were flooded. Several barricades were used to close roads. Several gravel roads in the eastern parts of the county were washed away. It was also reported that parts of SHs 56 and 22 had to be closed down. A recently rebuilt bridge on CR 3125 over Neils Creek was flooded out. The bridge had just been replaced last year.
Significant flooding problems continued across the county with several roads and low water crossings impassable. A few parks in the city of Gatesville were closed due to flooding.

Flooding continued along many creeks, rivers, and streams in the county; especially across the northern half of the county. In particular, heavy flooding was noted along the Mound Prairie Creek from near Elmtown to SH 155, and roads were impassable near the Trinity River in the eastern portions of the county.
Mound Prairie Creek at SH 155 was out of its banks and flooding nearby pastures.
Persistent rainfall resulted in the flooding of fields across the county. Some lesser traveled roads had water flowing over them, but no roads were closed.

A couple had to be rescued after driving into high water at the Spirit of the West Resort. Water from the lake at the resort was overflowing its banks due to heavy rainfall of 6-8 inches and flooding the surrounding roadways. The water was reported to be up to the headlights of the car. No one was injured, and the water began receding shortly after the rescue and was cleared by the next morning.

A car was swept off the road at a low water crossing on Salesville Road that was covered with about 2.5 feet of water. The woman driver was rescued from the middle of the raging creek by a local resident.  The road was barricaded after the incident. Local residents reported they had only seen the creek as high one other time.
Some roads in Harker Heights were barricaded due to high water.
TxDOT was forced to close portions of a few roadways for a few days due to high water: FM 1915 and Big Elm Creek and at the Little River, FM 437 at Donahue Creek, and FM 486 at the Little River.
Persistent rainfall pushed Bois d'Arc Creek out of banks by at least half a mile on each side. This flooded nearby pastures on each side of the creek.
A Lipan school bus got stuck in 3 feet of water at a low water crossing. The exact location of the incident is unknown.  No one was injured.
A man had to be rescued from his car off NE 1030 near Rice after it got stuck in a low water crossing. The water was reported to be knee deep or approximately 1.5 feet deep.
A man had to be rescued from a low water crossing on Riverside Trail that was still covered in water several hours after the rainfall had ended. The water was up to the bumper of his stranded truck.
Overflowing creeks and ponds flooded nearby farmland in parts of the county.

Locations and roadways near creeks and large bodies of water were flooded.  Locations along the Bosque River in the northwestern portions of the county experienced flooding problems due to the swollen river. The Eichelberger Crossing bridge over the Bosque River had to be closed. Some parks around Lake Waco were also closed due to overflow from the lake.
Mother Neff State Park was closed for four days to flooding. Its access roads (SH 236 and CR 338) were also flooded.
Mother Neff State Park was closed for several days due to flooding of the park and its access roads.

According to the US Drought Monitor, Severe Drought was observed across the county in the beginning of the month. However, beneficial rainfall early in the month quickly relieved the drought status and the county was categorized as D0 (Abnormally Dry) by the end of the month.

According to the US Drought Monitor, Severe Drought was observed across the county in the beginning of the month. However, beneficial rainfall early in the month quickly relieved the drought status and the county was completely removed of any drought status by the end of the month.
CRs 142, 185, 247, 260, and 303 were closed due to high water.

Several roads were closed in the Nevada, Josephine, and Blue Ridge areas due to flooding.  These roads were: CR 590@PR 5337; CR 638@FM 1777; Milton Street in Josephine; CRs 484, 504, 637, 668, 825, and 1216, and SH 1216. Barricades were installed at all of these locations. In addition, the bridge support of SH 5 at the East Fork of the Trinity River in McKinney was being washed out and the bridge had to closed for a few months. The flooding was the result of several hours of rainfall on ground that was already well saturated.

A car hydroplanned on SH 78 just south of SH 205 causing the head-on collision of two cars. The collision resulted in the death of three adults and injured three others; including a toddler. The injuries to all three were nonlife-threatening and mostly consisted of broken bones.

An average of 8-9 of snow fell across Montague County as reported by local law enforcement and COOP observers. Strong winds created near blizzard conditions across the county during the afternoon hours. The peak wind reported at the automated weather station in Bowie (K0F2) was 40 mph. Traffic on HWY 287 was snarled by the weather and several motorists were stranded on the highway through the night. Some icy roads were reported during the day, but at night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. Numerous accidents were reported during the event. Three days later, a motorcycle rider was killed when he wrecked on a patch of ice that remained under the Texas 59 overpass on HWY 287 in Bowie.

Snowfall totals of 4-9 were reported across the western half of the county by the emergency manager and COOP observers. The highest snowfall totals were observed in the far western and northwestern portions of the county. The eastern half of the county received 2-3 of snow. Strong winds resulted in blowing snow for a few hours during the afternoon. The peak wind reported at the automated weather station in Gainesville (KGLE) was 40 mph. The strong winds created snow drifts of 3-6 feet which blocked roads resulting in roads closures across mainly the western half of the county during the afternoon hours. Bridges also began to ice during the late afternoon hours, but at night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.
An average of 2-3 of snow fell across the county but at night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.

An average of 7-8 of snow fell across the county as reported by local law enforcement and COOP observers. Strong winds created near blizzard conditions across the county during the afternoon hours. The peak wind reported at the automated weather station in Graham (KRPH) was 39 mph. Snow drifts as high as 4 feet were reported in some locations. Several roads during the day became impassable because of the snow and icy roadways, but at night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.

An average of 4-6 of snow fell across the county. Strong winds created near blizzard conditions across the county during the afternoon hours. The peak wind reported at the automated weather station in Breckenridge (KBKD) was 46 mph. Some roads during the day became impassable because of the snow, but at night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.

An average of 3-6 of snow fell across the county. Strong winds created near blizzard conditions across the county during the afternoon hours. Interstate 20 by Ranger Hill and from Cisco to Abilene was closed due to icing. Both of these areas remained closed until the next day. Several accidents occurred and several motorists spent the night stranded in their vehicles. Local law enforcement spent the night either evacuating people from their cars or bringing them food and blankets.  Other roads during the day became impassable because of the snow, but at night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.

An average of 6-9 of snow fell across the county as reported by local law enforcement, COOP observers, CoCoRaHS observers, and TxDOT. Strong winds created near blizzard conditions across the county during the afternoon hours. Snow drifts up to 2 feet were reported by a local COOP observer. Some roads during the day began to ice and became impassable because of the snow, but at night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. Numerous traffic accidents were reported throughout the event.

Snowfall totals of 4-5 were reported around the county including a local COOP observer in Alvord. The remainder of the county received an average of 1-3 of snow. Strong winds resulted in blowing snow for a few hours during the afternoon. The peak winds reported at the automated weather station in Bridgeport (KXBP) and Decatur (KLUD) were 38 mph and 34 mph, respectively. At night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.

Up to 3 of snow fell across the county and some blowing snow was reported in the afternoon hours. The automated weather station at Denton (KDTO) reported a peak wind of 39 mph. The biggest impact came at night when the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. The Denton police reported 86 weather related accidents and a few injuries, but several other accidents were reported around the county.

Local COOP Observers reported 4-5 of snow across the western half of the county. Only 3 of snow was reported at Mineral Wells and other eastern parts of the county. The local newspaper reported that up to 9 of snow may have fallen in the far northwestern corner of the county near Possum Kingdom Lake. Strong winds created near blizzard conditions across mainly the western half of the county during the afternoon hours. The peak wind reported at the automated weather station in Mineral Wells (K0F2) was 45 mph. At night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. No roads were closed in the county during this event, but a fatal accident occurred during the afternoon hours on HWY 281 killing one female.

Most locations in the county saw 1-3 of snow. DFW Airport reported 3 of snow and one location in Haslet reported close to 4 of snow. Some blowing snow was reported in the afternoon hours; particularly in the northwestern corner of the county. Automated weather stations across the county reported peak winds of 43-47 mph. Some icy roads were reported during the day and hundreds of accidents were reported during the day; but the biggest impact came at night when the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. Several more accidents were reported and numerous people slid off the icy roads.  Some people spent the night in their cars.

Up to 2 of snow fell across the county but at night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. The Sheriff's Office responded to 36 traffic accidents. Only one sustained a minor injury.

Up to 2 of snow fell across the county but at night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. Some of the accidents from the icy roads resulted in minor injuries.

Snowfall totals of 1-3 of snow were reported across the county. The biggest impact came at night when the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. By 645 pm, the High Five exchange was closed down. Several accidents were reported and numerous people slid off the icy roads. Some people spent the night in their cars.  The Dallas County Sheriff's Office responded to 321 weather related accidents on Thursday. About 150 flights were cancelled at DFW Airport and about a handful were cancelled at Love Field.

Up to 1 of snow fell across the county, but numerous accidents due to icy roads were reported in the evening hours and overnight as the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.

Up to 1 of snow was reported across the county. The biggest impact came at night when the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. Several accidents were reported and numerous people slid off the icy roads.  A fatal accident occurred in Frisco around 430 pm on HWY 380 between Preston Road and the Dallas North Tollway. Three cars were involved in a collision when one car lost control on an icy bridge. Three people were killed and three more were injured with non-life threatening injuries.

Snowfall totals of 3-6 were reported around the county by the local newspaper. Strong winds resulted in blowing snow at times during the afternoon. The peak winds reported at the automated weather station in Comanche (KMKN) was 39 mph. At night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.

The Sheriff's Department in Stephenville reported 2 of snow, but up to 6 of snow  was reported in the northern half of the county; including Dublin. Strong winds created blowing snow at times during the afternoon hours and snow drifts up to a foot in some places. The biggest impact came at night when the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. It was noted that several cars slid off HWY 281 north of Stephenville.

Up to 3 of snow fell across the county, but numerous accidents due to icy roads were reported in the evening hours and overnight as the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning. Conditions were especially bad on HWY 377 East and the road had be closed in two spots: east of Fall Creek Highway and west of Tolar.

In Killeen, less than an inch of snow stuck to grassy surfaces, but Veterans Memorial Boulevard, W.S Young, Twin Creek Dr and Water St were closed due to ice.  Bridges in the area were also slick to drive on.

Up to 1 of snow fell across the county, but the biggest impact came at night when the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.

Up to 2 of snow fell across the county, but the biggest impact came at night when the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.

Up to 2 of snow fell across the county, but the biggest impact came at night when the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.
The sign of the Luxury Inn on Hwy 190 in Copperas Cove was blown down in high winds. The winds at the time were gusting to 45 mph.
Up to 1 of snow fell across the county but at night, the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.
Nickel size hail was reported 4 miles SSE of Kaufman.

Snowfall totals across the western half of the county averaged 4 inches or more. Across the eastern half, the snowfall totals averaged 1-3. Some blowing snow was reported in the afternoon hours across mainly the western half of the county. The peak wind reported at the automated weather station in Mineral Wells (K0F2) was 45 mph. The biggest impact came at night when the snow froze on the roadways, creating icy roads and treacherous travel conditions across the county through Christmas morning.

Periods of heavy rainfall during the late afternoon and evening hours resulted in flash flooding in Hopkins County. The following roads were impassable at some point during the evening hours: CR 1197 near FM 2297 and CR 1174, FM 69 north of Interstate 30, FM 1870 near the bridges, FM 2560, CR 1444, CR 1152 near FM 1567, FM 71 west, CR 2316 near FM 69 south, and several of the main streets in Sulphur Springs. It was also reported that some vehicles got trapped in water on SH 11, CR 2316, and SH 154.
FM 71 near the Delta/Hopkins County line and FM 69 near the Mahoney slab remained impassable due to heavy rainfall from the night before.
Golfball size hail fell in the city of Forney.
Quarter size hail fell in the city of Quinlan.
Half-dollar size hail fell along Interstate 20 at exit 519 west of the city of Canton.
Penny to quarter size hail fell along Highway 64 west of Myrtle Springs.
Quarter size hail fell in the city of Grand Saline.
Quarter size hail fell in the town of Crossroads.
Quarter to golfball size hail fell in the town of Tigertown.
Quarter size hail fell on County Road 1116 five miles southwest of Sulphur Springs.
Quarter size hail was reported in the town of Deport.

A NWS survey team found evidence of a long track tornado in Van Zandt County. The tornado touched down near CR 859 north of Highway 64 on the northwest side of Canton and traveled approximately 15 miles in a northeast direction. Numerous structures were damaged along the track of the tornado which ended near the Silver Lake community in the extreme Northeast corner of the county. Along the damage path, a single family home lost its entire roof and part of its exterior walls. A number of large trees were uprooted and several sheds and outbuildings suffered extensive damage. A small church was destroyed in the community of Starr. A total of 150 homes suffered damage, but only one injury was reported.  Based on the damage, the tornado was rated an EF-2 with peak winds in the 110 to 120 mph range.

A NWS Storm Survey found evidence of a tornado touchdown approximately 4 miles southwest of Sulphur Springs and tracked approximately 5.5 miles to the northeast. One mobile home was destroyed resulting in two injuries. A pre-fabricated metal building on Highway 19 south of County Road 174 suffered considerable damage. The damage was consistent with the upper end of the EF-0 rating with wind speeds estimated near 80 mph.

A NWS storm survey found evidence of a tornado in a sub-division 2 miles east of Sulphur Springs. Around 50 homes suffered some degree of roof damage, two of which sustained more severe damage after being impaled by large tree branches. This damage was consistent with the rating of an EF-0 with wind speeds around 80 to 85 mph.
Two tractor trailers were overturned on Interstate 30 at mile marker 131.
Power poles and large trees were damaged at the intersection of Highway 19 and Highway 154 on the north side of Sulphur Springs.
A roof was caved in, a truck was overturned, and debris was noted on Irwin Rd between Drexel Drive and Hines Drive in Sulphur Springs.

A NWS Storm Survey concluded a tornado touched down about 3 miles south of the town of Larue and tracked northeast for about a mile. A total of seven homes were damaged, and the exterior walls collapsed on some structures. The Larue Church of Christ suffered extensive damage. This tornado was rated an EF-2 with estimated maximum winds around 130 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey concluded that an EF-1 tornado with maximum estimated wind speeds of 90 to 100 mph touched down near Poyner and tracked 3 miles to the northeast toward Coffee City. A mobile home was dislodged and a wood framed home had significant damage. Tree damage was also noted along a three mile path with an average width of 100 yards.
An awning was blown off a building in downtown Gorman. Large tree limbs and a stop sign were also blown down.
A wind gust of 60 mph was estimated in the town of Carbon. Dime size hail was also reported.
A wind gust was estimated to be 60 mph. Dime size hail was also reported.
Part of the roof of the physical plant at Tarelton State University came off.
Fairly widespread damage was reported in the city of Stephenville with many 4 to 6 tree limbs down, roofs damaged, and fences blown down.
A 60 mph wind gust was estimated by a trained spotter.
A trained spotter measured a 66 mph wind gust in the city of Stephenville.
A trained spotter measured a 62 mph wind gust at the intersection of Highway 174 and Highway 67.
Light icing from freezing drizzle created slick roads across the county. At least one accident was reported on HWY 281 in Jacksboro. Road conditions improved by the afternoon.
Freezing drizzle resulted in icy bridges on HWY 380. A major accident occurred on FM 101 south of Chico. No other information was available. Road conditions improved by the afternoon.
Freezing drizzle resulted in the icing of bridges in Burleson. Several accidents in Burleson were reported due to the slick roads. Road conditions improved by the afternoon.

Light icing from freezing drizzle created slick roads across the county. Numerous accidents were reported around the county. The Fort Worth PD reported 40 accidents, and the Arlington PD reported 34 accidents and numerous cars sliding off Interstate 20. Road conditions improved by the afternoon. Some school districts closed for the day or delayed opening.

Light icing from freezing drizzle created slick roads across the county. Numerous accidents were reported around the county and the DART trains were affected, too. The HOV lanes of Interstate 30 between Arlington and Mesquite were closed due to icing. The Dallas PD reported 83 accidents and 45 of these accidents resulted in injury. No further details on the injuries were provided. Road conditions improved by the afternoon. Some school districts closed for the day or delayed opening.
Light icing from freezing drizzle created slick roads across the county. Several accidents were reported on Interstate 35 and HWY 82. Road conditions improved by the afternoon.

A large tree fell on top of a residence and three tractors and three pickups parked outside also were damaged. Another residence suffered damage to its tin roof and lost siding off the side of the house.
One power pole was knocked down south of the town of Lone Oak.

Numerous county roads and city streets were closed due to high water. A culvert on Plum Creek, north of the town of Purmela, was washed out. Most low water crossings in the county were also closed due to the flooding.
Numerous streets were flooded in the city of Breckenridge after 3 to 4 inches of rain fell in 2 to 3 hours.
The roof of a barn was torn off and a large tree was uprooted. Several structures also suffered minor damage.
Roads were barricaded around Sulphur Creek due to a rapid rise in water.

Light icing from freezing drizzle created slick roads across the county. Numerous accidents were reported on major roadways throughout the county. Road conditions improved by the afternoon. Some school districts closed for the day or delayed opening.

Light icing from freezing drizzle created slick roads across the county. At least 20 vehicle and 18-wheeler accidents were reported around the county. On Spur 579 in northern Hillsboro, two cars ended on their tops after losing control on an icy spot. Four people were sent to the hospital. Several more cars slid off roadways around the county but were not damaged. Road conditions improved by the afternoon.
Numerous roads throughout the county remained closed due to flooding well after the heavy rain had ended.
Numerous roads in the northern and eastern parts of the county remained closed due to flooding well after the heavy rain had ended.
Several county roads throughout the county were covered with water. County Road 243 was closed east of the city of Kaufman.
Several roads throughout the county were covered with water or closed. This included Farm-to-Market roads 36, 118, 2655, and 3211.

A police officer for the city of Richardson suffered minor injuries when his patrol car spun out of control and flipped over after hitting any icy patch. The patrol car hit a road sign and a utility pole before flipping over. A few hours later, an 18-wheeler lost control on an icy patch on East R.L. Thornton Expressway near Jim Miller Road in Dallas, causing a 5 vehicle accident. No major injuries were reported.

During the day on January 9th, the pipes to the sprinkler system at an assisted living center in Temple burst, damaging the ceiling of at least 10 rooms and the adjacent hallways. The residents had to be evacuated. The temperature in Temple the morning of the 9th fell to 9 degrees. Also during this 3-day cold spell, a hotel in Temple sustained damage to the Sheetrock in one room from a broken water pipe, and a department store sustained some type of damage from broken water pipes.

Classrooms at Fellowship Academy in southwest Arlington were flooded when frozen water pipes burst sometime on the 9th or 10th. The school was closed on the 11th and 12th to clean up the damage. The city of Fort Worth responded to 121 water breaks during the period of the 8th-11th. Most of the water breaks were in the northwest and west areas of the city, inside Loop 820.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell across the county. A total of 3.5 inches was reported in Palestine.

Four to six inches of snow was reported in several parts in the northern half of the county. In the southern parts of the county, around 2-3 of snow was reported. The COOP observer in Meridian reported 5.25 of snow. Several vehicles slid off the roads.

An average of 8-12 of snow fell across the county. A COOP observer in Frisco reported a total of 12 of snow. A trained spotter in Plano reported 8.5 of snow. A few carports collapsed but no major damage was reported. Sixteen vehicle accidents were reported, but no serious injuries were reported.
Snowfall reports up to 3 were reported across the northern portions of the county. A total of 1.5 was reported in Comanche.

An average of 7-10 of snow was reported around the county. Several places reported snowfall totals of 10; including parts of Precinct 4, Lake Kiowa, northeast of Gainesville, and north of Muenster. Some minor traffic accidents and vehicles sliding off roadways were reported.

An average of 9-12 of snow fell across the county. An NWS employee measured 12.5 in Garland. Power outages and vehicles sliding off the road were numerous around the county.  About 50 major accidents were reported and nearly 200 minor accidents. No serious injuries were reported. Several carports collapsed in Coppell with cars under them and several more collapsed carports were reported around the county. Just west of Dallas on Interstate 30, the roof of a tire warehouse partially collapsed around 5:30 AM on the 12th. The roof of the sanctuary at Central Pointe Church of Christ in the Red Bird area also collapsed and the sanctuary was considered a total loss.
An estimated 7-9 of snow fell around the county.

An average of 9-10 of snow fell across the county, but as much as 12 of snow was reported near Denton. Nearly 100 minor vehicle accidents were reported around the county. Five injuries were reported in vehicle accidents. A seven car accident occurred on I-35E in Corinth but no serious injuries were reported. Near the University of North Texas campus, a large post oak tree branch fell on four vehicles, damaging them all.

An average of 2-4 of snow was reported across the county. The winter precipitation first fell as sleet and then changed to all snow. The highest snowfall totals were reported in the northeast corner of the county. Two major accidents were reported near Ranger Hill, but no other information was available.

Much of the county reported 8-11 of snow with the highest amounts generally across the northern portions of the county. The COOP observer in Waxahachie reported 13 of snow and 13 of snow was also estimated in Ferris. In Ferris, several business awnings collapsed under the weight of the snow. In Red Oak, the roof of the Wayne Boze Funeral Home collapsed and the entire building was thought to be a loss. In Midlothian, it was reported that at least one awning at a boat and RV storage facility collapsed, and also the wood roof of a 6000-square foot chicken house collapsed. Only 10 vehicle accidents were reported in Ennis; most reports around the county were for assistance for vehicles that had slid off the roads.

An average of 4-8 of snow fell across the county with the highest snowfall totals reported across the northeastern half of the county. The local TXDOT reported 8 of snow in the northern and northwestern portions of the county, 5-6 in Stephenville, and 4 in the southern portions of the county. A retired NWS employee reported 7 of snow between Stephenville and Bluff Dale. The COOP observers in Chalk Mountain and in Morgan Mill both reported 5 of snow. Several accidents were reported around the county from people sliding on the slick roads.

About 5-8 of snow was estimated around the county. The COOP observer in Monkstown reported a total of 7 of snow, and the COOP observer in Trenton reported a total of 8 of snow. Only a few minor vehicle accidents were reported.
It is estimated that 1-3 of snow fell across the county. Three inches of snow fell in Fairfield.

About 5-8 of snow was estimated around the county. A trained spotter in Denison reported a total of 7 of snow, and another spotter in Bells reported 7.5 of snow. Several crashes were reported along HWY 75 and two vehicles were overturned. Parts of HWY 289 became icy.
About 2 of snow fell across the county, but a local newspaper reported that some parts of Hico reported up to 4 of snow.

Six to ten inches of snow fell across the county. The COOP observer in Athens reported 6.5 of total snow, and a trained spotter near Payne Springs reported 7.5 of total snow. The local newspapers reported 5-8 in the Mabank and Gun Barrel City areas and 8 in Malakoff. TXDot officials reported 10 in Seven Points. About 7 minor wrecks were reported in and around Athens, but no serious injuries were reported. Other motorists slid off the road and required assistance.

During the early morning hours, a mix of rain and snow was reported but then the precipitation changed to all snow around 10:30 am. An average of 4-6 of snow fell across the county. Higher snowfall totals up to 7 were reported in the northern portions of the county. The COOP Observer in Hillsboro reported 4 of total snow, the COOP Observer in Brandon reported 4-6 of total snow, and the COOP Observer in Itasca reported 6 of total snow. The public reported 5 of total snow in Whitney, and the media relayed a report of 7 of total snow in Covington. A local newspaper reported about 4 of snow in Hubbard. The Sheriff's Office reported over 50 wrecks during the evening and overnight hours, but no major injuries.

Snowfall total reports ranged from 4-10 across the county, but most reports averaged 7-10 of total snow. A trained spotter in Decordova reported a total of 7.5 of snow and another spotter in Oak Trail Shores reported 9 of snow. A total of 29 vehicle accidents were reported by the Sheriff's Office with four ambulance transports required. However, no other information was available on the injured except that the injuries were minor. The most troublesome spots for travelers was HWY 377 West and the area between Tolar and Lipan.

Reports of 8-12 of snow were reported across the county. The heaviest snowfall totals were reported in the southwest corner of the county. A total of 8.5-9 of snow was reported in Sulphur Springs, and a total of 12 of snow was estimated in Brashear. According to the local newspaper, only a few minor vehicle accidents and a few power outages were reported. The roads that were impacted the most were SH 11 east from Como to the county line, westbound I-30 from Franklin County to Sulphur Springs, and SH 154 South.

Snowfall totals across the county ranged from 8-12.5.  A trained spotter near Quinlan reported 9 of total snow. Local newspapers reported around a foot of snow in Greenville and near Royse City and 9 of snow in East Tawakoni. Two major accidents were reported in Greenville with several other minor accidents reported across the county. Around 9 pm on the 11th, a car crashed into a traffic signal pole in Greenville injuring all three passengers. All three passengers were transported to the hospital; one with serious injuries. The other significant accident occurred around 1:15 am on the 12th when a car lost control and struck the Hunt County Criminal Justice Center causing minor damage to the building. There were no injuries with the second accident. Several of the remaining minor accidents were fender benders.

Eight to thirteen inches of snow fell across the county. The heaviest snowfall totals occurred across the southern portions of the county. The COOP Observer in Antelope reported 8 of snow and the COOP Observer in Jacksboro reported 13 of snow. TXDot also estimated 13 of snow in Bryson.

An average of 6-8 of snow fell across the county, but local newspapers also reported 10 of snow in Keene and 12 of snow in Joshua. The COOP Observer in Burleson reported 8 of snow, and the COOP Observer in Cleburne reported 6.2 of snow. Around 75 accidents were reported in the county, but about a hundred more reports were of people sliding off the roads. Some minor injuries were reported, but no additional information was available on the number of injuries. In Cleburne, a tree fell on a car and boat heavily damaging both, and a carport collapsed at an auto sales business. Several vehicles were damaged by the carport.

An estimated 6-9 of snow fell across the county. In Paris, 7-9 of snow was reported by several sources and over 8 of snow was reported in Deport by the local newspaper. Only a few accidents and no major damage was reported.

An average of 2-4 of snow fell across the county. In Buffalo, about 2 of snow was reported and about 2.5 of snow was reported in Normangee. The Sheriff's Office reported numerous road problems from the slushy roads, and a local newspaper also reported numerous power outages.

An average of 9-13 of snow fell across the county. In Terrell, 12 of snow was reported by an amateur radio operator, and the COOP Observer southeast of Kaufman reported 9 of total snow. The local newspaper in Forney reported 10-13 of snow. Also in Forney, a fatal two-vehicle accident was reported on FM 548, six miles north of US 80. One person died in the accident. In Kemp, the metal roof of a workshop collapsed, damaging the interior contents.

Up to 3 of snow fell across the county. The emergency manager reported 2 of snow north of Mexia. The COOP Observer in Thornton reported 1.5 of snow and local media reported 2 in Groesbeck. Several vehicles slid off into ditches but no major traffic accidents were reported.

Up to an inch of snow fell across parts of the county. The official report for Waco was 0.5 inches, but some locations in the city measured an inch. Slick roads resulted in around 25 vehicle accidents and several more vehicles slid off the road.

An average of 8-12 of snow fell across the county. The COOP Observer near Bonita reported 8.5 of total snow. The Nocona PD reported 8-9, and TXDot in Bowie reported 11-12 of total snow. About a foot of snow was reported in Saint Jo.

During the morning and early afternoon hours, a mix of rain, sleet, and snow was reported, but the precipitation changed to all snow by the mid afternoon hours. About 3-6 of snow fell across the southern half of the county while 6-9 fell across the northern half of the county. In Chatfield, 7.5 of total snow was reported, and 6 of total snow was reported in Corsicana. A local newspaper reported 5-9 in Kerens.  Many accidents occurred on Interstate 45 and several vehicles slid off the road.

An average of 7-12 of snow fell across the county. The highest totals were reported in the northeast half of the county. The COOP Observer in Strawn reported a total snow of 6.5, the COOP Observer in Brazos reported a total snow of 10.0, and the COOP Observer near Gordon reported a total snow of 10.5.  The TXDOT in Mineral Wells estimated 12 of total snow, but other estimates from the city were 8-10 of total snow. Due to slick conditions from snow accumulation on the roadways and slush, some roads in Mineral wells were barricaded; including NW 10th Street, Mesquite Street, Travis Drive, NE 23rd Street, FM 1821, and all the hills going into Western Hills except for Holly Hill Drive. Local law enforcement reported responding to some accidents but most calls were for assistance for vehicles that had slid off the roads. HWY 4 between Palo Pinto and Santo was closed for about 7 hours due to an overturned delivery truck. In Mineral Wells, a wooden carport collapsed, crushing an SUV under it and another carport collapsed at a business. Near Santo, the roof of a roping area collapsed under the weight of the snow, and at Possum Kingdom a covered storage facility collapsed at the Slalom Shop.

An average of 10-13 of snow fell across the county with slightly lesser amounts in the far southern portions of the county.  The COOP Observer in Weatherford reported a total snow of 11.0, and a citizen from Weatherford reported 12.4 of total snow. Local newspapers reported 11+ of snow in Aledo and about 12 in Springtown. Nine school buses in Springtown slid off roads and into ditches while transporting students home on the 11th. Several carports, sheds, and barns collapsed or the roof collapsed from the heavy snow.
Estimates of 8-10 of snow were reported but some locations may have received up to 12 of snow. Only two vehicle accidents were reported but numerous vehicles slid off the road.
Nine to twelve inches of snow fell across the county. A trained spotter in Royse City reported a total snow amount of 12 and icy bridges. The local newspaper reported 9 in Rockwall.
The COOP Observer in Bremond reported a total snow of 0.5, and the COOP Observer in Franklin reported a total snow of 1.5.

An estimated 4-7 of snow fell across the county. The COOP Observer in Rainbow reported a total snow of 4, and a citizen in Glen Rose estimated 7 of total snow. Only a few accidents were reported and some cars slid off HWY 67.

Snowfall totals ranged from 5-12 across the county  The COOP Observer in Edom reported a total snow of 5, and the COOP Observer in Wills Point reported a snow depth of 10.8 the morning of the 12th. TXDot in Canton estimated a snow total of 12.
An estimated 4-8 of snow fell across the county. TXDot measured 8 of snow across the northern portions of the county, and a total of 6 of snow was reported in Breckenridge.

An average of 10-12 of snow fell across the county. The COOP Observer in Alvord reported a snow depth of 7 the morning of the 12th, and the COOP Observer in Decatur reported a total snow of 11.  A NWS meteorologist measured 12 of snow southeast of Decatur. The local newspaper reported 8 of snow in Alvord, 11.5 in Cottondale, 12 in Runaway Bay, and 12.5 in Decatur. Numerous minor vehicle accidents were reported across the county. Several thousand customers lost power and extensive tree damage was reported.
An estimated 4-7 of snow fell across the county. The Graham Fire Department reported 6.5 inches of snow while the local newspaper reported over 7 of snow in Graham.

Most of the county received 10-14 of snow; however, lesser totals around 7-8 were reported in the far southwestern portions of the county. A COOP Observer in Haslet measured a snowfall total of 14.4 which was the highest reported total from the event. Another COOP Observer in Keller reported a total snow of 9.5, and the COOP Observer in North Richland Hills reported a total snow of 11.5. At the NWS office in north Fort Worth, a total of 12.6 of snow fell, and DFW International Airport officially reported 12.5 of total snow which set several new climate records.  Damaged and broken trees and tree limbs caused problems across the county.  Nearly 100 accidents were reported by area law enforcements and even more vehicles slid off of roadways and required assistance. No injuries were reported. Several reports of fallen carports and awnings were reported across the county. Around 5:45 am on the 12th, the roof of Rahr & Sons Brewing Co., a microbrewery south of downtown Fort Worth, collapsed, damaging the building and coolant lines to the storage tanks.  At Garcia's Tire and Detail Shop in Azle, a foot of snow caused the awning to collapse into all 5 service bays. The metal roof of the Eagle Mountain Memorial VFW Post #2137 also collapsed damaging the interior of the building.

An average of 3 to 5 inches of snow fell across Bell County. The local COOP observer in the city of Troy recorded 4 inches of snow. There were more than 20 vehicle accidents in the county due to the hazardous driving conditions. About 2,000 customers in the city of Belton lost power for a brief period of time. Almost all flights at the Killeen-Ft. Hood Regional airport were canceled, and several streets and bridges in the county were briefly closed before sand trucks were able to treat the roadways.

Four to six inches of snow fell across Anderson County. A NASA meteorologist recorded the highest amount of 6 inches at the Palestine upper air balloon facility. Several roads across the county were temporarily impassible as the snow was falling, but crews from TXDOT were able to treat the roadways and the roads were re-opened. The weather conditions played a significant role in numerous traffic accidents across the county, including a fatality on U.S. Highway 79.
A local newspaper reported that up to 5 inches of snow fell across Coryell County. Numerous roads were slushy, but ice was not a problem.
The emergency manager reported 3 to 5 inches of snow fell across the county. There were no major impacts.

Due to persistent rainfall of 1-2 over the county, some low lying areas flooded nearby roads. Most of the closed roads were reported in Precinct 2 which covers the southeast quadrant of the county. Closed roads included: CR 2310 at CR 3343, parts of CR 2336, CR 2408, and the south side service road of Interstate 30 at mile marker 134.  CR 2408 was washed out and would likely be closed for longer. Most of these roads remained closed through the morning hours of February 5th.
A motorist got her vehicle stuck in high water on CR 4754 and the vehicle had to be removed by a wrecker.
Mostly pea size hail fell but a few hail stones up to 0.75 were mixed with the smaller hail. The report was from the north Fort Worth/Keller area.

Up to 2 of snow was reported around the county but some icy spots on bridges were reported by the local TXDot.  Higher snowfall totals close to 5 of snow were reported in the southeastern portions of the county, and the Emergency Manager estimated 5 of snow near Lake Kiowa.

Four to six inches of snow fell in the northeastern corner of the county. The public reported 4.3 of snow 1 mile east of White Rock Lake, and 4.5 of snow in Mesquite. Elsewhere in the county, an average of 0.5-2 of snow was reported. The City of Dallas police reported about 284 accidents from midnight to 10 am on the 21st. A motorcyclist was injured on North Central Expressway after skidding on an icy patch.

An average of 2-4 of snow fell across the county, but some locations across the eastern third of the county reported 4-6 of snow. Six and a half inches of snow was reported in Pilot Point, and 5.5 of snow was reported near Frisco. The city of Denton reported 40 minor traffic accident and 7 major traffic accidents between the hours of 4:30 am and 10 am on the 21st.
A local newspaper reported that most of the county received at least four to five inches of snow. No major impacts were reported.

The local COOP observer in the town of Thornton received 4 inches of snowfall. A local newspaper reported that up to 5 inches of snow fell across the county with 4.5 inches of snow in Groesbeck. There was one minor accident due to the hazardous driving conditions.
The COOP observer in the city of Davilla reported 5 inches of snowfall. A local newspaper reported 4 to 6 inches of snow fell across the county. No major impacts were reported.
An average of 3 to 5 inches of snow fell across the county. The COOP observer in the city of Bremond recorded 4.2 inches of snowfall and the observer in Franklin recorded 4 inches.
An average of 4 to 5 inches of snow fell across the county. The local COOP observer in the city of Rosebud reported 5 inches of snowfall. No significant impacts were reported.
An average of 4 inches fell across the county. No significant problems were reported.

An average of 4-6 of snow fell across the county with the highest snowfall totals across the northern half of the county. The Emergency Manager reported 5.4 of snow in Terrell with the light snow was tapering off.  The public reported 4 of snow in the city of Kaufman. A local newspaper reported 1-4 of snow had fallen around Cedar Creek Lake.
Four to five and a half inches of snow fell across the county. A report of 5.2 of snow in the western part of the county was received.
An average of 6-8 of snow fell across the county. Eight inches of snow was reported in Plano by the Emergency Manager, and the COOP observer in Frisco reported 8 of snow.
An average of 3-7 of snow fell across the county with the highest amounts reported in the southwestern portions of the county.

Five accidents were also reported on the southbound ramp from East Loop 820 onto Interstate 30 due to ice, and the ramp had to be closed for 4 hours. Another person was killed in one of accidents on the ramp. Up to 1 of snow was reported around the county.

Timbers were also driven into a nearby double-wide mobile home, and a window was broken out at the residence. Some timbers were sticking up out of the ground around the residence. One 50-60' tall elm tree near the home was snapped in half and fell on a car. Only minor dents were sustained to the car. Also nearby, a fireworks stand was destroyed.

A house in the city of Denton was struck by lightning. The chimney was partially damaged, but the lightning strike did not start a fire.

A 60 foot tall oak tree was uprooted and crashed into a residence on 4th street in Lampasas. The house was significantly damaged. Also in Lampasas, the roof was blown off a portable building at the Lampasas Middle School.
