At a residence near West, high winds knocked a temporary building on its side. Tree damage and other minor building damage was also reported. Power outages were also reported in town.
Tree damage and minor building damage was reported in and around Ross, Tours, Leory, and Elm Mott. Power outages were also reported.

A 7 month old baby girl died after being left in a car for over 3 hours in Oak Cliff. The infant was discovered in the car at around 1:30 pm.  Ambient temperatures at the time were in only in the upper 70s but the heat inside the car was too much for the infant.
The Corsicana ASOS measured an 87 mph wind gust.
Thunderstorm winds lifted part of the roof off the Stonebriar Apartment complex in southwest Corsicana. The Altera Sterling House next door also sustained significant roof damage.
Numerous large trees were blown down from thunderstorm winds in a large swath starting from near Dawson and ending near Kerens. Some of these trees blocked roads or fell on cars and other structures.
Brookshire Grocery store in Corsicana lost approximately 30 percent of its roof and had some trusses bent due to thunderstorm wind damage.

A large boathouse had half of its roof blown off by thunderstorm winds in the Pinnacle Club Subdivision. Hundreds of trees were also reported to be down in the subdivision and some of the fallen trees damaged homes.
In Star Harbor, minor roof damage was reported and large tree limbs were blown down from thunderstorm winds.
In Key Ranch Estates, several homes were left uninhabitable after large trees were blown onto them from thunderstorm winds.

The roof of a business in a strip mall in Gun Barrel City collapsed due to thunderstorm winds. Significant sign damage was also reported in the city and large trees were uprooted. In Loon Bay, a boat dock was lifted out of the water and smashed into the porch of a resident. The neighboring house sustained extensive damage to its second story and the wind also moved the back wall.

A member of broadcast media measured a wind gust of 78 mph in Malakoff. The local newspaper reported two light poles were knocked down at the football field. A tin roof of a building was peeled back, and the sign at a church was blown out. Several trees were also knocked over and some trees fell on homes.

Several buildings in Mabank sustained significant damage due to thunderstorm winds. The fire marshall estimated that 14-15 commercial buildings were damaged. Terry's Furniture Store, Mid-Cities Storage, and Groom & Sons Hardware all sustained significant damage. Part of the second story collapsed at the furniture store, at least one storage building was blown over at the storage center, and the roof of the hardware store was partially lost. Blown off shingles were common at residential homes.
A brief EF-1 tornado, producing winds of 90 mph, touched down in Mabank and significantly damaged a residential home.  The tornado was approximately a quarter mile in length.
Trained spotters reported numerous trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds approximately 2 miles west of Van.

The Emergency Manager reported a long track of thunderstorm wind damage extending from just northeast of Mabank to Grand Saline.  Most of the damage resulted from numerous large trees being blown onto area roadways while some trees were reported to have fallen onto homes and vehicles.

The county newspaper reported that lightning caused a fire at a residence on County Road 2309.  One man died in the fire as he reentered the residence to try and put the fire out.  Nine children in the home escaped with only minor injuries. Two other house fires were also reported in the county: one on CR 3814 and a vacant house on CR 2319.
Several trees were reported down on several county roads near Emory.
Large trees were reported blown down by thunderstorm winds near Frankston.
Many trees were knocked down at Purtis Creek State Park, and the clean up took about a week to complete.

A county commissioner reported approximately 50 trees were over roads in the Precinct 2 area. Most of these trees were broken off at 30 to 40 feet up the tree trunk. It took two days to clean up the tree debris.

The large Love's Travel Center sign was knocked down in very strong thunderstorm winds. The sign fell on a part of the gas pump awning, damaging the awning and causing minor damage to a few of the gas pumps. Also in Van, large trees were uprooted, a few trees fell on the roofs of homes, and light poles and power lines were also down.
A vehicle accident at East Belton and CR 333 during a thunderstorm resulted in two injuries and extensive damage to the vehicles.

The county sheriff reported that 23 barricades were set up on various roads around the county due to flooding from persistent steady rainfall across the county. At one intesection in Acton the water was 8-10 inches deep. Rainfall totals averaged 3-3.5 across the county but were reported as high as 5 inches in the northern portions of the county. Most of the water had receded within a few hours. Some damage to the road surface on Paluxy Highway near Neri Road occurred.

Rainfall totals over 6 over the weekend resulted in Lake Graham overflowing its banks and flooding the nearby land. Also, flooding along the Brazos River backed up into area creeks and streams resulting in widespread flooding around the county. A high water rescue of three teenagers was performed on April 18th around 4 pm CDT when rising flood waters pushed their car off Power Plant Road in Graham. Another vehicle nearly got stuck in this same area. Rising waters also flooded Graham Bible Church where several inches of water was found inside the building, and the water in the parking lot was almost waist deep. Fireman's Park in Graham was under water. Several major roadways were closed on the 18th due to high water: HWY 380 West at Elm Creek, HWY 61 near Spivey Hill, HWY 16 north at the Archer Co line, and HWY 578. All roads were re-opened by the morning of the 19th.

Hopkins County local and county Emergency Management officials determined that damage and debris reported near the intersection of Interstate 30 and Highway 67 was caused by straight line winds of approximately 70 mph.  Winds damaged trees, powerlines and power poles near this location.

At 206 pm CDT a tornado near Midloathian was reported by an Arlington Airport weather observer in a special observation.  The tornado was last reported by Ellis County Emergency Management at 211 pm CDT.  This tornado was also reported by local county spotters and HAM radio operators.  The tornado occurred over open county and no damage was reported.  This tornado has been rated an EF-0 producing wind speeds between 70 and 85 mph.
Two semi-trucks were blown off of Interstate 45 near Alma by thunderstorm outflow winds.  The occupants of these trucks were not injured.  Winds also damaged some trees within the community of Alma.
McGregor Municipal Airport ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 54 kts as thunderstorms moved through the county.

Dallas Fort Worth area broadcast media reported 6 to 12 inch diameter trees were snapped by thunderstorm winds near Corsicana.  A sheet metal roof was also blown off of an old gas station.

Hill County Emergency Management and storm spotters reported a brief tornado southeast of the community of Hubbard.  This tornado occurred over open country and was only briefly on the ground and produced no damage. The tornado was rated EF-0, producing winds around 70 mph.
Waco broadcast media reported thunderstorm winds blew down a few large trees on Old Lorena Road near Woodway.  Winds were estimated to have gusted as high as 70 mph.

Ellis County Emergency Management reported a brief tornado touchdown approximately 2 miles northeast of Alma.  This tornado damaged an abandoned barn and uprooted and twisted a few trees.  The abandoned barn eventually collapsed due to the structural damage caused by the tornado.  This damage is consistent with a tornado producing wind speeds of 80 mph, so it has been rated EF-0.
Power lines were blown down in Cisco. The local emergency manager estimated a 60 mph wind gust.
Several large tree limbs and power lines were blown down by estimated an estimated 60 mph wind gust.

There was minor roof damage and windows blown out of a residence due to high winds. The shed next to the residence was destroyed.
Measured at Fort Worth Meacham Airport.
Several trees were blown down due to high winds in Thorndale. Several power lines were also knocked down after the trees fell on the lines.

Large trees were blown down near Palestine. The wind gust was estimated at 65 mph.
Six to eighteen inch diameter trees were blown down west of Palestine.
Several trees were blown down along county roads near Highway 51 northeast of Springtown.
Several homes in Ranger had shingles blown off the roofs. Winds were estimated at 55 to 60 MPH.

Significant urban flooding was reported in Killeen. Water had risen up to car doors and was stalling vehicles. Over 5 inches of rain fell in less than 2 hours.

Flash flooding was reported along Highway 199 west of Farm-to-Market Road 920 about 5 miles west of Boonsville. There was also water near the roadway on Farm-to-Market Road 2210 near the town of Gibtown.

Firefighters responded to a house fire caused by a lightning strike. The fire initially began in the attic, but the heat and smoke forced the firefighters back. The 4,000 square foot home was built in 2002.
A local auto-repair business suffered damage to six bay doors in Decatur. There were also tree limbs scattered along roadways and several homes had shingles removed from the roofs.

A 73 year old female was found deceased in her home on June 20th. The official cause of death was hyperthermia. No other details were made public. A 79 year old female was found deceased in her home, but had underlying medical conditions.
Penny size hail was reported in Tioga.
Lightning caused a house fire 3 miles southwest of Azle.
Measured by the Automated Weather Observation System at the Decatur Airport (KLUD).
An aircraft hanger was blown over, three aircraft were damaged and one was destroyed due to high winds. The report was relayed by the FAA.
Nickel size hail fell in the town of Bolivar.

High water was reported over Highway 79 near the town of Gause and Highway 36 near Milano at 945 AM CST. Heavy rain continued to fall through the morning hours and by the early afternoon hours, high water was still being reported near the town of Gause along County Roads 326 and 347 and Highway 79.

Reports of flash flooding in Robertson County began at 10 AM CST. High water was reported on Farm-to-Market Road 391 about 2.5 miles northwest of Wheelock, and over Highway 6 and Farm-to-Market Road 50 south of Hearne. Heavy rain continued through the afternoon hours and by 1245 PM CST, additional reports of flash flooding were reported. There was high water on Old Spanish Road near the town of Eaton, on Highway 6 near Benchley, on Highway 46 near the town of Wheelock, and on Farm-to-Market Road 50 near Mumford.

High water was reported in a residential structure in the city of Lorena. Several intersections in Hewitt were barricaded due to high water and Farm-to-Market Road 185 west of Waco Lake was closed due to flash flooding. Several roads by the Waco airport were also closed due to high water. Flooding was also reported in Lacy-Lakeview and Lorena.
Highway 164 at the Union Pacific railroad crossing was closed due to high water. Multiple streets were closed in Groesbeck due to flash flooding.

Numerous roads across the county had significant flash flooding. There were several flooded homes and a house rescue conducted in Palestine. Parts of Highway 315 was washed away and a vehicle was stranded near the town of Elmwood. At least 4 feet of water was over County Road 404 12 miles NNW of Palestine. Several roads in the city of Palestine were closed for several days due to damage suffered by the flood waters.

Significant flash flooding occurred in the southern parts of Kaufman County, especially in the city of Mabank. Numerous roads were flooded and water flowed over several bridges. Over 10 inches of rain fell in Mabank and this led to numerous homes threatened with flood water and at least four homes were inundated with water. One home had to be evacuated. Numerous vehicles suffered damage as the water rose and flooded the insides. The flooding was directly responsible for power outages throughout the area and led to a boil water notice.

Numerous reports of flash flooding were reported in the southeastern portions of the county. A vehicle was overtaken with water on Farm-to-Market Road 308 near the town of Bynum. Additional water was reported over Farm-to-Market Road 308 between the towns of Penelope and Birome and near Malone. There was also water over County Road 2114 west of Penelope and a bridge was washed out, stranding four motorists along NW 3150 Road, northeast of Dawson. Water was reported in homes between Hillsboro and Brandon.
High water was reported over Farm-to-Market Road 308 near the town of Leroy.

Significant flash flooding was reported in western Henderson County. Numerous high water rescues were conducted in the cities of Eustace, Log Cabin, Malakoff, Key Rance, and Goliad. The Precinct 1 County Commissioner reported that 15 to 20 roads were flooded at one time.

Water was reported over Farm-to-Market Road 73 near Coolidge. Highway 171 from Munger to Coolidge was flooded and impassable.  Low water crossings along Farm-to-Market Road 27 east of Coolidge were flooded, and Farm-to-Market Road 638 was also closed for one mile NE of Coolidge.

Significant flash flooding occurred in the southern parts of Navarro County as portions of the county received up to 14 inches of rainfall. Over twenty high water rescues were conducted by volunteer fire departments throughout the county. Many of the rescues were in the southwest parts of the county, near the town of Dawson. Both roads into the city of Dawson were blocked due to high water. This included Farm-to-Market Road 709 and Farm-to-Market Road 1838. Several homes in the towns of Pursley and Union High had water in them. Many roads in the southern parts of the county received damage and several bridges were washed away. Additional flooding near the town of Kerens was also reported. Farm-to-Market Road 309 near highway 287 was impassible due to high water. Flood waters also destroyed property throughout the county and preliminary damage estimates totaled 1.85 million dollars.
Lightning sparked a house fire about 10 miles east of Centerville.

Farm-to-Market Road 47 was underwater one mile north of Highway 198, County Road 308 was washed away two miles east of Highway 198, and Farm-to-Market Road 316 was closed due to high water at the intersection of Highway 198.

Residual flooding lasted for many hours after the heavy rain had ended. Farm-to-Market Road 2330 remained closed as did Farm-to-Market Road 315 from Farm-to-Market Road 837 to Highway 175. Several county roads throughout the county also remained closed due to residual flooding.
Minor flooding was reported at the intersection of Interstate 35 and Swisher Rd near Lake Dallas.
Several flood prone locations experienced minor flooding in Hillsboro.
Several streets experienced minor flooding and small streams around the county were filled with water.

Numerous trees and large limbs were blown down with a few trees landing on cars. Power poles were leaning around the Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, where a major league baseball game was to be played at 7 PM. The damage was concentrated from Highway 360 between Interstate 30 and Division Rd, west to Collins Street. Five parking lot attendees for the Texas Rangers suffered minor injuries from flying debris.
There was minor damage to a warehouse and minor damage to local businesses roofs and signs. The damage was at the intersection of Highway 360 and N Carrier Parkway in Grand Prairie.
Penny size hail was reported in Crandall.

The automated surface observation system at the Waco Airport reported a 77 MPH wind. There were multiple trees down around the airport and near China Springs. Power outages were reported near the airport.
Quarter size hail fell just east of Forney.
Downburst winds caused damage to barns and several homes in the city of Forney.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell north of Bridgeport.
An eighteen-wheeler tractor trailer was blown off Interstate 30 near Campbell.
A large tree was blown down into a power line in the town of Petty.
A large tree was uprooted and fell on a house in Leonard. The felled tree also damaged a storage building and outdoor playground equipment.
The Sheriff's Office reported large trees were knocked down and blocking roads in McKinney.
Multiple large trees were knocked down by downburst winds in Elkhart.
The automated weather station at the Sulphur Springs Municipal Airport (KSLR) measured a 67 mph wind gust.
Dime size hail was reported on CR 4131, two miles south of Cumby.
Trees were knocked down by thunderstorm winds on CR 4131, two miles south of Cumby.
A 60 mph wind gust was estimated at the Van Zandt Sheriff's Office in Canton.

PSI Industries in Olney lost its roof and a door due to thunderstorm winds. Also in Olney, the drive-thru menu at Dairy Queen was knocked over, the sign at Goldsmith Supply Co. was damaged, and trees, tree limbs, signs, and power poles were knocked down. A possible downburst may have caused the damage. In addition, several power poles were knocked down along FM 2178 on the north side of town.
Sixty mph winds were estimated in the city of Kaufman. A few trees were knocked down by the strong winds.
Penny size hail was reported in Garrett.
Thunderstorm winds of 60 mph were estimated in Garrett.
A trained spotter reported roof damage to 3 buildings on the north side of Ennis. No other information was available.
Roof and ceiling damage was reported at the Villager Inn near Highway 80 and Spur 557; west of Terrell. A large portion of the roof was torn off.
The emergency manager reported roof and wall damage to one home on CR 213A and also 2 metal buildings in the same area were destroyed.
Numerous power poles and trees were reported down north of Highway 82 between Texoma Parkway and Loy Lake Road. Additional wind damage was also noted to the north and east of this location.
Estimated thunderstorm winds of 60-70 mph were reported in Sherman by a local newspaper reporter. Powerlines and trees were knocked down in the city.
Damaging downburst winds hit a home 2 miles outside the city of Comanche, ripping off most of the roof and uprooting a large mulberry tree. The tree fell across the garage.

More than 30 homes in the Oakmost subdivision of Corinth were damaged when a downburst hit the area. The only information regarding the damage was limited to a shed imploding on Andover Street, a brick wall fell over, and several chimneys were damaged.
In the Post Oak/Meadowview area of Corinth, trees up to 14 in diameter were knocked down by downburst winds.  The roof of a mobile home was also peeled back.
One inch hail was reported at the intersection of Highway 287 and Parks School House Road on the east side of Waxahachie.

Strong thunderstorm winds caused tree damage and downed power lines along a stretch from north Waco to downtown Waco. Large trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds on Lake Shore Drive near McLennan Community College. Four large trees were also down at 19th Street and Tanglewood Ave near the McLennan Community College. Other downed large tree limbs and splintered trees were reported along the path towards downtown Waco.
Numerous tree limbs were broken off in Breckenridge due to thunderstorm winds that were estimated at 60 mph.

Numerous large trees and tree branches were knocked down across Stephenville by thunderstorm winds.  The newspaper reported that the northwest parts of the city appeared to be hit the hardest by the winds.  Power lines were also down in parts of the city.

A possible microburst caused damage along a 3 mile stretch on FM 219 between Lingleville and Huckabay.  The exact location of the damage is unknown.  Trees were snapped, homes were damaged, and a barn lost its metal roof.  More significantly, a large silo was blown from its base across a field.
A condo in DeCordova Bend Estates sustained minor roof damage due to thunderstorm winds. Also, some large trees were knocked down.

Scattered tree damage was reported in Rising Star where large tree limbs and small trees were knocked over by thunderstorm winds. One large tree was uprooted and fell onto part of a manufactured home.  Another tree fell on a parked minivan.
Lightning struck a utility pole on Cottage Avenue that resulted in a small fire and damage to the pole.
The automated weather station at North Texas Regional Airport/Perrin Field (KGYI) measured a wind gust of 68 mph.
A construction trailer was damaged at the Hagerman National Wildlife Refuge Visitor Center, and several trees that were larger than 6 inches in diameter were split. One minor injury was reported.

Strong thunderstorm winds, possibly from a microburst, turned over several portable buildings at a business in Reagor Springs. The roofs were torn off a few of the portable buildings and nearly all 18 were damaged. A mobile home on the same property was turned over and landed on two vehicles. Also in Reagor Springs, trees were knocked down and shingles were torn off roofs.
Quarter size hail was reported in Bellmead.
A tree was blown onto a house in Lacy-Lakeview.
Quarter size hail was reported in Lacy-Lakeview.
The Forney PD reported wind damage to the Dairy Queen on HWY 80 near Pinson Road.
Penny size hail was reported in Forney by the local police department.
A brief tornado was spotted over Benbrook Lake. No damage occurred with this tornado.

An EF0 tornado with maximum winds of 75 mph touched down in far northeastern Lamar County. The tornado touched down near FM 195 and CR 46650, and then moved due east, crossing FM 195. Tree damage was noted early in the track. Near the end of the track, the tornado damaged a few barns; causing them to lose part of their roofs. Near this same location, on CR 45600, a manufactured home was damaged and lost part of its roof.
A trained spotter reported a tornado just north of Lindsay.  No damage was reported.

A tornadic supercell produced several tornado touchdowns from east of Ferris to Seagoville. The first touchdown occurred a few miles east of Ferris in open country and tracked to the northeast into Dallas County.

This tornado is a continuation from Ellis County. A tornadic supercell produced several tornado touchdowns from east of Ferris to Seagoville. The first touchdown occurred a few miles east of Ferris in open country.  The tornado moved to the northeast into Dallas County where it remained in open country until it entered the city limits of Seagoville in southeast Dallas County. In Seagoville, three duplex buildings just east of HWY 175 near May Rd. suffered significant roof damage with almost complete loss of the roofs.  Also, a single-family home to the northeast of the duplex buildings suffered significant roof damage. The winds estimated with this tornado at its peak intensity were 90 mph, and the total path length was over 9 miles long.

Minor roof damage on the order of EF0 damage was noted along much of the path of this tornado, but EF2 damage was observed near the intersection of Irving Blvd and Mockingbird Lane in west Dallas. Near the intersection, substantial damage occurred to a warehouse. An exterior wall of the warehouse collapsed causing part of the roof to collapse. In addition, a tractor trailer traveling on Mockingbird Lane in front of the warehouse was blown into the warehouse, and the driver sustained minor injuries. Additional stores in the industrial area near the intersection sustained roof damage and holes were ripped into some roofs. Local broadcast media recorded this tornado live as it moved north through the western portions of the city of Dallas. Maximum wind speeds were estimated to be 115 mph.

Significant flooding occurred in Bell County from the remnants of Tropical Storm Hermine. In Killeen, Highway 190 was closed due to flood waters. Residents were evacuated from an apartment complex on Watercrest Dr due to rising waters, and numerous cars with occupants were submerged in Killeen. There was one fatality in the city of Killeen when a 19 year old female's vehicle was submerged in flood waters on Reese Creek Road. Homes near the towns of Elms and Robinette had to be evacuated by boat. In Nolanville, a car was swept away, and a mobile home park was evacuated resulting in the rescue of 35 to 40 people. Salado Creek in Salado flooded the access roads of Interstate 35 and destroyed several businesses and residential structures along the creek. A bridge on Armstrong Road which crossed Salado Creek was washed away. Numerous roads were also flooded in the city of Temple. There were 17 businesses and 26 residences affected by the flood waters in the city of Belton.

Highway 190 east of Copperas Cove, Farm-to-Market Road 1829 at Highway 236, and several other roads throughout the county were closed due to high water. There was one high water rescue on County Road 132 just off of Farm-to-Market Road 1783. A few homes around the county were damaged when flood waters entered the homes.

Several county roads and Farm-to-Market roads were impassible or closed due to high water. Swift water rescues were conducted in Whitney after two apartment complexes were flooded. There were at least 17 high water rescues conducted across the county. At least 40 homes suffered damage due to flood waters, and county roads across the county experienced significant damage.

Water was reported over a bridge on Farm-to-Market Road 1126 one mile west of Interstate 45 near the town of Rice. Several roads were closed in the western portions of the county, and rising water was reported near several residential structures on Farm-to-Market Road 709 south of Dawson.

At least 10 cars stalled on Highway 287 north of Decatur due to high water on parts of the highway. There was also one foot of water over Highway 114 at Farm-to-Market Road 718 near the city of Aurora.

Heavy rain began to fall before sunrise and several intersections across Tarrant County had to be closed due to high water as numerous vehicles stalled. In east Fort Worth, 10 employees had to be rescued from a well drill site after becoming trapped by high water. A mobile home park in North Richland Hills had to be evacuated due to rising flood waters. High water rescues and evacuations were also conducted at an apartment complex in Arlington as high water entered numerous apartment buildings. At least 129 homes and 68 apartment units in Arlington suffered damage as the water levels reached 8 feet in some structures. Additional evacuations were conducted in the city of Everman as flood waters reached residential structures; entering three of the homes. An intermediate school in the city of Keller was evacuated as a nearby creek quickly rose, and water entered the gym at Cross Timbers Middle School.  In Southlake, two bridges on White Chapel Blvd were damaged forcing the closure of the roads, and chunks of asphalt fell off North White Chapel Blvd. Four feet of water was reported on Love Henry Court in Southlake. In Mansfield, several roads were closed and 20 homes had water damage. Several creeks across the county flooded over 100 additional homes. The most significant flooding occurred along Johnson Creek, Key Branch, Bear Creek, and Rush Creek. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
A high water rescue was conducted in the city of Crawford due to rapidly rising flood waters.

Several low water crossings in the city of Dallas were closed shortly after sunrise due to several feet of water covering the roadways. As the rain continued, additional flooding was reported. The entrance and exit ramps along Interstate 35 at Royal Lane were closed due to high water. Several high water rescues were conducted in the cities of Lancaster and Grand Prairie. A creek in Irving threatened numerous homes and 90 people were evacuated by dump trucks.

A tornado caused mainly roof damage to several brick homes on the southeast side of Lake Ray Hubbard near Heath. Another home had its chimney knocked over and some large tree damage also occurred along the path of this tornado. The winds were estimated to be between 85-95 mph.

A storm chaser caught a brief tornado approximately two miles south of Riesel.  The tornado was on the ground as it crossed HWY 6, but otherwise the tornado remained over open land and did not cause any damage.
A 65 mph wind gust was estimated at Hall Road and HWY 175 in Seagoville.
A lightning strike started a house fire in Celina.  No other information was available, and the time of the strike was estimated from radar.
A lightning strike started a fire at a home in the 3900 block of Estrella Court in northwest Fort Worth.

A lightning strike hit a home in the Chisholm Spring subdivision in Newark.  The lightning strike entered the home through the satellite dish and traveled through the cable, charring the walls and floor around the cable. The charge caused a computer to catch on fire.
A lightning strike struck the chimney of a home in the 1000 block of Aspen Ridge Drive in Southlake. The home sustained heavy smoke damage.
A lightning strike at a home in the 200 block of Moonlight Drive in Euless resulted in a small attic fire and roof damage.
The automated weather station at Cox Field in Paris (KPRX) recorded a 61 mph wind gust. Some tree damage was reported in and around Paris.
The automated weather station at Addison Airport (KADS) recorded a 60 mph wind gust.
A brief tornado touched down at Mother Neff State Park near the cave. At least six trees were twisted and snapped. The trees were at least a foot in diameter.
Flooding was reported along FM 926 approximately 1 mile west of Newcastle.
Residual flooding continued along FM 926 west of Newcastle after the rain ended.
Quarter size hail was reported 1.5 miles south of Dodd City on FM 2077.
Penny size hail was reported in Canton.
Quarter size hail was reported 1 mile east of Corsicana on HWY 31.
Quarter size hail was reported on FM 309 south of Kerens.
Three-quarter inch hail was reported in Frankston by the volunteer fire department.
Nickel size hail was reported 3 miles south of Harker Heights.
Half dollar size hail was reported near Salado.
Quarter size hail was reported 2 miles north of Salado.
Nickel size hail was reported 2 miles southwest of Hewitt.
Nickel size hail increased to slightly larger than quarter size 2 miles southwest of Hewitt.
Golf ball size hail was reported 1 mile northwest of Lake Creek Lake.
Quarter size hail was reported at Lake Creek Lake.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Wortham.
Nickel size hail was reported in Morgan Mill.
A retired NWS employee reported half dollar to golf ball size hail fell at his residence located approximately 6 miles southwest of Bluff Dale. The retired employee's car was heavily dented.
Three-quarter inch size hail was reported north of Sanger on I-35 at mile marker 480.
Numerous roads were closed throughout the county for several hours due to the heavy rainfall. No major problems were reported.
Several trees were knocked down by strong thunderstorm winds near Loop 820 and Trinity Blvd in east Fort Worth.

Numerous roads throughout the county were closed due to flood waters. Interstate 35 was closed in both directions in the cities of Corinth and Lewisville. Three people were rescued from stranded vehicles in Lake Dallas and evacuations of homes were conducted in the city of Aubrey. Flood waters reached homes along Timbercreek Drive in Lewisville after the homes were evacuated. A total of 30 homes suffered some degree of flood damage in the county.

A trained spotter measured a 76 mph wind gust in Hubbard. The storm spotter also reported tree limbs were knocked down in the town. The sheriff's office reported some minor structural damage occurred in Hubbard, but no other information could be obtained.

Numerous roads throughout the county were closed due to high water, especially in the southwestern portions of the county. Water rescues were conducted in the cities of Sherman and Gunter. One house was flooded in the city of Denison.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Purdon.
Hen egg size hail was reported 2 miles south of Corsicana.

Numerous roads across the county were closed due to high water but the Alvarado area was hit the hardest. One driver was swept away on CR 607 at Mountain Creek near Alvarado and drowned. A two story home near Alvarado had water above the first floor of the home. Elsewhere one man was trapped in a van by high water on Farm-to-Market Road 917 near County Road 613 and was rescued by first responders. Five individuals were swept into rising waters along English Trail in the northeast part of the county and were later rescued.
Golf ball size hail was reported just south of Eustace.
Quarter size hail was reported in Murchison.
Several county roads were closed in the southern portions of the county due to flood waters. Farm-to-Market Roads 678 and 2896 were also closed. One home suffered flood damage.
Trees were blown down in Berryville.
A few county roads throughout the county and Farm-to-Market Road 217 near the town of Mosheim was closed due to high water.
A couple of trees were knocked down in Jewett.

Significant tree damage occurred in Palestine with several large trees falling on roofs. Some trees also fell on cars causing significant damage. The newspaper also reported that several metal portable buildings were blown onto the east loop, and the roof was blown off The Silver Lady on West Oak Street in downtown Palestine. The store sustained significant damage to the interior.  Thousands of residents lost power during and after the storm.

Four buildings at the Woodstock Apartment Complex were damaged by strong thunderstorm winds possibly from a microburst.  Part of the roofs of each building were damaged resulting in holes in some roofs. Some windows were also blown out, and a few chimney stacks were blown over.

A very brief EF0 tornado partially removed a roof off a home on Bowspirit Lane in northeast Fort Worth. Several wood fences were also damaged in the subdivision. The maximum estimated winds were 75 mph.
Residual flooding of area roadways and creeks occurred after 7 to 8 inches of rain fell across the county.
Numerous roads and creeks remained flooded well after the heavy rain had ended. This was after 6 to 7 inches of rain fell across much of the county.
Numerous roads and creeks remained flooded for many hours after the heavy rain had ended. Up to 8 inches of rain fell across the county.
Several roads and creeks across the county remained closed due to high water after the heavy rain had ended. Up to 7 inches of rain fell across the county.
Up to 10 inches of rain fell across Coryell County, and many roads and creeks remained closed for many hours after the heavy rain had ended.
Many roads and creeks remained flooded after 10 inches of rain fell across the county.
Tree limbs were knocked down throughout Mart due to strong thunderstorm winds. A few tree limbs fell on a parked truck and damaged the vehicle.

A lightning strike started a house fire at CR 2310 and FM 1870 east-southeast of Sulphur Springs. The upper story was engulfed in flames at one point and the home was heavily damaged. One person was treated at the scene with minor injuries.
Tree limbs were knocked down around the city of Frankston.  Crews spent much of the night removing tree limbs from power lines and roadways.
Two boys were shocked by a downed power line near Kris Street and Jerrell Street in North Richland Hills. Both boys were transported to area hospitals.
Quarter size hail was reported 5 miles northeast of the intersection of US 69 and HWY 19.
Quarter size hail was reported on I-30 at mile marker 125 on the southeast side of Sulphur Springs.
Half inch to penny size hail was reported in Pickton.
Penny size hail increased to the size of nickels in Moody.
Hen egg size hail was reported at FM 2194 and CR 658 northeast of Farmersville.
Golf ball size hail was reported at HWY 69 and FM 903 near Celeste.
Nickel size hail was reported in Wagner.
Quarter size hail was reported 2 miles north of Moody.
Lots of penny size hail was reported in Lorena.
A trained spotter reported mostly quarter size hail 4 miles north of Moody, but some golf ball sized hail stones were mixed in.
Nickel size hail was reported in Greenville by a trained spotter. The local newspaper reported hail up to 1 inch in diameter had fallen in Greenville.
Quarter to golf ball size hail fell in Lorena. Cars were damaged in the city.
Quarter size hail was reported in Golinda.
Quarter size hail was reported in South Sulphur.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Commerce. The local newspaper reported some minor roof damage and lots of car damage from the hail.
Nickel size hail increased to quarter size hail in Merit.
Quarter to golf ball size hail was reported in Avalon.
Nickel and quarter size hail was covering the ground in Deport.
Baseball size hail was reported 3 miles southeast of Avalon.
Quarter size hail was reported in Able Springs.
Golf ball size hail was reported 4 miles south of Otto.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Lone Oak.
Penny size hail was reported in Wills Point.
Three inch size hail was reported in Rice. The mayor of Rice reported that vehicles were damaged at city hall.
Golf ball size hail increased to baseball size hail in Seven Points.
A 60 mph wind gust was estimated in Seven Points.
A 60 mph wind gust was estimated in Eureka. Half inch size hail also fell.
Hail up to quarter size was reported in Powell.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Eustace.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Sulphur Springs.
A 60-70 mph wind gust was estimated in the Bethel-Cayuga area.
Quarter size hail was reported at ACR 460 and FM 860 near Bois D'Arc.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Bradford.
Quarter size hail was reported near Fosterville which is located about halfway between Brushy Creek and Poynor.
Golf ball size hail was reported on HWY 155 two miles south of Frankston.
Nickel size hail was reported in Berryville.
The Sheriff's Office received at least 20 calls about trees on roadways across the county.  The Precinct 1 County Commissioner was still out removing tree limbs from county roads the next morning.
A large tree in Fairfield was snapped by strong thunderstorm winds. Other minor tree damage was also observed in the city.
Hail up to the size of quarters was reported in Gun Barrel City.
Up to 12 inches of rain fell in a 12 hour period across Bell County and this led to residual flooding of many roads and small creeks for several hours after the heavy rain had ended.

An EF0 tornado hit the Rolling Hills subdivision southwest of Lone Oak. Ten homes sustained damage with one home completely destroyed. The destroyed home was an unoccupied apartment over a garage. The apartment was lifted up from its wood beam supports and displaced along the track of the twister. In addition, tree damage was observed, and some trees and tree limbs damaged homes and cars. The maximum winds were estimated to be between 80-85 mph.

A strong EF2 tornado hit the town of Rice damaging several homes, derailing train cars, damaging a school, and overturning cars on the interstate. The tornado began about 4 miles outside the town limits of Rice and first damaged two homes near NW 050 road.  One of the homes was completely destroyed. About a mile and half later, the tornado struck another home causing the exterior walls to collapse and taking the roof off the home. Next, the tornado entered the town of Rice and moved over a train track derailing 11 train cars. One of the train cars ended up in the nearby baseball field of the high school. The baseball field and nearby football stadium was also damaged, and the softball field was completely destroyed. Power poles and bleachers were damaged at the football and baseball field. At the softball field, the fences, dugouts, scorekeepers stand, scoreboard, light poles, and bleachers were all destroyed. The tornado then damaged an intermediate school causing one wall to lean and peeling the roof off the gymnasium. Next, the tornado crossed Interstate 45 where it overturned a few cars and trapped some people. One 18 wheeler carrying a dump truck lost the dump truck which fell onto a car traveling in the other direction.  The driver of the car sustained minor cuts.  East of the interstate, the tornado damaged 4 more homes causing mainly roof damage to the homes. The roof damage east of the interstate was mostly EF1 intensity. A total of 4 persons were injured during this tornado. All were transported to area hospitals with minor, non-life threatening injuries. In addition to the structural damage, trees were snapped along the path of the tornado. The maximum sustained winds were estimated to be 135 mph.
A large oak tree was knocked down along FM 148 near Lively and Peeltown.
A barn in Kerens that housed tractors and other similar equipment was destroyed by high thunderstorm winds.
Quarter size hail was reported 4 miles south of Elkhart on HWY 287.

A microburst damaged part of the southern portions of the city of Greenville. Several businesses and residential structures sustained roof damage. The roof of a Braum's was heavily damaged, and the roof at an automobile service station on Business 67 was partially blown off. In addition, the garage door at the service station at the Enterprise Rent-A-Car was blown in and a gash was torn into the wall. Several large trees were blown down, a gas station sign was blown down, and a sign at Crossroads Mall fell on a car. Three power poles were snapped on Sayle Street causing a black out in the area. Maximum wind gusts were estimated to be 65 mph. One person sustained minor injuries, and was treated and released from the medical center.

Lightning started a house fire on Boydstun Loop in Killeen. The lightning bolt burned a large hole in the roof and caused extensive damage to the roof and attic.  Fire control damage occurred in three other rooms.
Lightning started a house fire in the 700 block of South White Chapel Blvd in Southlake. The million dollar home sustained substantial damage.
According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Severe Drought was observed across the county.
According to the U.S Drought Monitor, Severe Drought was observed across the southern half of the county.

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across the southeastern portions of north Texas, drought conditions worsened. In the early part of December, the drought conditions in Leon County quickly worsened into the Extreme Drought (D3) category according to the US Drought Monitor.

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across the southeastern portions of north Texas, drought conditions worsened. In the early part of December, the drought conditions in Robertson County quickly worsened into the Extreme Drought (D3) category according to the US Drought Monitor.

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across the southeastern portions of north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. In the early part of December, drought conditions across Milam County were classified as Severe Drought (D2). Near the end of the month, conditions worsened into the Extreme Drought (D3) category over the eastern half of the county.

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across the southeastern portions of north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. For nearly all of the month of December, the drought conditions in Anderson County were classified as Severe Drought (D2); however, the extreme southern portions of the county were classified as Extreme Drought (D3) by the end of the month.

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. For nearly all of the month of December, the drought conditions in Mills County were classified as Severe Drought (D2).

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. The drought conditions in Freestone County were classified as Severe Drought (D2).

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. The drought conditions in Limestone County were classified as Severe Drought (D2) and encompassed all but the northwestern corner of the county.

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. The drought conditions in Henderson County were classified as Severe Drought (D2).

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. The drought conditions in Erath County were classified as Severe Drought (D2); however some relief was noted over part of the county near the end of the month due to 0.50-1.50 of rain.

The drought conditions in Eastland County were classified as Severe Drought (D2); however some relief was noted over part of the county near the end of the month due to 0.50-1.50 of rain.

The drought conditions in Stephens County were classified as Severe Drought (D2); however some relief was noted over part of the county near the end of the month due to 0.50-1.50 of rain.

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. The drought conditions in Palo Pinto County were classified as Severe Drought (D2); however some relief was noted over part of the county near the end of the month due to 0.50-1.50 of rain.

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. For about two weeks, much of Young County was classified as Severe Drought (D2); however the drought conditions were eased by the end of the month due to much of the county receiving over an inch of rain.

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. The drought conditions in Falls County were classified as Severe Drought (D2) and encompassed most of the county.

As rainfall deficits continued to grow across north Texas, drought conditions worsened according to the US Drought Monitor. The drought conditions in Van Zandt County were observed across only the southern half of the county, and were classified as Severe Drought (D2).
A three foot diameter tree was blown down at the intersection of Highway 294 and Farm-to-Market Road 319 near Elkhart.

A 1500 to 2000 acre grass fire ignited around 4 PM near County Road 574 about three miles west of the school house in the town of Ridge. Volunteer fire departments from Goldthwaite, Mullin, and Brookesmith fought the fire until 930 PM and then returned the next day from 11 AM until 7 PM. No structures suffered damage.

Strong winds with a cold front gusted between 50-55 mph in Bell County. On Interstate 35 in Temple, a tractor-trailer rig was flipped over by the strong winds. In Killeen, the wall of an apartment building was knocked in due to the strong winds. The strong winds also resulted in power outages across the area caused by leaning power poles and tree limbs and debris blown into the power lines.

An accumulation of 1.0-1.5 of ice and snow fell across Collin County. Most of the winter precipitation accumulation is thought to be from ice and sleet. A COOP observer in Frisco reported an ice/snow total of 1.2. Travel on roadways was treacherous and several accidents were reported. A driver was injured in Plano when the vehicle hit a wall and another accident involved a DART bus. The entire region remained entrenched in cold air for 5 days, and thus the ice and snow did not have much chance to melt. This resulted in numerous accidents during the week as the roads remained icy. Another vehicle rollover during the week at HWY 380 and CR 458 resulted in one injury.

A man was found frozen to death near Wright Historical Park in Dublin. The man was discovered the morning of February 1st. A cold front had come through during the night with temperatures falling into the teens by daybreak and strong north winds sustained at 20-25 mph with higher gusts.

Total ice and snow accumulations of up to 1.5 were received across Dallas County. Sleet was reported to be covering the ground in some locations. The icy roads resulted in treacherous roadways and numerous major accidents. Parts of Interstate 35E had to be shut down after numerous tractor-trailers became stuck or jackknifed.  Loop 12 in Oak Cliff proved to be especially treacherous for travelers. The ice and snow caused a party tent to collapse inside the Cotton Bowl.  The tent had been set up for festivities surrounding the Super Bowl.

The Possum Kingdom West fire began in Stephens County near FM 1148 and FM 3253. However, strong winds on critical fire weather days also drove this fire into Palo Pinto and Young County. On the 18th, it made a fast run towards Graham in Young County resulting in evacuations for the town of Bunger. The fire also caused several hundred people to be evacuated around PK Lake. It scorched 90% of the 1500 acre Possum Kingdom Lake State Park on April 17th, but no structures were lost at the park. On April 15th, this fire merged with the Hohertz Fire in Palo Pinto County and the fires were renamed the PK Complex. On April 17th, the PK East Fire in Palo Pinto County was added to this complex, and on April 19th, the Jackson Ranch Fire in Stephens County also burned into the complex. In all, 126,734 acres were burned by this complex of four fires, 167 homes were destroyed, 2 churches were destroyed, and another 124 outbuildings were lost. The PK West Fire burned the most acres and may have burned over 80,000 acres. This fire burned 52 homes in Sportsman World, 37 homes at Gaines Bend, and 24 homes in Hog Bend. Several mobile homes on the west side of the lake near FM 1148 and FM 1287 were burned. This fire also burned the 100-year-old Cedar Springs United Methodist Church west of Palo Pinto. At least 22 known heads of cattle were killed by this fire and several more were injured.

The Hohertz fire began in southwest Palo Pinto County, approximately 9 miles northwest of Strawn. The local newspaper reported an arching power line started the fire in a pasture. Early on, some deer stands and oil field equipment were burned. On April 15th, this fire merged with the PK West Fire in Stephens County and the fires were renamed the PK Complex. On April 17th, the PK East fire in Palo Pinto County burned into this complex, and on April 19th, the Jackson Ranch Fire in Stephens County also joined this complex. In all, 126,734 acres were burned by this complex of four fires, 167 homes were destroyed, 2 churches were destroyed, and another 124 outbuildings were lost.

The Jackson Ranch Fire began in southeast Stephens County, approximately 4 miles east of La Casa. On April 17th, this fire caused the evacuation of the towns of Caddo and Strawn. On April 19th, it became a part of the PK Complex Fire. In all, 126,734 acres were burned by this complex of four fires, 167 homes were destroyed, 2 churches were destroyed, and another 124 outbuildings were lost. The Jackson Ranch Fire burned an estimated 6,687 acres of land.

The PK East Fire began in northern Palo Pinto County and became part of the PK Complex Fire. On April 17th, parts of Palo Pinto County west of Hwy 16 and south of PK Lake were evacuated, and also the Peninsula on PK Lake. In all, 126,734 acres were burned by this complex of four fires, 167 homes were destroyed, 2 churches were destroyed, and another 124 outbuildings were lost. The PK East Fire burned an estimated 10,996 acres of land. This fire burned the First Baptist Church of Possum Kingdom Lake near Hwy 16.
The Hubbard Creek Fire burned 800 acres.

The East Sidwynicks Fire began east of Carbon and burned around 3000 acres. The north side of Gorman was evacuated as a result of the fire. One firefighter died while fighting the fire and 6 more were injured. The firefighter that died was struck by a vehicle while trying to escape the inferno. The six injured firefighters were burned and two of them required hospitalization.

The Bryson Complex Fire burned a total of 7500 acres and consisted of two fires: The Rockcreek Fire that burned 5300 acres and the Shanafelt Fire that burned 2200 acres. Some of this acreage was in neighboring Young County. One fire was started by downed electrical lines. U.S. Highway 380 west of Bryson in Young County had to be closed for several hours on the 23rd.
The CR104 Fire began 2 miles north of Cisco and burned approximately 2000 acres. Five homes and one vehicle were destroyed.
The Mossy Rock Ranch Fire began 8.5 miles southwest of Caddo and burned approximately 850 acres.
The Smith Fire burned approximately 2000 acres.
The Molshee Road Fire burned one acre of land and 60 square bales of hay.
The Lake Cisco fire began near the Williamson Dam off Hwy 6 and burned approximately 2000 acres. A barn was lost, and so was a garage that contained a motorcycle, truck, and riding lawn mower.

An arsonist set a grass fire in the 1500 block of Liberty Street in Weatherford. This fire burned a barn, a well house, a shed, and a Ford Mustang. It also damaged a historic home on the same property.

The city park had to be closed due to extensive tree and wind damage to the park. Several trees in the city were uprooted or split in half. Extensive roof damage also occurred to barns at Texas Safari outside of Clifton. Multiple trees and power poles were also downed throughout the county.
Large trees were blown down by thunderstorm winds 1 to 2 miles south of Meridian on Highway 6.
Trees were knocked down by high winds at the Bosque Valley Golf Course.
A 5-year old boy drowned on Benbrook Lake after the boat he was in capsized due to strong winds gusting to around 35 mph.
A home and a barn near Jackson Road and Ripy Road, west of Denton, sustained roof damage. The doors were also ripped from the barn.
Thunderstorm winds estimated at 65 mph blew down power poles east of Haslet near Alliance Airport.
A one foot diameter tree was downed on North Beach St., north of Interstate 820 and south of Fossil Creek Blvd.
Thunderstorm winds blew down a large tree in the Kennedale community.
A trained spotter measured a 61 mph wind gust in Mansfield.
One inch hail fell near Bonham.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed a very large barn 4 miles north-northwest of Cleburne.

Straight-line winds resulted in the collapse of a wall of the Medicine Chest Pharmacy in Alvarado near North Cummings Dr. and Highway 67.  Straight-line winds also damaged signs, power poles, and a bank drive-through in the same general area. A light pole was knocked down at Charles Head Stadium, a field goal post was bent, and the track was damaged at the facilities. The American Red Cross reported that 38 homes were damaged in Alvarado and three of these homes were destroyed.
Trained spotters measured 70 mph winds in Burleson.
Trained spotters measured 67 mph winds and reported power outages in Sand Flat which is approximately 8 miles southeast of Cleburne.

Significant wind damage occurred in Grandview. The American Red Cross reported that 12 structures were damaged in Grandview. Most of these were commercial buildings and four sustained major damage. A building behind city hall had its roof peeled back, a city barn was heavily damaged, several houses had shingle damage, and a nursing home and apartment building had roof damage. Numerous trees and tree limbs were knocked down, and two 18 wheelers were blown over.
Power poles and trees were knocked down in Venus. The American Red Cross reported than 31 homes sustained minor damage in Venus.
Thunderstorm winds blew several trees down in the community of Blum which is approximately 6 miles south of Rio Vista.

An elderly woman on oxygen died during a power outage that was caused by a tree that had blown into the power lines down the street. The woman lived in the west side of Fort Worth. Area automated weather stations recorded wind gusts up to 40 mph on this day.

The Hubbard's Furniture Store in Denison was damaged by strong winds. The winds ripped a 75 foot by 25 foot piece of metal from the front of the building, and sent it sailing into two trucks parked in front of the store. Minor damage was sustained to the trucks. The automated weather station nearby reported peak wind gusts up to 46 mph on this day.

Winds up to 70 mph were estimated in Sherman. A tree split and fell onto a house on the 1200 block of Wells Ave in Sherman. The tree went partially through the roof of the house. Trees were also reported down in other parts of the town.
One inch hail fell near Rowlett Road and Lakeview Pkwy in Rowlett.
Thunderstorm winds damaged the roofs of two mobile homes and one single family home south of Venus.
Thunderstorm winds blew down 6 to 12 inch diameter tree limbs near FM 2738 and Highway 67.  This location is approximately 4 miles northeast of Alvarado.
Measured from a school's weather-net observation.
Thunderstorm winds were responsible for broken windows approximately 6 miles south-southwest of Midlothian.

Significant roof damage was reported in Waxahachie. The damage was surveyed by the NWS and straight-line winds around 80 mph were confirmed. A warehouse on the south side of town lost most of its roof. An apartment complex on Franklin Street sustained partial roof loss and damage to brick walls. Damage also occurred to the roof of the Comfort Suites near I-35E and Hwy 287 on the north side of the city. Along I-35E, the Stelco Industries building was nearly destroyed. Heavy machinery at the plant was moved. The awning at a gas station at the Walmart along I-35E also collapsed.
Thunderstorm winds blew a one foot diameter tree onto a single family residence.  A two foot diameter tree was blown over onto FM 875.
A mobile storm spotter measured a 90 mph wind gust approximately 5 miles north of Waxahachie.
The automated weather station at Midway Regional Airport (KJWY) measured a 61 mph wind gust.
A mobile storm spotter estimated 75 mph thunderstorm winds approximately 2 miles south of Lancaster.
Thunderstorm winds caused carports to collapse and downed business signs and 1 foot diameter trees in Seagoville.
Thunderstorm winds downed large trees and power lines in Crandall.
Thunderstorm winds blew a roof off a single family home near Nike Dr. and Highway 205 north of Terrell.  Numerous large trees were also blown down.
A 63 mph thunderstorm wind gust was recorded at a school-net site in Crandall.

Thunderstorm winds produced widespread damage near Quinlan and across areas south of Greenville in Hunt County.  The strongest hit areas were along a line from near Cash to Lone Oak. Winds downed numerous trees, power lines and damaged several structures in these areas.
A large tree was blown through power lines by thunderstorm winds on Reservoir St. in Sulphur Springs. A utility pole near Mulberry Street and Middle Street was snapped in two.

A tornado began near County Road 1210 south of Pat Cleburne Lake and traveled approximately 1.5 miles to the east.  The first signs of damage were to a garage and a house that was shifted off its foundation.  Several trees were also blown down.  Near the end of its track, the tornado damaged 5 homes with one of the homes sustaining heavy damage.  This tornado has been rated an EF-1 with maximum estimated wind speeds of 100 to 110 mph.

There was a brief tornado touchdown in the city of Alvarado, just southwest of the intersection of Interstate 35W and Highway 67.  A mobile home was overturned resulting in 2 minor injuries.  The Equine Vet Building and 4 other commercial buildings sustained damage.  This tornado has been rated an EF-1 with estimated maximum wind speeds of 90 mph.

A tornado touched down north of Forney near the intersection of FM 740 and Lover's Lane.  This tornado was approximately 60 yards wide and remained on the ground along a half mile path.  Five homes suffered roof damage.  This tornado has been rated an EF-1 with maximum winds estimated at 100 to 105 mph.

A tornado touched down near the town of Cash and then moved northeast producing a non-continuous path of damage over 6 miles long.  Up to 8 homes, a pipe manufacturing plant and two metal buildings were damaged in Cash. In addition, four U-haul trailers were blown across the highway in Cash. As the tornado continued northeast out of Cash, it damaged several more homes with most of them sustaining minor roof damage. However, one home sustained significant damage to the roof and second story near FM 1564 and FM 3519. Just before the tornado lifted, it damaged 5 more mobile homes, one of which was destroyed, and also significantly damaged a single family residence near the intersection of FM 1564 and Highway 69.  This tornado has been rated an EF-1 with estimated maximum wind speeds of 100 to 110 mph.
Thunderstorm winds turned over RVs and trailers at Texas Motor Speedway. Signs, fencing, and flag poles were also damaged.

Golfball size hail pelted the city of Hamilton damaging roofs, siding, automobiles, and windows. The hail left holes in the siding of many homes. The windows at City Hall and the post office were broken by the hail.

Severe thunderstorm winds damaged barns, outbuildings, and trees across Hamilton County. Some trees were fully uprooted. The combination of severe winds and large hail damaged oat and wheat fields that were already suffering from the ongoing drought.
A tree fell on a home near Lanham. Extensive damage was done to the home, causing part of the roof to collapse. The side of the house was also pelted with hail leaving holes in the siding.
Trees were uprooted and roofs were damaged by straight-line winds in Terrell. A mobile home on Hwy 34 north of Terrell was rolled onto its side and one end collapsed.
Straight-line winds damaged trees and some outbuildings across the northern portions of Kaufman County.
Straight-line winds up to 95 mph damaged a church on Dewberry Blvd in Lancaster. Nearly the entire roof of the church was peeled off.

Several trees were knocked down across the county but the hardest hit area was along Hwy 19 north of Sulphur Springs. On either side of the highway, numerous trees were knocked down and many trees blocked roads. On CR 4769, a carport was blown across the road. The roof of an unoccupied trailer on CR 4591 was ripped off. A few trees were also knocked down across the southern half of the county.
Severel streets were barricaded due to high water in the Oaklawn neighborhood of Corsicana.
Flash flooding was reported 2 miles west of the town of Carson.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey concluded an EF-0 tornado initially touched down about 1 mile northwest of Honey Grove near the intersection of County Road 2781 and Highway 82. The tornado moved to the northeast and lifted near the intersection of County Road 2875 and Private Road 287. Several structures and trees were damaged along the path. Estimated winds were 85 mph.
A brief EF-0 tornado occurred with no damage approximately 2 miles north-northwest of Sidney.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 2 miles southeast of Bluff Dale in Erath County and continued to the east into Hood County. This tornado had a path length of approximately 2.5 miles and an estimated width of 150 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 85 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 2 miles southeast of Bluff Dale in Erath County and continued to the east into Hood County. This tornado had a path length of approximately 2.5 miles and an estimated width of 150 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 85 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 4.5 miles southwest of Tolar. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.5 miles and an estimated width of 25 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75-80 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 2.5 miles west-northwest of Rainbow. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.75 miles and an estimated width of 50 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75-80 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred north of Cleburne State Park. This tornado had a path length of approximately 2.5 miles and an estimated width of 400 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred 3 miles east-northeast of Cleburne State Park. This tornado had a path length of approximately 1 mile and an estimated width of 150 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred 2 miles south-southeast of Itasca. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.7 miles and an estimated width of 30 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75 mph. The tornado was described as small and rope-like.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began just west of Avalon and moved east into town. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.5 miles and an estimated width of 50 yards. An elementary school suffered partial roof loss and a residence also sustained minor damage to its roof. Winds were estimated at 80 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred approximately 3 miles northeast of Coolidge. This tornado had a path length of approximately 1.3 miles and an estimated width of 100 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 70 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred just west of Wortham. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.8 miles and an estimated width of 100 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred approximately 4 miles southwest of Fairfield.  This tornado had a path length of approximately 3.5 miles and an estimated width of 500 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado occurred approximately 1 mile east of Oakwood.  This tornado had a path length of approximately 1 mile and an estimated width of 100 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated at 75 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began on the northwest bank of Cedar Creek Reservoir and tracked northeast over the Cedar Creek Country Club and across Highway 175. This tornado had a path length of approximately 5 miles and an estimated width of 500 yards. Mostly tree damage occurred with this tornado, especially on three holes of the golf course. Winds were estimated at 85 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-1 tornado began approximately 2 miles south of Ben Wheeler and tracked northeast across Van Zandt County before continuing into Smith County. This tornado had a path length of approximately 7.5 miles in Van Zandt County and was estimated to be a 1/2 mile wide. A mobile home south of Ben Wheeler was rolled onto its side, and several homes were damaged 4 miles northeast of Ben Wheeler. The Friendly Center Baptist Church also sustained major damage. Wind speeds were estimated to be 100 MPH. A lady in the rolled mobile home sustained minor injuries.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began over Cedar Creek Reservoir and tracked east into Mabank. This tornado had a path length of approximately 5 miles and an estimated width of 400 yards. Buildings in Mabank sustained roof damage. Winds were estimated between 80 and 85 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 2 miles northeast of Purtis Creek State Park. This tornado had a path length of approximately 1 mile and an estimated width of 100 yards. Mainly tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated near 80 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 5.5 miles northeast of Corsicana. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.5 mile and an estimated width of 100 yards. Some tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated near 70 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-1 tornado occurred in Groesbeck. This tornado had a path length of approximately one mile and an estimated width of 75 yards. Tree and building damage was observed along the path, mainly in downtown Groesbeck. The Courthouse, the Dairy Queen, the Tire Shop, the Lord's Store House, and the Volunteer Fire Department sustained building damage.  An estimated 40 businesses sustained some type of damage, and the steeple of a baptist church was ripped off. Window damage to buildings and cars was caused by the winds and flying debris. Winds were estimated between 85 and 90 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 1.5 miles southwest of Personville. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.75 miles and an estimated width of 100 yards. Some tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated near 75 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 3.75 miles east-northeast of Elm Mott. This tornado had a path length of approximately a third of a mile and an estimated width of 50 yards. Some tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated near 75 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 2 miles north of Mart. This tornado had a path length of approximately 1.5 miles and an estimated width of 30 yards. Some tree damage occurred with this small rope tornado and winds were estimated near 75 mph.

A NWS Storm Survey determined an EF-0 tornado began approximately 4 miles south-southeast of Thornton. This tornado had a path length of approximately 0.75 miles and an estimated width of 100 yards. Some tree damage occurred with this tornado and winds were estimated near 75 mph.

Thunderstorm winds damaged the roofs of 3 single family homes and 2 mobile homes north of Venus.
Power poles and trees were knocked down in Godley.

The American Red Cross reported that 16 homes in Rio Vista were damaged by severe thunderstorm winds. Two of these homes were destroyed and three others sustained major damage. The roofs of six homes north of Rio Vista were torn off. Trees were also knocked down in the city, and the breezeway between city hall and the civic center sustained damage.
Large tree branches were knocked down in Denton. At least one large branch landed on the roof of a house.
A 22 year-old male was struck by lightning while working outdoors in Star Harbor. It is believed that lightning struck the tree next to him.
Trees were knocked down on CRs 3511 and 3504. A barn in the area was also destroyed.
A barn in the Pickton-Pine Forest area lost its metal roof.
Part of a large tree was snapped on Ann Drive in Ennis.

The roof of a wood storage shed at the Columbia Manufacturing plant was ripped off by high winds, likely from the RFD of a supercell. Tree damage and uprooted trees were also reported along South Highway 287 in the same area.
A vehicle driving south on Highway 14 near Thornton hydroplanned and crashed resulting in one fatality and one injury.
The COOP Observer from Frisco reported 1.5 hail in the northwestern portions of the city. Minor tree damage was noted due to the hail.
Golfball to baseball sized hail was reported in Cleburne for nearly 15 minutes by several sources including spotters, broadcast media, and a local COOP Observer.
Half dollar sized hail fell approximately 6 miles southeast of Cleburne.
Golfball sized hail fell in Parker, which is approximately 5 miles east of Rio Vista.
A storm chaser observed tennis ball sized hail just west of  Itasca.
A storm chaser observed tea cup sized hail, which is about the size of an orange, approximately 5 miles north-northwest of Hillsboro.
Golfball sized hail fell 1 mile north of Carl's Corner, which is approximately 8 miles northeast of Hillsboro.
Quarter to golfball sized hail fell in Klondike, which is approximately 4 miles southwest of Cooper.
Sporadic tree damage was reported across Freestone County from several thunderstorms that moved across the county.
Strong winds ripped the roof off the Bridgeport High School gym.
A grass fire, fanned by strong winds gusting up to 50 mph, destroyed a 100 year-old, two-story home northeast of Decatur.
A mobile storm spotter estimated 75 mph thunderstorm winds approximately 2 miles south of Lancaster.
Significant tree damage occurred along Sawsawi Trail in Desoto. Several large tree limbs were broken off and other large trees were snapped or uprooted.

Severe thunderstorm winds uprooted and snapped trees and tree limbs across Lamar County. Power poles were also snapped, and the giant steer at Sirloin Stockade on NE Loop 286 in Paris was blown off its trailer moorings and tossed across the parking lot.
The COOP Observer in Itasca reported hail stones up to 3.5 inches in diameter.

Severe thunderstorm winds, likely from the RFD of a supercell, caused damage about a mile east of DeLeon along Highway 6. Tree limbs were snapped, the metal roof of a building was partially peeled back, and light poles at a baseball field were snapped or knocked down.
A house between Commerce and Campbell was struck by lightning and ignited a small fire. The rain put the fire out and damage was limited to television equipment.
Dime sized hail was reported at Lois Lane and I-35N, north of Sanger.
Dime sized hail was reported 1 mile east of Bolivar.
A trained spotter estimated 60 mph winds near Lewisville.
Golfball sized hail fell in Garland.
A trained spotter reported penny sized hail just east of Rowlett.
A trained spotter reported penny sized hail just east of Rowlett.

Nearly 100 homes and several outbuildings were damaged across mainly the southern half of Van Zandt County from two strong supercells. These homes were damaged by either a tornado in the same region, damaging downburst winds, and/or RFD winds. It cannot be determined how many of the homes were damaged by the tornado and how many by the RFD or downburst winds. In addition, numerous trees were also knocked down and several were blocking roadways. Power lines were also down as well.
A trailer house was damaged along FM 744 south of Blooming Grove. The roof was torn off the home. The damage was likely caused by the RFD of a supercell.
Penny sized hail was reported 2 miles southwest of Vineyard.
Nickel sized hail was reported 1 mile east of Graham.
Quarter sized hail was reported just west of Jacksboro on Highway 380.
Quarter sized hail was reported 2 miles northwest of Jacksboro near Highway 280.
Quarter sized hail was reported 2 miles east of Postoak in the far northern part of the county.
Baseball sized hail was reported 1 mile south of Mineral Wells.

Golfball sized hail fell near Salt Creek Road and Highway 199 in southern Wise County.
Penny sized hail fell in the Sendera Ranch neighborhood just west of Haslet.
Sixty MPH winds were estimated with a thunderstorm in Ringgold. No damage was reported.
Penny sized hail was reported by a NWS meteorologist in far north Keller.
Quarter sized hail was reported south of Muenster.
Golfball sized hail was reported 4 miles west of Keller.
Seventy MPH winds were estimated in Era which is between Valley View and Rosston.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported in the southern portions of Euless by a NWS meteorologist.
Golfball to baseball sized hail was reported about 2 miles north of Springtown.
Half dollar sized hail was reported 1 mile southwest of Lindsay.
Hail stones up to 2 in diameter fell in the Sendera Ranch neighborhood just west of Haslet.
Grapefruit sized hail was reported 1 mile north of Sanctuary.
Trees were blown down and shingles were blown off the roofs of an apartment complex on Boat Club Road near Lake Worth.
Quarter to golfball sized hail fell in North Richland Hills. Cars were dented by the hail.
Nickel sized hail was reported 3 miles southwest of Keller.
Tennis ball sized hail fell 1 mile west of Keller.
Hail fell for several minutes in Avondale. The hail began as nickel sized but progressively grew to softball sized hail.
Golfball sized hail fell at the intersection of Highway 114 and North MacArthur Blvd in Irving.
A house was damaged by thunderstorm winds in Saginaw. Shingles were also damaged in the city and several trees were either knocked down or uprooted.

Golfball sized hail fell for several minutes in Grapevine.  The hail damaged many cars parked outside at DFW International Airport. In addition, about 50 American Airlines airplanes and three other large planes were damaged by the hail.

Seventy to seventy-five MPH winds were estimated along and just north of Loop 820 from Highway 377/Denton Highway to near Holiday Lane. These strong winds damaged several business signs and the roof of a commercial building at Loop 820 and Rufe Snow Drive. Several large trees and power poles were also knocked down along Rufe Snow Drive north of Loop 820. In the neighborhood around Richland Hills High School, many large tree limbs were broken, a few power poles were leaning about 20 degrees, and some trees were either split or knocked down. One tree fell on a house and damaged the roof.
A 67 MPH wind gust was measured at the National Weather Service Office.
Tennis ball sized hail was reported in west Keller between Highway 170 and Golden Triangle Blvd.
Golfball sized hail fell near Highways 183 and 121 in Bedford.

Hail up to the size of grapefruits was reported around Irving for several minutes. Windows were broken or smashed out by the hail. The hail also damaged the TPC Four Seasons Las Colinas Country Club and golf course where the PGA's Byron Nelson Golf Championship was being held. Crews had to repair over 4,000 divots on the golf course before play could resume the next day. The greens of seven holes were significantly damaged. The hail at the golf course was reported to be up to baseball size.
Softball sized hail was reported on the northwest side of Keller.
Seventy MPH winds were estimated in the northwest side of Keller.
Seventy MPH winds were estimated on the east side of Fort Worth. Two large trees were blown down, and they fell on the roof of a house.

Golfball sized hail was reported at Highway 183 and Mockingbird Lane in northwest Dallas. The hail also impacted operations at nearby Dallas Love Field Airport (KDAL) where 8 Southwest planes were damaged.
Nickel sized hail was reported at FM 3902 and FM 678 on the east side of Gainesville.
Seventy to eighty MPH winds were estimated 2 miles north of Valley View.
Golfball sized hail was reported 3 miles southwest of Whitesboro near the Grayson/Cooke County line.

Baseball sized hail was reported a mile south of Fort Worth.
Golfball sized hail was reported at Interstate 30 and Beach Street on the east side of Fort Worth.
