About 1-4 of snow fell across Wise County on Christmas Day. The snow resulted in slick roads that caused a few accidents with injuries in the county. A pickup truck rolled near Highway 287 and FM 407, and one person was transported to the hospital. Another accident with injuries occurred on FM 51 near Slidell. Several other accidents were reported in the county but no other injuries were reported. The hazardous road conditions continued into the night as temperatures dropped into the lower 20s.

The tops of several utility poles caught fire in McLennan County when fog combined with dust that had accumulated on the insulators of the utility poles ignited the tops of the poles on fire. The phenomenon is referred to by experts as tracking. Utility poles that were on fire in McLennan County included 2 in the Waco area, a few near Lorena, and a few west of Waco along US Highway 84.

The tops of several utility poles caught fire in Hill County when fog combined with dust that had accumulated on the insulators of the utility poles ignited the tops of the poles on fire. The phenomenon is referred to by experts as tracking. Utility poles that were on fire in Hill County included nearly 30 poles along I-35 south of Hillsboro, another 20 poles near Bynum, and a few more in the Aquilla area.

The tops of a few utility poles caught fire in Falls County when fog combined with dust that had accumulated on the insulators of the utility poles ignited the tops of the poles on fire. The phenomenon is referred to by experts as tracking. Utility poles that were on fire in Falls County included a few poles along Highway 6 near 112 and 113, and some poles near Perry. The fires forced the closure of Highway 6 and stopped a train.

The tops of a few utility poles caught fire in Bell County when fog combined with dust that had accumulated on the insulators of the utility poles ignited the tops of the poles on fire. The phenomenon is referred to by experts as tracking. Utility poles that were on fire in Bell County were along I-35 north of Troy.
Strong northwest winds behind a cold front blew down a few trees in the county. One tree in Athens was blocking part of Clifford Street. Some power lines were also knocked down by the strong winds.

The 30-foot Christmas tree outside the police station in Greenville was knocked over by strong thunderstorm winds. The tree was not replaced. At least one other tree was knocked down in Greenville. The nearest automated weather station at Major Field Municipal Airport (KGVT) reported 43 mph winds with the storms.

Two homeless people in the city of Dallas died from hypothermia as temperatures plunged into the lower 20s and wind chills fell into the teens. A 50-year old woman and a 60-year old man were found in different locations of the city, but both were found outside.

Strong thunderstorm winds rolled a mobile home onto its top in the community of Copeville. No one was home at the time of the incident. Other substantial wind damage was reported in Copeville including the exterior metal roof of another mobile home was also peeled off. Outbuildings, sheds, playground equipment, trees, and fences were also damaged in the community.

Montague County began the month of February with extreme drought conditions in place county-wide. Beneficial rain during the second half of the month allowed conditions to improve some, however, the drought was still classified as extreme by the U.S. Drought Monitor over the southern half of the county  at the end of the month.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, extreme drought conditions were in place across Cooke County at the beginning of February. Conditions improved some during the second half of the month due to modest rainfall amounts. However, conditions were still severe across most of the county with a few areas remaining in the extreme category at the month's end.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, drought conditions were predominately in the severe category across Grayson County, with areas over the far western portions of the county experiencing extreme drought throughout the month.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Severe drought conditions were in place across Fannin County at the beginning of February and persisted through the end of the month.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Severe drought conditions were in place across Lamar County at the beginning of February and persisted through the end of the month.
Severe drought conditions during the first half of February improved to moderate drought midway through the month. Drought conditions remained in the moderate category through the end of February.

Young County experienced the most severe drought conditions of all 46 north Texas counties, reaching the exceptional drought category across the western half of the county for the entire month. Otherwise, extreme drought conditions were in place across the rest of the county.
Jack County was generally split between extreme drought conditions across the northwest half of the county, and severe drought conditions across the southeast half, for the month of February.
Extreme drought conditions affected only the far northern reaches of Wise county during the month of February. Otherwise, drought conditions remained in the severe category.

Denton County spent all of the month of February in the grip of a severe drought. The exception was over the northern and northwestern-most portions of the county, where drought conditions were extreme for a good part of the month.

The severe drought that was in place across Collin County at the beginning of the month improved to moderate drought across the southern half of the county by February 12. The severe drought remained in place across the northern third of the county for the rest of the month, with moderate drought conditions remaining elsewhere.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Hunt County began the month of February with ongoing severe drought conditions in place. Conditions improved to moderate drought by the middle of February and remained as such through the end of the month.

Severe drought over the western third of Hopkins County at the beginning of February improved to moderate drought by the end of week two, and remained as such through the end of the month. The rest of Hopkins County was classified as moderate drought for the whole month.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Stephens County was in an extreme drought at the beginning of February, and remained as such through the entire month.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, severe drought conditions were in place the entire month over all but the far southeastern portions of the county.
Severe drought conditions in place at the beginning of February improved during week 2, becoming categorized as moderate by February 12 and remaining as such through the end of the month.

Severe drought conditions in place at the beginning of February improved to moderate over all but the far southern portions of the county by February 12. Severe and extreme drought remained in place just north of the Tarrant/Johnson County line through the end of the month.
Severe/D2 drought conditions at the beginning of the month improved to moderate by February 12, and remained as such through the end of the month.

Quarter sized hail was reported in Rising Star.
Pea to nickel sized hail was reported in Mineral Wells.
Sixty MPH winds were estimated in Weatherford.
Sixty MPH winds were estimated at Longhorn Rd and North Main Street in Saginaw. A basketball goal was knocked over in town.
A 64 MPH wind gust was reported at Huffines Blvd and 10 Mile Bridge Road near Marine Creek Lake in northwest Fort Worth.
Two business signs and two port-o-johns were knocked over in White Settlement. The nearby automated weather station at Carswell AFB (KNFW) reported a peak wind of 43 mph around the same time.
The automated weather station at Waco's Madison Cooper Airport (KACT) measured a 63 MPH wind gust. This wind gust occurred from nearby light rain helping to drag strong winds aloft to the ground.
A 66 MPH wind gust was reported at Nolan Catholic High School in Fort Worth.
Strong thunderstorm winds moved a hay ring on property that was located between south Sherman and north Howe. In addition, trees were knocked down onto fences.

Straight line winds estimated at 85-95 mph damaged several homes and uprooted several trees in the Luella area. The damage stretched for approximately 6 miles and occurred in conjunction with a bookend vortex on the north side of a bow echo. A home on Tribble and another home on Bois D'Arc suffered major damage. Most of the roof of the home on Bois D'Arc was torn off and much of the second story of the home on Tribble was destroyed. Another 3 homes suffered roof damage.
Sixty MPH winds were estimated in west Plano. Power poles were also knocked down on Midway Road north of Plano Parkway.
Nickel sized hail was reported on the southwest side of Temple near Loop 363 and 57th Street.
A telephone pole was snapped in half on the southwest side of Temple. Sixty-five MPH winds were also estimated in the same area near Loop 363 and 57th Street.
Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 65 MPH were estimated in the Duncanville and Mountain Creek Lake area. Large tree branches were knocked down and shingles were torn off roofs.
Sixty-five MPH winds were estimated between Richardson and Addison.
Sixty-five MPH winds were estimated at North Central Expressway/Highway 75 and Northwest Highway/Loop 12 in University Park.
Penny sized hail was reported in Palestine.
Severe/D2 drought conditions in place across most of Rains County at the beginning of February improved to D1/ moderate by the middle of the month.
Lightning struck the Main Street Presbyterian Church in Honey Grove and the church burned to the ground. The church had been built in 1902.
A bait shop and the roof of a restaurant at Eagle Mountain Lake were damaged by high thunderstorm winds.
A house was destroyed by lightning in the 6000 block of Lakecrest Drive in Sachse.

Strong thunderstorm winds impacted the Western Hills area of Temple where several large trees were uprooted, fences were knocked over, and at least one street sign was bent over. Much of the tree damage was reported along West Adams Ave, Apache Dr, and Blackfoot Drive. One tree fell on a home in the Whispering Oaks subdivision. The awning and part of the roof of 4 units at the Brentwood Apartments on West Adams Avenue was peeled off. A few large satellite dishes were knocked over on Moody Lane. Business signs at the Quick Shop & Go on Olaf and the New Hope Community Church on Apache Drive were damaged.
A few boat docks were damaged at Frank's Marina on Lake Belton. Shore moorings were uprooted and underwater anchorages were sheared off.
Hail up to the size of dimes was reported in the Duncanville and Mountain Creek Lake area.
For all of February, Eastland County experienced extreme/D3 drought conditions over the northwestern quarter of the county with severe/D2 drought conditions elsewhere.

Severe/D2 drought conditions plagued most of Erath County during the entire month of February. The far southern portions of the county were even classified in the extreme/D3 category for the whole month.

Severe drought/D2 conditions in place county-wide at the beginning of February had retreated and improved to moderate across the northern half of the county by the second week. The county remained split between severe drought to the south and moderate drought to the north for the rest of the month.
Extreme/D3 conditions were in place over all of Somervell County at the beginning of February, and remained in place through the end of the month.

High winds tore most of the metal roof off a metal shop building on Gerald Lane in Elm Mott. Some items inside the shop were damaged. These strong winds occurred from nearby light rain helping to drag strong winds aloft to the ground.

Johnson County began the month of February with extreme/D3 conditions over the western two-thirds of the county, and severe/D2 conditions over the eastern third of the county. These conditions remained in place through the end of the month.
Severe/D2 drought conditions were felt over only the far western reaches of the county, with moderate/D1 conditions elsewhere, during the entire month of February 2013.
Severe/D2 drought conditions were in place county-wide at the beginning of February, and remained in place through the end of the month.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, extreme/D3 drought conditions were in place across all of Bosque County for the entire month of February.

Hill County began the month of February 2013 with extreme/D3 conditions over the western third of the county, and D2/severe drought conditions across the rest of the county. By the second week in February, the eastern third of the county improved to moderate/D1 drought. That left the central third of the county in severe/D2 drought, and the western third in D3/extreme drought; and these conditions continued through the end of the month.

Severe/D2 drought plagued only the southwestern quarter of the county during the first week of the month. By week 2, all of the couty had improved to D1 status or better, with the improved conditions persisting through the end of the month.

Mills County began February with severe/D2 drought conditions county-wide. Around the middle of the month, the southern half of the county had deteriorated to extreme/D3 drought status, with severe drought remaining across the northern half. These conditions persisted through the end of the month.
Pea to dime sized hail was reported in Faught.
Severe/D2 drought conditions plagued Hamilton County for the entire month of February, with a few areas on the extreme east and southeast portions of the county reaching extreme/D3 levels.

Strong and gusty south winds caused damage in Bell County, especially in the Killeen area. During the afternoon hours, the winds were gusting over 50 mph at times. The strongest measured wind gust was 54 mph at the Killeen/Fort Hood Regional Airport (KGRK). Many tree limbs were broken with several limbs knocking down power lines and causing power outages. Up to 5500 customers in the county were without power at some point. At least two tree limbs fell on cars. Fences were blown down, some windows were broken by flying debris, and a few sheds were also knocked over by the strong winds. Shingles and roofs were also damaged by the strong winds. One TV station reported the roof of a hangar partially collapsed at Fort Hood. In addition, the strong winds hampered fire fighting efforts at a few structure fires.

Severe/D2 conditions in place at the beginning of the month improved to D1/moderate drought over all but the western third of the county by week 2. Conditions then remained as such thorugh the end of the month.

Extreme/D3 drought plagued the northwestern two-thirds of Coryell County, while D2 conditions were prominent over the southeastern third of the county. These conditions were in place for the entire month.

Severe/D2 drought over the northern third of Limestone County at the beginning of February improved to moderate/D1 during the second week of the month. These improved conditions lasted for the rest of the month.

A homeless man built a campfire between a home and a church on West Seminary Drive in Fort Worth. After he had fallen asleep, strong winds whipped the campfire out of control. The fire burned the homeless man on his feet and legs, burned an exterior wall of the home, and a nearby pickup truck. Automated weather stations around the area were reporting sustained winds around 25 mph with gusts as high as 37 mph at about the time the fire was reported.

National Weather Service crews surveyed the damage from the Granbury tornado. The tornado first occurred on the west bank of Lake Granbury / Brazos River. The tornado crossed the lake heading east, towards Davis Road. On the east side of the lake, the tornado damaged several power lines and trees, before hitting the American Legion hall on Davis Road. ||The tornado then took much more of a northerly track through the Rancho Brazos subdivision. This subdivision was severely damaged, with 97 of the 110 homes suffering at least minor damage. Four homes suffered EF-4 damage, and ten others had EF-3 damage. The vast majority of the subdivision had evidence of EF-1 or EF-2 damage. Six individuals lost their lives in this subdivision as a direct result of the tornado. All six were in mobile homes at the time. ||Moving north from the Rancho Brazos subdivision, the tornado dissipated approximately one mile to the north-northeast of the area that suffered the most damage.

The exception was during the first week of the month when the southwestern corner of the county was briefly classified as Moderate/D1 drought severity.

Severe/D2 drought conditions which were in place over the northern third of Parker County at the beginning of May expanded to encompass the entire county by May 14. Severe/D2 drought remained in place over the entire county through the end of the month.

Severe/d2 drought conditions which were in place over the northern third of Parker County at the beginning of May expanded to encompass the entire county by May 14. Severe/d2 drought remained in place over the entire county through the end of the month.

Tarrant County began May with only the northwestern corner of the county experiencing Severe /D2 drought. By May 14, the drought expended to include roughly the western half of the county, with Moderate/D1 conditions over the eastern half. These conditions continued through the end of the month.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Eastland County spent the entire month of May 2013 in Severe/D2 drought.

Severe/D2 drought conditions were present over only the southern fourth of the county at the beginning of May, with Moderate/D1 drought across the rest of the county. By May 14, the Severe/D2 drought conditions had spread across all of Erath County and remained in place through the end of the month.

D2/Severe drought conditions over extreme southern portions of Hood County at the beginning of May spread northward across the rest of the county by the middle of the month. Severe/D2 drought then remained in placed across Hood County through the end of the month.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Severe/D2 drought conditions covered all of Somervell County for the entire month of May 2013.

Severe/D2 drought over the far western reaches of Johnson County at the beginning of May spread east to cover all of the county by May 14th. Severe/D2 conditions remained in place over all but the extreme eastern portions of Johnson County, where D1/Moderate drought returned, through the end of the month.

Severe/D2 drought conditions covered the majority of Comanche County in May 2013. The exceptions were the small northeast corner of the county, which fell under Moderate/D1 severity during the first half of the month; and the southern third of the county, which was upgraded from Severe/D2 to Moderate/D1 severity during the second half of the month.

Severe/D2 conditions covered all of Hamilton County during the first half of May. Approximately 3 inches of rain occurred during the third week across much of the area, which led to an upgrade to Moderate/D1 conditions over the western half of the county by May 21. The county remained split between Severe/D2 conditions over the eastern half and Moderate/D1 conditions over the western half through the end of the month.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Severe/D2 drought conditions covered Bosque County for all of May 2013.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Severe/D2 drought conditions occurred over roughly the western half of Hill County for all of May 2013.

Severe/D2 drought conditions covered Mills County for the first half of May 2013. Beneficial rains from thunderstorms during the middle of the month led to improvement to Moderate/D1 conditions over all but the far southern portions of the county during the second half of May.

Severe/D2 drought conditions across the western half of McLennan County during the first half of May improved during the second half of the month; due to over 3 inches of rain occurring during this period. By the end of the month, conditions had improved to Moderate/D1 severity over all but the extreme western tip of the county.

Severe/D2 drought covered the majority of Limestone County during the first half of May. Conditions improved to Moderate/D1 over the northern half of the county during the second half of the month, due to beneficial rains, with Severe/D2 continuing across the southern half of the county through the end of the month.

Severe/D2 drought conditions covered all but the extreme northern portions of Freestone County during all of May. Extreme/D3 conditions briefly surfaced across the southern third of the county during the second week of the month. Fortunately, convective weather around the middle of May ended the brief run of D3 severity.

Extreme/ D3 drought conditions covered most of Lampasas County at the beginning of May. Conditions were upgraded to Severe/D2 during the second week of  May, and remained as such through the end of the month.

The western two-thirds of Coryell County began May of 2013 in Extreme/D3 drought, with the eastern third classified under Severe/D2 status. The areas under D3 severity were upgraded to D2 by the second week of the month. Severe/D2 drought remained over all but the northwestern corner of the county, where conditions had improved to D1/Moderate severity by the end of the month.

Severe/D2 drought conditions covered all of Bell County for approximately the first half of May 2013. Conditions were upgraded to Moderate/D1 over the eastern half of the county during third week of the month, splitting the county into severe drought over the western half and moderate over the east for the second half of the month.

Drought conditions were classified as Severe/D2 across all of Falls County during the first half of May, 2013, according to the U.S. Drought Monitor. Conditions were upgraded to Moderate/D1 by May 21, and remained as such through the end of the month.

Severe/D2 conditions covered all of Milam County at the beginning of May, 2013. Conditions improved slowly but steadily from northeast to southwest across the county during the month, and all of Milam county had improved to D1/Moderate drought by the final week of May.

Severe/D2 drought conditions at the beginning of May improved to Moderate/D1 by the middle of the month over all but the northern tip of the county. Conditions remained as such through the end of the month.

Extreme/D3 conditions in place over the vast majority of Leon County during the first half of May were upgraded to Severe/D2 status around the middle of the month. Conditions improved further to D1/Moderate severity over the southern third of the county by the end of the month, with severe drought continuing over the rest of the area.

D2/severe drought conditions developed over Hunt County by the 14th of May. Beneficial rains during the second half of the month allowed conditions to improve to d1/moderate severity by May 28, with these conditions continuing through the end of the month.
Several 3 inch diameter tree limbs, about 10 feet long, were blown down on the northwest side of Breckenridge.
The automated weather station at Bowie Municipal Airport (K0F2) measured a 62 mph wind gust.
Strong thunderstorm winds blew down several small trees and fences. These winds were likely from the outflow boundary.
Golf ball sized hail was reported on Highway 67 just south of Ivan.
A tree was uprooted 6 miles south of Breckenridge.
Several tree branches were blown down by thunderstorm winds. Several power lines were affected, causing a power loss to several homes in Grand Prairie.
Several trees and power lines were blown down by thunderstorm winds. The Henderson County Sheriff's Office report showed 16 calls of trees down across the city of Athens and across the county.
Skylights and roofs were damaged at Acton Middle School, northwest of downtown Acton. A tennis court fence, wind screen, and portable bleachers were damaged as well.
Lometa Volunteer Fire Department fought and contained a 74 acre brush fire on Monday and Tuesday May 13-14. Ranch land was burned, but no structures caught fire.
Palo Pinto Volunteer Fire Department, and the Texas A&M Forest Service fought a 39 acre wildfire near Possum Kingdom Lake. Thirty homes were evacuated, but no structures were damaged in the fire.

The Denton County Fire marshal reported a house in the 9300 block of Blanco Drive caught fire after lightning struck the roof. The house was severely damaged, causing the home to be temporarily uninhabitable. Due to the fire, the roof is completely gone and the first floor suffered water damage. The siding of a neighboring house was damaged by the heat of the fire.
The Young County Emergency Manager reported lightning struck a tank battery, resulting in a fire. No other structures were impacted.

Several fires were started by lightning on the afternoon of May 21st. Two houses suffered fire damage after lightning struck their roof. Another lightning strike destroyed a battery of oil tanks near County Road 208.

The Cooke County Emergency Manager and a Cooke County Commissioner reported several large trees were blown down. The tree damage was concentrated in the southern third of the county, along or near County Roads 337, 328 and 348. One mobile home in the same area suffered severe damage.

The Hunt County Emergency Manager reported power lines and tree limbs blown down throughout the county. Homes in the Royse City and Caddo Mills areas suffered roof and fence damage. Two barns along County Road 2630 were also damaged by the winds.

A one year old child died on May 17th after being left in a car on the parking lot of an elementary school. Temperatures on the 17th only reached the lower 90s in the city of Dallas. However, heat was determined to be the cause of death.

Six house were struck by lightning in Keller. Four of the homes took direct strikes, and only two homes caught on fire. A home on Bourland Road suffered major roof damage from a lightning strike. Other strikes also occurred on Richmond Drive, Edgewood Drive and Lismore Court.

Water was reported up to the hood of cars approximately 2 miles west of Rockdale on US 79. Multiple streets in Rockdale were flooded, and the local newspaper reported extensive flooding at the intersections of US 79 and Childress, Meadow, and Calhoun streets. The worst flooding was at US 79 and Meadow Rd where four inches of water entered a restaurant and moved a large outside cooler about 40 yards. A trash dumpster near the restaurant was also moved. FM 908 & 487 were briefly closed during the event. In addition, a portion of Cypress Trail Loop on the western side of Rockdale was washed out.
A foot of water was flowing over a roadway near Interstate 35 and State Highway 84 in Bellmead.

Four people had to be rescued in southeast Arlington when Bowman Branch Creek overflowed its banks and trapped their cars. The incidents happened near the intersection of Webb Ferrell Road and Hanrahan Ave. One car was swept off the road, and its two occupants were rescued from the nearby trees. The other car stalled in the high water and the two occupants were rescued from the roof of the car. The creek rose after 4-5 inches of rain fell in a 12 hour period with most of the rain falling during the few hours before the cars were trapped. The water was 4-5 feet deep where the cars were stalled.
A trained spotter southwest of Rockdale reported 7.69 inches of rain between 11 PM - 1 AM. The spotter also reported that creeks in the area were out of their banks.
Several creeks remained swollen out of their banks and several roads remained impassable in and around Rockdale after nearly 8 inches of rain fell over the town in a few short hours.
Near tennis ball sized hail was reported in Eastland.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported 5 miles north of Rising Star.
Quarter sized hail was reported 5 miles north of St Jo.
Quarter sized hail was reported at Lake Proctor.
Half dollar sized hail was covering the ground in Proctor.
A spotter reported half dollar sized hail north of Jacksboro.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported 2 miles west of Runaway Bay.
Quarter sized hail was reported just south of Rhome.
Quarter sized hail was reported 5 miles west of Haslet.
Half dollar sized hail was reported south of Haslet.
Quarter sized hail was reported 1 mile north of McGregor.
Golf ball sized hail was reported 2 miles south of Haslet on FM 156.
Quarter sized hail was reported in the Sendera Ranch neighborhood.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Keller. The hail was driven by estimated 60 mph winds, causing damage to roofs and fences. Several roofs in the area needed to be at least partially replaced.
NWS employee reports hail up to 1 near the intersection of Beach Street and Shiver Road.
Golf ball sized hail was covering the ground near Eagle Mountain Lake.
Hail up to the size of golf balls was covering the ground in Southlake.
Quarter sized hail was reported near the McGregor Municipal Airport.
Multiple trees were uprooted in Belton including a very large live oak.
Multiple trees were blown down across the county.

Several cars were stalled in high water on Trinity Blvd in Hurst, behind the Bell Helicopter facility. In addition, several cars were also stalled in high water in the construction area near Northeast Mall.
Seven inches of water was reported over Interstate 35W at North Loop 820.

A 31-year old male was struck by lightning at the Rednecks with Paychecks event. The lightning struck the tree he was taking cover under and entered his body through his boot. He survived without serious injury.
Three power poles were downed near Clifton High School.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees near CR 317 and CR 314 in the Jewett area.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees in the Hilltop Lakes area.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees on Blackjack Street in Jewett.

A landspout occurred near the southwest shore of Lake Ray Roberts, east of Sanger. The landspout did not cause any damage and was observed for 5-6 minutes. It formed from a thunderstorm that developed along a cold front moving through the region.
Cooke County was evenly split between moderate/D1 drought over the western half and Severe/D2 drought over the eastern half during September 2013.
Severe/D2 drought conditions covered all of Grayson County during September 2013.
Severe/D2 drought conditions covered all of Fannin County during September 2013.
Despite receiving around 3 inches of rain, Lamar County was classified as being in Extreme/D3 drought through the whole month of September 2013.
Thunderstorm winds estimated at 60 mph were reported in Keller. The winds blew down several large sections of fences.

Extreme/D3 drought conditions covered most of Young County during the first half of September 2013. The September 19 rain event allowed for an upgrade to Severe/D2 conditions on the 9/24 outlook, and these conditions remained in place through the end of the month.

For the first, second and third weeks in September 2013: Extreme/D3 conditions were felt over the southwestern corner of Jack County with Severe/D2 conditions across the rest of the county. ||For the final week of the month: Conditions were classified as Severe/D2 county-wide.
Severe/D2 drought conditions were felt over all of Wise County for all of September 2013.

According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Severe/D2 drought conditions were felt over all of Denton County for all of September 2013. Conditions were even downgraded to Extreme/D3 over the southeastern third of the county for a week during the middle of the month. The 9/19 rain led to the removal of this small Extreme/D3 region.

Severe/D2 conditions covered Collin County during the first and final weeks of September 2013. Conditions were downgraded to Extreme/D3 for roughly 10 days during the middle of the month before the 9/19 rains allowed for the removal of the Extreme classification.

Extreme/D3 conditions covered most of Hunt County up until the 9/19 rain event. This rain prompted the removal of the extreme wording, leaving Severe/D2 conditions across the county for the last week and a half of the month.

Extreme/D3 conditions covered Delta County up until the 9/19 rains. This rain event prompted the removal of the extreme classification, leaving Severe/D2 conditions in place through the end of the month.

Extreme/D3 conditions over the western half of Hopkins County at the beginning of September were expanded to include all of the county by September 17. These conditions were downgraded to Severe/D2 following the 9/19 rain event. D2 conditions remained in place through the end of the month.
Rains County spent the first and last weeks of September in Severe/D2 drought while the middle weeks were spent in Extreme/D3.

For Stephens County, Severe/D2 conditions covered the northern half and Extreme/D3 covered the southern half of the county up until the rain event on 9/19. After this rain, all of Stephens County was classified under Severe/D2 drought through the end of the month.

Palo Pinto County County was split between Extreme/D3 conditions over the western half and Severe/D2 conditions over the eastern half of the county up until the 9/19 rain event. After these rains, extreme drought was removed, leaving all of the county in Severe/D2 drought through the end of the month.

Parker County spent all of September 2013 in Severe/D2 drought. The exception was during week 3 when Extreme/D3 conditions reached the southeastern corner of the county; only to be removed after the 9/19 rainfall event.
Severe/D2 drought conditions over Tarrant County were downgraded to Extreme/D3 on Sept 17, only to be upgraded back to Severe/D2 by September 24 following the 9/19 rainfall event.
Severe/D2 drought conditions over Dallas County were downgraded to Extreme/D3 on Sept 17, only to be upgraded back to Severe/D2 by September 24 following the 9/19 rainfall event.
Severe/D2 drought conditions over Rockwall County were downgraded to Extreme/D3 on Sept 17, only to be upgraded back to Severe/D2 by September 24 following the 9/19 rainfall event.
Severe/D2 drought conditions in place across Eastland County were upgraded to Moderate/D1 over all but the far northern reaches of the county during the last week of the month.

Erath County began September with Severe/D2 drought conditions in place county-wide. A downgrade to Extreme/D3 conditions was done on September 10th over the southeastern fourth of the county. These conditions were removed after the September 19th rain event, and Severe/D2 conditions were again the norm from the 24th through the end of the month, with a few spots even reaching Moderate/D1 status.

Severe/D2 drought conditions at the beginning of September deteriorated to Extreme/D3 around the middle of the month. Conditions improved to Severe/D2 again by the 24th following widespread rainfall that week, and remained as such through the end of the month.

Severe/D2 drought conditions at the beginning of September 2010 deteriorated to Extreme/D3 by the 10th. Rainfall during the second half of the month brought relief to the county, and conditions had improved back to Severe/D2 by September 24.

Severe/D2 conditions at the beginning of September 2013 deteriorated to Extreme/D3 by the 10th of the month. Rainfall on 9/19 brought some relief to the region...prompting the removal of the Extreme/D3 wording and placing all of the county in Severe/D2 conditions by September 24. These conditions continued through the end of the month.

Ellis County began September with Extreme/D3 conditions over the southern quarter of the county and Severe/D2 conditions elsewhere. By September 10, Extreme/D3 conditions had spread county-wide. Rainfall on 9/19 brought relief to the area, and conditions were upgraded back to Severe/D2 by the 24th. These conditions remained in place through the end of the month.

Severe/D2 drought conditions over Kaufman County at the beginning of September were downgraded to Extreme/D3 by September 10th. Beneficial rains around 9/19 allowed conditions to be upgraded to Severe/D2 by September 24th, and these conditions remained in place through the end of the month.

Severe/D2 drought conditions over Van Zandt County at the beginning of September were downgraded to Extreme/D3 by September 17th. Rainfall around 9/19 brought some relief to the county, allowing for the return of Severe/D2 conditions by September 24th.

Severe/D2 drought over the northern tip of Comanche County at the beginning of September expanded to cover all of the county by the 10th of the month. Conditions were upgraded to Moderate/D1 by September 24 due to rainfall received during the preceding week.

Severe/D2 drought over the southern tip of Hamilton County at the beginning of September expanded to cover all of the county by the 10th of the month. Conditions were upgraded to Moderate/D1 by September 24 due to rainfall received during the preceding week.

Severe/D2 drought over the southern half of Mills County at the beginning of September expanded to cover all of the county by the 10th of the month. Conditions were upgraded to Moderate/D1 by September 24 due to rainfall received during the preceding week.
Severe/D2 drought conditions were in place county-wide until September 24, when an upgrade to Moderate/D1 drought transpired due to beneficial rains received during the preceding week.

Severe/D2 drought conditions were in place county-wide until September 24, when an upgrade to Moderate/D1 drought transpired due to beneficial rains received during the preceding week.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, Milam County experienced Severe/D2 drought conditions during all of September 2013.

Severe/D2 conditions covered all of  Bosque County at the beginning and at the end of September. During the middle weeks of the month, western Bosque County was characterized as Severe/D2 drought, while eastern Bosque County was classified as Extreme/D3.

Severe/D2 drought conditions covered all of Hill County at the beginning of September. Conditions were downgraded to Extreme/D3 by September 10. On the 24th, conditions were uprgaded back to D2/moderate severity.
Extreme/D3 drought over all of Navarro County at the beginning of Sepember improved to Severe/D2 on the 24th, which contunued through the end of the month.

Mclennan County began September of 2013 with Extreme/D3 conditions in place. Conditions were upgraded to Severe/D2 by the 24th of the month following rainfall which occurred during the preceding week.

Extreme/D3 conditions in place over Falls County at the beginning of September of 2013 were upgraded to Severe/D2 by the 24th of the month, following beneficial rainfall received during the preceding week.

Limestone County began September of 2013 with Extreme/D3 conditions covering the majority of the county. Conditions were upgraded to Severe/D2 by the 24th of the month following beneficial rains received during the preceding week.

Severe/D2 drought conditions over Henderson County at the beginning of September 2013 were downgraded to Extreme/D3 by the 17th of the month. Conditions were upgraded back to Severe/D2 on September 24th following beneficial rainfall received during the preceding week.

Extreme/D3 drought conditions at the beginning of September 2013 were eventually upgraded to Severe/D2 by the 24th of the month following beneficial rainfall which was received over much of the area during the preceding week.

Extreme/D3 conditions in place over Robertson County at the beginning of September of 2013 were upgraded to Severe/D2 by the 24th of the month, following beneficial rainfall received during the preceding week.

Extreme/D3 conditions in place over Leon County at the beginning of September of 2013 were upgraded to Severe/D2 by the 24th of the month, following beneficial rainfall received during the preceding week.

Anderson County began September of 2013 split between Severe/D2 conditions across the north and Extreme/D3 conditions across the southern part of the county. The extreme conditions were expanded to cover all of the county on the 17th, only to be upgraded to Severe/D2 county-wide on the 24th due to beneficial rains received during the preceding week.

Heavy rains caused flooding around Waco. Several cars were stalled in high water. One of the most flooded areas was the I-35 overpass at University Parks Drive. The heavy rain also resulted in road damage at 4th Street and Jefferson Avenue, and part of the intersection had to be closed.
Lightning started a house fire in the 6000 block of Sterling Drive in Colleyville. Flames were coming from the garage when firefighters arrived.
Lightning started a house fire in the 4900 block of Waterford Drive in Colleyville. Flames were coming from the roof when firefighters arrived.

Three people were injured when their pickup truck rolled after losing control on a rain-slicked road. The accident occurred near the intersection of US 287 and Texas 114 West. All three passengers were transported to local hospitals.

Extreme/D3 drought conditions covered the northern two-thirds of Lamar County at the beginning of October, with Severe/D2 drought in place across the southern third. Beneficial rainfall of 5-6 inches occurred across the county during the month, which eliminated the D3 area. At the end of the month, Severe/D2 conditions covered the northern two-thirds of the county with Moderate/D1 over the southern third.
Severe/D2 drought in place during most of October improved to Moderate/D1 by the end of the month, due mainly to heavy rain received area-wide on October 26th.
Severe/D2 drought over the southeastern quarter of the county ended by Oct 22, due to beneficial rainfall received during the month.
Severe/D2 drought in place at the beginning of October was upgraded to Moderate/D1 by October 22, due to much-needed rainfall occurring throughout the month.

Severe/D2 drought conditions in place at the beginning of October ended by October 22, as the U.S. Drought monitor upgraded conditions to Moderate/D1. This was due to much-needed rainfall which occurred throughout the month.

Severe/D2 drought conditions over the eastern half of Young County at the beginning of October were expanded across the rest of the county by the 8th. These conditions remained in place through the end of the month.
Severe/D2 drought conditions were in place over all but the far northern portions of Jack County during October 2013.

Severe/D2 drought conditions covered Tarrant County for all of October 2013.
Hood County was split between Severe/D2 conditions across the southern half of the county and Moderate/D1 conditions across the northern half for all of October 2013.

Severe/D2 conditions over all of Somervell County were scaled back to Moderate/D1 across the southern half of the county by October 22. These conditions remained in place through the end of the month.

Heavy rainfall resulted in flash flooding in the Holland area. Six inches of water was over Highway 95 between Holland and Bartlett. Water rescues were performed along Sunshine Rd and Strasburger Rd, and the two roads were barricaded due to the high water. One man was also rescued on Donahoe Rd to the southeast of Holland. The area received nearly 8 of rain in less than 12 hours.
One to two feet of water was flowing over the intersection of FM 436 and Old TX 95 in Little River. Heavy thunderstorms produced nearly 8 of rain in just a few hours resulting in flash flooding.

Heavy thunderstorms produced flash flooding in southern Falls County. FM 1373 was underwater between FM 413 and HWY 6. High water was reported on HWY 6 where it crosses Little Brazos River. Water was also reported on FM 2413 and FM 46. Nearly 8-10 of rain fell over the area in just a few hours.
Highway 53 near Rosebud was under water.

Numerous roads were closed across the county due to very heavy rainfall resulting in flash flooding. 4-12 of rain fell across the county in just a few hours. Water entered one house on Highway 84 in Teague. 4 houses on the northeast side of Teague were evacuated as Turtle Creek quickly rose.

Numerous roads were closed due to flash flooding that resulted from heavy thunderstorms that produced 4-8 of rain across the county in less than 8 hours. Portions of Highway 79 in Palestine were closed. Part of Highway 79 between Palestine and Tucker were also closed. Numerous other roads in Palestine were impassable including Reagan, Azell, Bassett, North Sycamore Rd near Ezell and Green Street. CR 2201 at Salt Works Rd, and CR 2715 and 2301 were also closed. One home on CR 2301 was flooded with 6 of water when Lake Creek overflowed its banks. FM 312 in Frankston was washed out. FM 321 at HWY 287 in Tennessee Colony was impassable. FM 321 between Tennessee Colony and Neches was closed in some places. FM 320 was closed near Harmony. A woman was trapped in her vehicle on FM 645 in Tucker due to high water, and FM 645 north of Tucker was also partially closed. Also, parts of FM 315, US 79 from Westwood to FM 645, FM 645 to FM 320, CR 2054, FM 321 to CR 2706, CRs 2223, 2401, 2504, 2303, & 2311 were closed or damaged. In many locations, it took the water several days to recede or the roads were closed for at least a week due to damage to the roads and/or culverts.

Significant flooding was reported along Highway 164 and the road was impassable. Several other major roads across the southern half of the county were closed due to flash flooding. Rainfall totals of 5-11 of rain fell across the southern half of the county in just a few hours.

Several county roads across the northern part of the county were impassable due to flash flooding. Heavy thunderstorms produced 3-7 of rain across the northern half of the county resulting in flash flooding. FM 2269 at Elm Creek was impassable for a few days. FM 485 at Elm Creek was closed for several weeks due to damage caused by flooding from the swollen creek. At least 3 people were rescued out of Elm Creek near FM 485. In addition, parts of FM 487 and 437 near Davilla were flooded. Damage was reported on FM 437. CR 116 was also closed because the asphalt was washed away.
A 43 year old male was killed when a semi jackknifed on a wet road and hit the oncoming car the male was driving. The accident occurred near the intersection of TX 101 and FM 1786.
A 26 year old male was killed when his car lost control on a curve in a heavy downpour and slid into an oncoming tractor-trailor. The accident occurred on Highway 7 about 3 miles west of Chilton.
A 24 year old female was killed in a chain reaction accident on Ranger Hill in rainy conditions.

A 65 year old female was killed when her car lost control on a rain-slick bridge and fell onto the riverbank below. The accident occurred on the Trinity River bridge on East Loop 820. Investigators determined weather played a role in the accident.
Heavy rain and flash flooding led to the closure of Wedel Cemetery Road. The road was damaged by the flood waters.

Approximately half of the trees in Yettie Polk State Park were uprooted or heavily damaged by thunderstorm winds, and the park had to be closed. Crews from the public works department worked overnight to remove debris from roadways. Power lines were also knocked down in the park.

Steady rainfall fell over Graham for several hours with periods of heavy rainfall. This resulted in street flooding around the city. The water was up to the front bumper of cars at a few intersections.
Just over 1.25 of rain fell in Mexia in a 2-3 hour period. This resulted in some street flooding in the city, and a portion of Hwy 84 had to be closed for less than an hour.

Significant flooding was reported in Mexia after nearly 4 inches of rain fell in a short period. The 700 block of Palestine Street was impassable with water running into nearby homes and manholes blowing their covers. A new culvert at Bonham St and Hopkins Street was pushed out of the ground creating problems for drivers at that intersection.
Four roads in Coryell County were barricaded overnight due to heavy rainfall from thunderstorms.

A lightning strike damaged an underground cable near Lake Belton that caused the Gatesville Regional Water Intake Structure to lose power. As a result, all Gatesville ISD campuses and less than 100 homes were without water through Monday.

Heavy rainfall totaling 2-4 inches caused the Normangee ISD drain pipes to back up, flooding Normangee Middle School's multipurpose building. The library, counselor's office and the technology coordinator's office received the most damage. The front foyer area in the gym also had standing water and some of the floor boards in the gym were damaged. The carpet in the library and some of the low sheet rock had to be replaced.

Significant flooding continued across eastern Bell County after nearly 8 of rain fell over the area. The water took several hours to recede. Several roads remained closed and some roads were damaged by the flood waters.
Flooding continued across parts of Falls County after nearly 8-10 of rain fell over the area. Most of the rain fell over the southern half of the county. The water took several hours to recede.

Flooding continued across mainly the southern half of Limestone County after 4-11 of rain fell over the area. The water took several hours to recede. Several roads remained closed and some roads were damaged by the flood waters.

Flooding continued across Freestone County after 4-12 of rain fell over the area. The water took several hours to recede. Several roads remained closed and some roads were damaged by the flood waters.
Flooding continued across Anderson County after 4-8 of rain fell over the area. The water took several hours to recede. Several roads remained closed and some roads were damaged by the flood waters.

Flooding continued across northern Milam County after 3-7 of rain fell over the area. The water took several hours to recede. Several roads remained closed and some roads were damaged by the flood waters.

Palo Pinto Sheriff's Department reported 0.10 of sleet that was affecting travel across the county.
Decatur Fire Department reported 0.10 of sleet that was affecting travel across the county. Several minor accidents were noted.
Public report of reported 0.10 of sleet that was affecting travel in Jacksboro. Several minor accidents were noted.
Broadcast media reports patchy ice on Grayson County roads which were causing accidents.
Broadcast media reported 0.01 inch of freezing rain in Sherman.
Several reports came in through social media, reporting 0.05 inch of freezing rain in  southwest Tarrant County. Approximately 18,000 customers lost power for a brief period of time.
Paris Police Department reported 0.05 inch of freezing rain in Paris along highway 271.
Grayson County Sheriffs Department reported 0.15 inch of freezing rain in Denison and across the County. Accidents were reported along highways 377, 82, and 75.
Up to 3-4 of ice and sleet accumulated in Montague County. On average, 2 of ice and sleet was reported on the roads. The highest accumulations were in the southeastern half of the county.

Up to 4 of ice and sleet accumulated in Cooke County. On average, 2-3 of ice and sleet was reported. The COOP Observer in Muenster reported 1 of ice and sleet. Several traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets and hundreds of tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice. Interstate 35 through the county was closed for an extended period as many vehicles and semis became stranded on the icy highway.

Up to 4 of ice and sleet accumulated in Grayson County. On average, 3-4 of ice and sleet was reported and most of the reports were sleet accumulations. One media station in Denison reported 0.10 ice with 3 of sleet accumulations. Traffic became very difficult, including Highway 82 and Highway 289. Several traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets and hundreds of tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice. Due to the weight of the ice, the Lonestar Lanes Bowling Alley in Sherman collapsed on the 6th and the gymnasium roof at the Boys and Girls Club in Sherman also caved in. The roof of the Cooper-B building sagged inward due to the ice. In Denison, an awning collapsed at the Main Street Lumber, and several porch covers on house also collapsed. Tom Bean ISD reported minor damage to some of their buildings including roof leaks at the elementary school and a portion of the high school roof was sagging, plus a shed in the bus barn was crushed by the weight of the ice. Power lines were also knocked down by the ice resulting in many power outages. Sherman police reported 6 vehicle accidents with injuries and the Texoma Medical Center reported approximately 30 injuries due to slips and falls. The county preliminarily estimated $5 million in damage.

Up to 4 of ice and sleet accumulated in Fannin County. On average, 2.5-3 of ice and sleet was reported and most of the reports were sleet accumulations. In Bonham, law enforcement reported 2.5 of sleet accumulation. Numerous tree branches broke under the weight of the ice. In Bonham, the roof of JCS Whiskey River caved in and the awning at Bonham Barber Stylists collapsed. In Ector, part of the roof of the junior high school caved inward and two of the main beams in the high school gym were twisted under the weight of the ice.

Up to 2 of ice and sleet accumulated in Young County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet and the heaviest amounts fell across the southeastern half of the county. Amateur radio reported 2 of ice and sleet accumulations in Loving and throughout the county.
Up to 3 of ice and sleet accumulated in Jack County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet and the heaviest amounts fell across the southeastern two-thirds of the county.

Up to 3 of ice and sleet accumulated in Wise County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet. Three inches of sleet was reported near Decatur. US 380 between Decatur and Bridgeport was shut down on the 7th. Traffic was very slow or stopped on parts of Highway 287 due to ice, and numerous accidents had been reported.

Up to 3-4 of ice and sleet accumulated in Denton County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet and the heaviest amounts were across the northern parts of the county. A trained spotter reported 2.5 of sleet with 0.3 of freezing rain to the NW of Sanger.  The public reported 3.5 of sleet in Little Elm. Up to 4 of ice and sleet was reported on the streets in Lewisville. Numerous traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets and hundreds of tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice. Interstate 35 between Denton and Oklahoma was closed at one point due to the icy conditions and motorists were stranded in their vehicles along I-35E. On I-35E on the bridge over Lake Lewisville, a 21-year old female died during the early morning hours on the 7th when she lost control on the icy bridge and her car plunged over the guardrail into the lake below.  Also at Lake Lewisville, a portion of the Pier 121 Marina collapsed on the 6th, damaging at roughly 50 boats. The popular TopGolf in The Colony sustained damage to several poles that hold the net up and remained closed for several days. Several power lines across the county also snapped due to the weight of the ice. As temperatures began to warm by the 8th and 9th, falling ice continued to be a hazard for several days and several more roof collapses were reported as the thaw continued. One large business sign in Sanger crashed into a parking lot on the 9th. In Lewisville, 2 people were injured when a carport collapsed on the 11th from the weight of the ice. The clean-up from the ice storm took several weeks.

Up to 3-4 of ice and sleet accumulated in Collin County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet and the heaviest amounts were across the northern parts of the county. The COOP Observer in Frisco reported 3.5-4 of ice and sleet. The public reported 3.25 of sleet in McKinney. Numerous traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets and hundreds of tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice. In McKinney, one tree fell through a house in the downtown area. Several power lines also snapped due to the weight of the ice. In Plano, carports tumbled under the weight of the ice, damaging some cars underneath. A few days later, as the ice finally started to melt on the 8th and 9th, ice tumbled off of multi-story apartment buildings in Plano and damaged several cars that were parked below. The clean-up from the ice storm took several weeks.

Up to 4 of ice and sleet accumulated in Palo Pinto County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet. Amateur radio reported 3 of sleet in Palo Pinto and 3-4 of sleet in Mineral Wells. The COOP Observer in Strawn reported 2 of ice and sleet. The metal roof/awning of a strip center in Mineral Wells collapsed under the weight of the ice.

Up to 4 of ice and sleet accumulated in Parker County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet and the heaviest amounts fell in the northwestern and southeastern portions of the county. Several traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets and hundreds of tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice. Interstate 20 was impassable at times and many motorists were stranded on the highway. TX 180 between Weatherford and Mineral Wells was also closed. Several power lines also snapped due to the weight of the ice. A male died when his ATV lost control and flipped on an icy road.

An average of 2-3 of ice and sleet accumulated in Tarrant County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet and the heaviest amounts fell in the northwestern portions of the county. Up to 0.50 of freezing rain/ice occurred. 2.5 of sleet was reported in Hurst, 2 of ice and sleet was reported in Keller, 2 of sleet was reported in Haslet, 2 was reported in North Richland Hills, and 2.25 of sleet was reported in the Benbrook area. 2 of sleet and ice was reported at the NWS Office in north Fort Worth. The I-20/I-30 split in west Fort Worth was especially treacherous to travel through due to cobblestone ice and so was I-35W north of North Tarrant Parkway. Numerous traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets. Fort Worth police reported nearly 40 major accidents and several smaller ones. A 7-car accident occurred on I-20 at Forest Hill around 9 pm on the 5th, and a 15-car wreck occurred on TX 121 in Grapevine. Only 3 people sustained minor injures in both of those accidents, but a male died in a separate accident on I-20 in Arlington. Hundreds of ice related falls were reported by area hospitals. Several power lines also snapped due to the weight of the ice and more than 200,000 customers were without power on the 6th. Several thousand people were stranded at DFW Airport throughout the weekend. The clean-up from the ice storm took several weeks. Hundreds of tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice. An elderly man died from hypothermia in Fort Worth.

An average of 1-3 of ice and sleet accumulated in Dallas County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet and the heaviest amounts fell in the northwestern portions of the county. 2.5 of sleet was reported on Coppell, and 0.30 of freezing rain was reported in Mesquite. Irving reported 2.75 of ice and sleet. Half an inch of freezing rain/ice was reported in Dallas. Hundreds of traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets and hundreds of tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice. Several power lines also snapped due to the weight of the ice. The clean-up from the ice storm took several weeks. A male died after his car lost control on icy roads at Preston and Royal in Dallas, an elderly woman died after falling on some ice in her yard, and another woman died from exposure to the cold.

Up to 1 of ice and sleet accumulated in Eastland County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet. Amateur radio reported 1 of ice and sleet in Cisco. Many people were stranded on Ranger Hill and forced to seek nearby shelter or were stranded in their cars for several hours.

Up to 3.5 of ice and sleet accumulated in Erath County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet and the heaviest amounts were located across the northern portions of the county. The COOP Observer in Chalk Mountain reported 3.5 of sleet. Amateur radio reported 1 of ice and sleet in Stephenville, and a retired NWS Employee reported 1.75 of ice and sleet in Bluff Dale. Several traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets and many tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice.

Up to 2 of ice and sleet accumulated in Hood County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet. A trained spotter reported 2 of ice and sleet in Oak Trail Shores. More than 1 of ice and sleet was reported in Granbury by the public. Lake Granbury Medial Center reported 75 patients from fall-related injuries due to the ice. Of that 75, 39 had fractures. Several traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets and numerous tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice. Some power lines also snapped due to the weight of the ice.
Up to 2-3 of ice and sleet accumulated in Comanche County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet. Amateur radio reported 2 of sleet at Lake Proctor with more ice underneath the sleet.
Up to 2 of ice and sleet accumulated in Hamilton County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet. Amateur radio reported 2 of ice and sleet throughout the county.

Up to 1 of ice and sleet accumulated in Hunt County. Several traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets and numerous tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice. Some of the falling branches damaged buildings and cars. Some power lines also snapped due to the weight of the ice. A 3-vehicle accident on the Two-Mile Bridge over Lake Tawakoni resulted in 3 hospital transports and closed the bridge for some time.

A 39-year old female died in a car accident when another vehicle lost control on an ice patch and struck the car she was traveling in. Five other passengers involved in the accident were seriously injured. The accident occurred on Farm Road 1885 near Farm Road 920 north of Weatherford. Light freezing rain was occurring around the time of the accident.
A lightning strike started a fire at a gas well on CR 308 just north of Highway 67 between Glen Rose and Cleburne.

Weather played a role in the death of a person who crashed their truck in the 4500 block of Davis Street near Cockrell Hill Rd. The roads were slick due to rain at the time of the accident. No other information about the deceased could be found.
A vehicle lost control on I-35E due to slick roads from rain and crashed through a guardrail. The driver of the vehicle was killed and the passenger was injured.

A 53-year old male died on I-35 in Temple due to icy conditions on a bridge near mile marker 303A. His car had struck the guardrail, and when he got out to check the damage, another vehicle lost control on the icy bridge and struck the male killing him. The local police reported icy roadways and bridges throughout the city.

Up  to 1 of freezing rain fell across the county causing significant damage to trees, tree branches, utility poles and lines due to the heavy collection of ice. The COOP Observer in Paris reported 0.75 of ice. Hundreds of trees, tree branches, and power lines were knocked down and travel was difficult across the county. The EOC in Paris lost power and all communications due to a power outage. All emergency radio communications were also knocked out by the power outage. Falling tree branches and ice damaged cars and roofs. In addition, an estimated $10.5 million in damage to roads and bridges was caused by the ice storm.

A 34-year-old truck driver died on US Highway 75 in Sherman. He lost control of his semi on an icy patch and crashed into the concrete pillar of the Loy Lake Road overpass. The temperature at the time of the accident was around 23 degrees.

According to the sheriff's office, up to 2 of ice and sleet accumulated in Mills County. Roads became covered in ice and several accidents due to vehicles sliding off the roadways were reported. The local police reported Highway 84 west of Evant was especially treacherous. Many tree branches and trees were broken or damaged from the weight of the ice.
Accumulations of ice and sleet resulted in significant tree damage across Rockwall County. The ice also brought down power lines, resulting in a few hundred power outages, and some carports toppled.

Icy road conditions resulted in numerous accidents or vehicles off the roadway along Interstate 35 from Hillsboro to the north. The icing was the result of freezing rain that left a thin layer of ice in the county.

Up to 3 of ice and sleet accumulated in Somervell County. Most of the accumulations were due to sleet. A few traffic accidents occurred on the icy streets and numerous tree branches broke due to the weight of the ice. Some power lines also snapped due to the weight of the ice. A few injures due to slips and falls on the ice were reported.

Up to 2 of ice and sleet accumulated in Johnson County. The COOP Observer in Burleson reported 1.75-2 of sleet and ice. The COOP Observer in Cleburne reported 1 of sleet and ice. Many tree branches were broken and power lines were knocked down due to the weight of the ice. The Burleson police reported 65 minor vehicle accidents and 3 major accidents.

Accumulations of sleet and ice resulted in tree and power line damage in Ellis County. The COOP Observer in Maypearl reported 1.25 of ice and sleet. On December 8th, a tree limb fell on power lines in the 500 block of North Rogers Street in Waxahachie, which sent a charge into a nearby home that started a fire in the kitchen.

Up to 2 of freezing rain and sleet fell across the county causing significant damage to trees, tree branches, utility poles and lines due to the heavy collection of ice. A trained spotter reported 0.50 of freezing rain in Cumby. The newspaper in Sulphur Springs reported over 1.75 of sleet. Hundreds of trees, tree branches, and power lines were knocked down. Falling tree branches and ice damaged cars and roofs. Bridges, overpasses, and elevated surfaces became icy but other roads were largely not impacted by the ice. One railroad employee was injured when a tree fell on him as he was working to remove tree debris from the railroad tracks.

A National Weather Service storm survey crew determined a tornado caused EF0 damage to a subdivision in Princeton. The tornado produced damage to a number of homes, along with several fences which were blown down.

This tornado caused damage to several homes and businesses, including the Birthright Volunteer Fire Department building. A total of 76 houses or businesses were damaged in this tornado.

After beginning April 2014 in Severe/D2 drought, much of Dallas County improved to Moderate/D1 after a week of receiving nice rainfall. Conditions quickly deteriorated back to Severe/D2 by the middle of April, with much of the county falling into Extreme/D3 by the end of the month.

Comanche County began the month of May split between Severe/D2 drought conditions over the western third of the county and Extreme/D3 conditions over the eastern two-thirds. Bosque County fell under Extreme/D3 category during the first week of May. Conditions remained as such through the end of the month.

Hill County began May split between Extreme/D3 conditions over the northwestern half of the county and Severe/D2 over the southeastern half. Significant flash flooding occurred in and around Granbury when 5-8 of rain fell over the area. Up to 3 feet of water was reported over some roads in Granbury. Many water rescues were reported; especially in areas northeast of Granbury. The Quail Run and Sunchase Meadows subdivisions (northeast of Granbury in unincorporated Hood County) were the hardest hit. The Quail Run area is near Rucker's Creek which overflowed sending several feet of water into the subdivision. One home was reported to have shifted off its foundation. Three mobile homes were destroyed and two had minor damage. In the Sunchase Meadows subdivision, 18 people had to be rescued from their homes. Four homes were destroyed and three had major damage in Sunchase Meadows. The DeCordova area was also impacted by flash flooding with road problems.
SH 174 north of Morgan was closed due to high water over the road. At least a few other smaller roads in the area were also covered in water. An estimated 5+ inches of rain fell over the area.

Social media reports showed significant flooding near Hulen and Bryce Streets in Fort Worth. Some roads in downtown Fort Worth were impassable and blocked by the fire department. In the West 7th district, the water was reported to be several feet deep. Many vehicles were flooded or trapped in flood waters. More than 40 high water rescues were conducted in Fort Worth.
Water was flowing over the Interstate 45 access road in Palmer.

Thunderstorm winds blew down small trees and several tree limbs in Jermyn.
Several inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing high water and flooding on Bonds Ranch Road to the west of Highway 287. Several vehicles were trapped in the high water.
Byron Nelson Blvd at Oak Street and under Highway 377 in Roanoke was closed due to high water. James Street between Crosby St. and Walnut St. was also closed.

Severe/D2 drought conditions affected only the northwestern corner of Ellis County during June 2014. The rest of the county remained under D1/Moderate drought status.

Flat Creek near the intersection of Hewitt Drive and Mars Drive, behind Midway High School, flooded over the roadway. The creek also overflowed near the intersection of Panther Way and Panther Run. It was reported that the creek overflowed by at least half a mile, was up to 2 feet over at least one road, and the water was swiftly flowing over the road; like a river. Several cars were stuck in the water. An 18-year-old male died when his car was swept off the road in the dark and swept down the creek. The car was found about 2 miles down the creek, and his body was found the next day near the creek. Part of the asphalt of Panther Way was destroyed in chunks and had to be replaced.

Castleman Creek in Hewitt overflowed its banks due to heavy rainfall and flooded Hewitt Park. It was reported that the water was as high as the 4-foot-tall disc golf baskets in some areas. The flood waters flooded the park restrooms. A 40-foot-long section of Earle Street near the creek had to be replaced after the flood waters ripped up the road and moved it about 100 feet.
Waco police department was closing I-35 South at New Road due to flooding.
Waco police department was closing I-35 North near Robinson due to flooding.
Interstate 35 south of Moonlight Drive in the Lorena area was closed due to high water. Some cars were partially submerged on the interstate.
A grass fire in a hay field near Faught heavily damaged a tractor and other hay baling equipment.
For the second day in a row, a 50-acre grass fire in a hay field near Faught burned a hay crop and heavily damaged hay baling equipment.

Severe/D2 drought conditions covered Lampasas County for all of June, 2014.

Residual flooding across the northwest parts of Tarrant County continued for several hours after the heavy rain ended. Some of the most significant flooding was along Highway 287 in the Saginaw and Haslet areas. Roads remained closed.

Residual flooding across the southwest parts of Denton County continued for several hours after the heavy rain ended. Some of the most significant flooding was in the Roanoke and Trophy Club areas. Roads remained closed.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed a tractor shed and a barn along FM 2874 near the intersection with FM 512. Several trees were also knocked over in and near Commerce.
Several homes in the Western Lakes Estates were flooded after over 5-6 of rain fell in the area. Several feet of water was reported over the roadway that connects the two lakes in the neighborhood.

Several homes in Horseshoe Bend were flooded after over 6 of rain fell in the area. The road to the boat ramp at Horseshoe Bend was washed out. Silverado Drive near Highway 51 was also shut down due to 3-4 feet of water over the roadway.
Lightning is believed to have been the cause of a large house fire in the 3900 block of West 6th St.

A few roads in Bellmead were under water due to heavy rainfall over a 1-2 hour period.

The roof of the Wine Haus near the intersection of Park Place Ave and 8th Avenue in Fort Worth partially collapsed during a period of heavy rainfall.
Lightning struck a tank battery igniting it on fire off Turpin Road, north of Graford.

Culverts at the Bear Creek crossing in White Bluff Resort near Huron collapsed due to heavy rainfall near 4 inches.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed a house that was under construction in Frisco. Only the frame of the house was built at the time.
Strong thunderstorm winds damaged the 18-foot tall, 5,900-pound statue on top of the McLennan County Courthouse. The statue of Themis lost her left arm. The arm was made of lightweight metal.

Several hours of moderate to heavy rainfall caused a few flooding problems in Crawford. Highway 185 near 4th Street had to be closed for much of the day, and the picnic area at Tonkawa Park near the creek was under water. Part of 4th Street near the community center also had to be closed for a few hours.

Heavy rainfall resulted in the flooding of several streets and areas in Corsicana. The most significant flooding was around Community Park which was under close to a foot of water. Nearby Oaklawn Drive was affected by an overflowing creek and had to be closed. Flooding was also reported on Northwood Blvd and on North Business 45 just north of East 1st Avenue.
Wind damage was reported near Country Club Road and Stacy Road in Fairview. An 8 diameter tree was also blown over.
A 65 mph wind gust was measured in Seagoville. Large tree limbs were damaged.
Eight inches of water was reported over Highway 287 about halfway between Decatur and Alvord.

Very heavy rainfall resulted in significant flash flooding across the southern portions of Cooke County. Up to 10 inches of rain fell in the area. The town of Valley View was significantly affected by the flooding. Interstate 35 was shut down from the Denton County line north to mile marker 491. The water was 5-6 feet deep on the frontage road in some locations. One gas station along I-35 in Valley View had standing water in the convenience store. The interstate reopened between 8-9 am CDT. Numerous cars, trucks, and semis were stranded in the area; including along Interstate 35. The emergency manager estimated 20-30 vehicles were pulled from high water. Numerous high water rescues were conducted.

Very heavy rainfall resulted in significant flash flooding across the northern half of Denton County. Up to 11 inches of rain fell in the area. A rain gage near the Denton/Cooke County line reported 10.78 of total rain. The town of Sanger was significantly affected by the flooding. Interstate 35 was shut down from Sanger north to the Cooke County line. Several other roads around Sanger were closed due to high water. Numerous cars, trucks, and semis were stranded in the area; including along Interstate 35. Numerous high water rescues were conducted.
In Krum, 5 people had to be rescued from their homes as high water prevented them from leaving.
High water was reported on FM 3264 along the Wise/Montague county line.
Trees were blown down in several locations across Lamar County.
Ten large trees and four utility poles were knocked down in Palestine.
Several tin roof structures and outbuildings were damaged by thunderstorms winds between Myra and Hood. Several trees were also damaged in the same area.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a building and several trees on the northeast side of Denton.
Some intersections in Gainesville have 2+ feet of water over them and are being closed. An estimated 2-3 inches of rain fell in just a few hours in the area.

One foot of water was reported over the Interstate 35 access road in Sanger, south of FM 455. Interstate 35 in and just north of Sanger also had to be closed two times due to high water. Up to 4 of rain was reported in Sanger in just a few hours.

The east side of Quail Run Circle was washed out by heavy rainfall. 2-4 inches of rain fell in the area in just a few hours.

Significant flooding was reported in Gunter and flood waters reached the edges of a few homes and businesses in the city. Parts of Highway 289 were closed due to high water.  Several residents were trapped in their homes until the waters receded. 3-5 of rain fell in the area in just a few hours.
Flooding along Highway 5 near Rosamond Pkwy in Anna closed the road.

Several roads across the northeastern half of Denton County were flooded by high waters due to 3-6 of rain that fell in that area in just a few hours. Denton County Road and Bridge East reported Mustang Trail in Sanger, Coffey Road in Aubrey, Shearer Road in Pilot Point and the county roads of North Legacy, Fairfield, and Mobberly near Celina and Prosper remained closed until crews could check on them later that morning.

A 27 year-old woman and her 13 month old daughter died of hypothermia with paradoxical undressing according to local news outlets. This occurs when the victim begins to feel hot in the cold weather and undresses unknowingly in an attempt to stay cool. The bodies were located about 500 yards from their wrecked sedan and the clothing was found nearby. Fort Worth Meacham airport reported a low temperature of 32 and a high of 40 that day.

A National Weather Service damage survey crew found evidence of EF-1 and EF-0 damage across a three mile swath in southeastern Wise County. This multiple vortex tornado occurred over mainly open land, but destroyed two mobile homes, and damaging twelve others. Several power poles and power lines were damaged in the New Fairview area, between the city of Rhome and Decatur.

A National Weather Service damage survey crew found evidence of EF-1 damage, especially near the Bolivar community in western Denton County, Texas.  This tornado formed from the same parent supercell which produced a tornado in Wise County. The tornado began in the far southwestern portion of Denton County, producing damage to open farm and ranch land. Once the storm moved into the Bolivar community, damage to several roofs on homes were noted, as well as substantial damage to barns. A metal storage tank was lifted and thrown into the base of a high tension power line, causing the steel beams to collapse.

A NWS storm survey team found EF-3 damage in the city of Van. This tornado began near highway 64, near Edom before moving in a northerly direction. The storm crossed Interstate 20 on the southeast side of Van, before carving a destructive path over the eastern side of the city. The greatest damage was done in a housing development to the north of the public school administration building, where over 50 homes were damaged or destroyed. Two fatalities occurred with this tornado, as a married couple was apparently asleep in their mobile home when the tornado hit.

The local emergency manager reported 40-60 homes sustained some type of damage in these areas. The damage included trees uprooted, tree limbs down, carports damaged, portions of roofs ripped off, and siding removed from homes. At least one mobile home was blown off its foundation and onto a few vehicles parked next to the home.

Penny sized hail in far NW Somervell County.
